pages.title: AGENTS
pages.content: When running shell commands, use RTK for noisy commands whenever possible. Prefer: rtk git status rtk git diff rtk rg rtk grep rtk pytest rtk npm test Only run the raw command if RTK fails or if exact raw output is required. Codex App-Server Runtime Hermes Agent's Codex App-Server Runtime is enabled so Codex provides much of the actual execution machinery for OpenAI/Codex turns. Use Hermes Agent's Codex App-Server Runtime to hand off programming and coding tasks when possible. The archived completed to-do items are stored at PWA/to-do-archive.md in this Obsidian vault.

pages.title: Feycaster
pages.content: Class Name: Feycaster Requirements Int 9, Cha 9 Prime requisite INT, CHA Hit Dice 1d4 Armour None Weapons Dagger, Staff Languages Alignment, Common, Sylvan (Once the Feycaster has encountered a Fey creature) Class Features Fey Spellblast: A Feycaster can cast a spellblast to strike a foe within 50'(+10' per level) for 1d[Effective Character Level] force damage. This action is subject to the same requirements as arcane spellcasting: ability to speak, and freedom to move, but it has no material components. Fey Magic: A Feycaster learns one Illusionist spell each level. This spell may be of a maximum level of what an Illusionist of her class level -1 could cast. A Feycaster cannot prepare these spells and has no spell slots to use. However, they may reduce their Effective Character Level for Fey Spellblast in order to generate the power to cast them. A spell reduces the Feycaster's Spellbast ECL by 1 per level of the spell. This penalty remains for on hour the first time a given spell is used. If that spell is used a second time, the penalty remains until the character has gotten a full night's rest. Spellblast ECL cannot be reduced below 1 with this ability. Fey Bond: A Feycaster must have the lineage or patronage of a powerful fey to use any of her class abilities. The first time a Feycaster encounters a fey creature, they receive Sylvan as a permanent bonus language. At the Game Master's discretion, Feycaster with the lineage or patronage of a fey with magical abilities may choose an appropriately-themed spell from another class in place of an Illusionist spell of the same level. For example, a Feycaster sponsored by a Dryad may be permitted to take Speak with Plants as a fourth level spell even though it appears on the Cleric and Druid lists and not the Illusionist spell list. pages.title: Loremaster Bard
pages.content: Return to variant classes index or read further below... --- an (OSE Variant) Prime Requisite Intelligence and Charisma Hit Dice 1d6 per level Armor & Weapons Allowed Armor Leather armor Chainmail Shields Allowed Weapons Any one-handed weapon Bows Spears Staves Swords --- Attack Progression As Cleric. Saving Throws As Cleric. XP Progression Similar to OSE Bard or slightly slower. Level XP --- --- 1 0 2 2,500 3 5,000 4 10,000 5 20,000 6 40,000 7 80,000 8 160,000 9 320,000 --- Class Abilities Lore The Loremaster may attempt to identify: ancient ruins, heraldry, relics, magical inscriptions, forgotten cultures, monsters, or historical events. Chance of Success Base chance: 2-in-6 at level 1 Improves by +1 every 3 levels: 3-in-6 at level 4 4-in-6 at level 7 The referee may modify difficulty based on obscurity. --- Saga of Heroes By reciting epic histories and sacred lays, the Loremaster can inspire allies. Once per day: allies within earshot gain: +1 morale +1 saving throws vs fear Effect lasts: one encounter or one exploration turn. At level 7: bonus becomes +2 vs fear. --- Tongues & Scripts The Loremaster begins play literate and knows: Common one ancient language one additional language of choice At levels 4 and 8: gains another language. May attempt to decipher unknown writing: 2-in-6 chance increases with level. --- Memory of Ages At level 3, the Loremaster may recall hidden truths about places or creatures after 1 turn of contemplation. Examples: legendary weaknesses, lost passages, forgotten names, burial customs, religious taboos, ancient betrayals. Usable: once per day initially twice/day at level 7. --- Bardic Spellcasting Beginning at level 2, the Loremaster casts spells as a limited arcane caster. Spell list focuses on: divination, protection, charm, memory, and warding. Uses Magic-User spells, but cannot cast: explosive battlefield magic, overtly destructive spells, or reality-warping sorcery. Appropriate spells: Read Languages Detect Magic Light Protection from Evil Sleep ESP Clairvoyance Legend Lore (high level) --- Optional Ability: Song of Rest At level 5: after one uninterrupted night of rest and storytelling: allies recover +1 hp. Cannot benefit more than once per day. --- Stronghold At level 9, the Loremaster may establish: a Hall of Records, monastery, skaldic court, archive fortress, or wandering college. Students, scribes, and seekers gather there. --- Typical Equipment weathered manuscripts rune-staff traveling cloak horn lantern ancient maps bone flute or harp reliquary of saintly writings satchel of ink and parchment --- Northern Reaches Flavor A Loremaster Bard in your setting could be: a chronicler of St. Ygg, a keeper of pre-Futurus oral histories, a survivor of lost Helvecian monasteries, a skald of Brine, or a wandering scholar investigating the Barrowmoor. Such characters are often welcomed in civilized halls because they preserve: ancestry, treaties, songs, and the names of the dead. But they are also feared, because loremasters remember truths others would rather bury. --- Return to variant classes index

pages.title: GetMarkdownFromResponse
pages.content: private static string GetMarkdownFromResponse(HttpResponseMessage response, string originalUrl) { using (response) { response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode(); var content = response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync().GetAwaiter().GetResult(); if (!IsHtmlResponse(response, content)) { return content; } var markdownUrl = GetObsidianPublishMarkdownUrl(content); if (markdownUrl is null) { return $"{UnresolvedUrlMessage}: {originalUrl}"; } using var markdownRequest = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, markdownUrl); markdownRequest.Headers.Accept.Add(new MediaTypeWithQualityHeaderValue("text/markdown")); markdownRequest.Headers.Accept.Add(new MediaTypeWithQualityHeaderValue("text/plain")); using var markdownResponse = HttpClient.Send(markdownRequest); markdownResponse.EnsureSuccessStatusCode(); return markdownResponse.Content.ReadAsStringAsync().GetAwaiter().GetResult(); } } private static bool IsHtmlResponse(HttpResponseMessage response, string content) { var mediaType = response.Content.Headers.ContentType?.MediaType; return string.Equals(mediaType, "text/html", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) content.TrimStart().StartsWith(" return match.Success && Uri.TryCreate(match.Groups["url"].Value, UriKind.Absolute, out var uri) ? uri : null; } In short: it detects HTML, finds Obsidian Publishs embedded window.preloadPage markdown URL, fetches that .md file, and returns the markdown content.

pages.title: GetMarkdownFromURL
pages.content: namespace DungeonMaster { internal static class MarkdownUtility { private static readonly HttpClient HttpClient = CreateHttpClient(); public static string GetMarkdownFromURL(string url) { if (!Uri.TryCreate(url, UriKind.Absolute, out var uri) (uri.Scheme != Uri.UriSchemeHttp && uri.Scheme != Uri.UriSchemeHttps)) { throw new ArgumentException("The URL must be an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL.", nameof(url)); } using var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, uri); request.Headers.Accept.Add(new MediaTypeWithQualityHeaderValue("text/markdown")); request.Headers.Accept.Add(new MediaTypeWithQualityHeaderValue("text/plain")); request.Headers.Accept.Add(new MediaTypeWithQualityHeaderValue(" / ", 0.1)); using var response = HttpClient.Send(request); response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode(); return response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync().GetAwaiter().GetResult(); } private static HttpClient CreateHttpClient() { var httpClient = new HttpClient { Timeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30) }; httpClient.DefaultRequestHeaders.UserAgent.ParseAdd("DungeonMaster/1.0"); return httpClient; } } } GetMarkdownFromURL( ) does the outer workflow to pull markdown data from a URL on my published vault: Validate the URL format. Send the initial HTTP request. Hand the HTTP response to GetMarkdownFromResponse( ).

pages.title: Internet Connection Check
pages.content: The internet check runs from the Shown event in Form1.cs (line 29): private static readonly Uri[] InternetConnectionCheckUris = [ new(" new(" new(" new(" ]; private static readonly HttpClient InternetConnectionHttpClient = new() { Timeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5) }; It is triggered when the form first appears: Shown += async ( , ) => await UpdateInternetConnectionStatusAsync(); The status update logic is here: private async Task UpdateInternetConnectionStatusAsync() { statusLabel.Text = string.Empty; using var timeoutCancellationTokenSource = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5)); var connectionCheckTask = HasInternetConnectionAsync(timeoutCancellationTokenSource.Token); var testingStatusDelayTask = Task.Delay(750); var testingStatusShown = false; if (await Task.WhenAny(connectionCheckTask, testingStatusDelayTask) != connectionCheckTask) { statusLabel.Text = TestingInternetConnectionStatusText; testingStatusShown = true; } var statusText = await connectionCheckTask ? ConnectedToInternetStatusText : NoInternetConnectionStatusText; statusLabel.Text = testingStatusShown ? $"{TestingInternetConnectionStatusText} {statusText}" : statusText; } And the actual viability test is this: it tries several public endpoints in parallel and returns true as soon as any one succeeds: Each endpoint check is just an HTTP GET that succeeds only on a successful status code: private static async Task CanReachInternetEndpointAsync(Uri uri, CancellationToken cancellationToken) { try { using var response = await InternetConnectionHttpClient.GetAsync( uri, HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead, cancellationToken); return response.IsSuccessStatusCode; } catch (HttpRequestException) { return false; } catch (OperationCanceledException) { return false; } }

pages.title: Methods Listing for Player Assistant
pages.content: Main - starts the single-instance WinForms application. Form1 - initializes the main form, assets, timers, and startup UI. OnFormClosed - disposes timers, images, and UI resources on close. OnShown - sizes the window, loads cached hero images, and starts listing updates. OnPaint - draws welcome and hero intro overlay text. ExitToolStripMenuItem Click - closes the application from the File > Exit menu. UpdatePlayerCharacterListingAsync - fetches player-character data and refreshes hero image state. EnsurePlayerCharacterDirectories - creates PCs, active, and inactive directories. InitializeCachedActiveHeroImages - loads existing active hero images from disk. IsMarkdownFetchFailure - detects markdown fetch error sentinel messages. ShouldDownloadActiveHeroImages - decides whether cached hero images are stale. GetCachedActiveHeroImagePaths - returns cached image files from the active directory. UpdateActiveHeroImageStatus - updates the status bar with image count and total size. StartHeroImageShowcase - begins the randomized hero image slideshow. StartHeroImageShowcaseIfReady - starts the slideshow only when startup conditions allow it. StartHeroImageShowcaseAfterDelayAsync - waits before starting the intro/showcase sequence. StartHeroImageShowcaseWithIntroAsync - displays intro text before starting hero images. StopHeroImageShowcase - stops slideshow timers and clears current images. ShowNextHeroImage - loads and displays the next hero image. StartPlayerCharacterListingUpdateAsync - gates and starts the listing refresh workflow. UpdateHeroImageShowcase - advances fade-in, display, fade-out, and next-image timing. GetCenteredHeroImageBounds - calculates centered scaled bounds for a hero image. GetHeroImageDisplayBounds - determines the usable image display area. InitializeHeroImagePictureBox - creates the picture box used for hero images. UpdateHeroImagePictureBox - renders the current image frame with opacity. ClearHeroImagePictureBox - hides and disposes the current picture-box image. LoadImageCopy - loads an image from disk, using SkiaSharp as fallback. LoadImageWithSkiaSharp - decodes image formats through SkiaSharp into a bitmap. GetProgress - converts elapsed time into a clamped 0..1 progress value. FormatByteSize - formats byte counts as bytes, KB, MB, or GB. ShowPlayerCharacterResolvedImagePathsOnce - shows resolved image paths once per install/run marker. ShowPlayerCharacterImageFileNames - shows discovered image file names. ShowPlayerCharacterHtmlImageUrisOnce - shows scraped HTML image URIs once. ShowPlayerCharacterImageUrisOnce - shows markdown image URIs once. FillCurrentScreenWorkingArea - resizes the form to the current screen working area. DrawOutlinedText - draws centered outlined text with a shadow. LoadBackgroundImage - loads the embedded marble background. LoadDragonBackgroundImage - loads the embedded dragon background. LoadApplicationIcon - loads the embedded application icon. OpenEmbeddedAsset - opens an embedded resource stream by asset name. CreateCenteredTextPath - creates a centered graphics path for text. Dispose - designer-generated cleanup for form components. InitializeComponent - designer-generated UI construction for menu/status controls. HtmlUtility.GetHtmlFromUrlAsync(string) - validates a URL string and fetches HTML. HtmlUtility.GetHtmlFromUrlAsync(Uri) - sends an HTTP request and returns HTML content. HtmlUtility.GetImageUrisFromHtml(string, Uri?) - extracts image src URIs from HTML. HtmlUtility.GetImageUrisFromHtml(string, string) - validates a base URL and extracts image URIs. HtmlUtility.AddImageUri - normalizes and adds absolute or resolved image URIs. HtmlUtility.CreateHttpClient - creates the HTML HTTP client. ImageDownloadUtility.DownloadImageAsync(string) - validates an image URL string and downloads it. ImageDownloadUtility.DownloadImageAsync(Uri) - downloads and validates image content. ImageDownloadUtility.CreateHttpClient - creates the image download HTTP client. MarkdownUtility.GetMarkdownFromURL - fetches markdown or resolves Obsidian Publish markdown. MarkdownUtility.GetImageUrisFromMarkdown - extracts image URIs from markdown. MarkdownUtility.GetImageFileNamesFromMarkdown - extracts image file names from markdown. MarkdownUtility.GetMarkdownFromResponse - handles direct markdown or HTML-to-markdown resolution. MarkdownUtility.IsHtmlResponse - detects whether an HTTP response is HTML. MarkdownUtility.GetObsidianPublishMarkdownUrl - finds the Obsidian markdown preload URL. MarkdownUtility.GetReferenceDefinitions - parses markdown reference-link definitions. MarkdownUtility.AddImageUri - normalizes and stores markdown image URIs. MarkdownUtility.AddImageFileName - extracts and stores valid image file names. MarkdownUtility.GetImageFileName - derives an image file name from a path or URL. MarkdownUtility.TrimMarkdownUrl - removes surrounding markdown angle brackets. MarkdownUtility.CreateHttpClient - creates the markdown HTTP client. ObsidianPublishUtility.GetAttachmentImagePathsByFileNameAsync - maps attachment file names to Obsidian access URLs. ObsidianPublishUtility.GetAccessUrlAsync - builds an access URL for a vault path. ObsidianPublishUtility.GetSiteInfoAsync - extracts Obsidian site UID and host. ObsidianPublishUtility.GetPublishedCacheAsync - downloads the Obsidian Publish cache index. ObsidianPublishUtility.GetAssetPathsByFileName - maps cached asset file names to vault paths. ObsidianPublishUtility.IsIndexMarkdownPath - detects attachment index markdown paths. ObsidianPublishUtility.GetImageFileNameFromAttachmentIndexPath - recovers original image names from index files. ObsidianPublishUtility.BuildAccessUrl - constructs an Obsidian asset access URL. ObsidianPublishUtility.EscapePath - URL-escapes vault path segments. ObsidianPublishUtility.CreateHttpClient - creates the Obsidian HTTP client. PlayerCharacterAssetUtility.DownloadActiveHeroImagesAsync - downloads active hero token images. PlayerCharacterAssetUtility.GetHeroRows - parses hero rows from the listing table. PlayerCharacterAssetUtility.ThrowIfMarkdownFetchFailed - throws on markdown fetch failure markers. PlayerCharacterAssetUtility.SplitMarkdownTableRow - splits a markdown table row while respecting escapes. PlayerCharacterAssetUtility.IsHeaderOrSeparator - filters table headers and separator rows. PlayerCharacterAssetUtility.CleanMarkdownCell - removes markdown/image syntax from a table cell. PlayerCharacterAssetUtility.GetObsidianImageFileName - extracts an Obsidian image target file name. PlayerCharacterAssetUtility.DownloadFileAsync - streams a remote file to disk. PlayerCharacterAssetUtility.CreateHttpClient - creates the player asset HTTP client. RandomNumberUtility.GenerateInteger - generates an unbiased cryptographic random integer in a range.

pages.title: Single Instance
pages.content: The current project contains single-instance protection in Program.cs. It uses a named global mutex: private const string SingleInstanceMutexName = @"Global\DungeonMaster.SingleInstance"; Then in Main( ) using Mutex singleInstanceMutex = new(true, SingleInstanceMutexName, out bool createdNew); if (!createdNew) { MessageBox.Show( "Dungeon Master is already running.", "Dungeon Master", MessageBoxButtons.OK, MessageBoxIcon.Information); return; } So if another instance is already running, the new process shows an informational message and exits.

pages.title: May-9-406-PR-Red-Thicket-Encounter
pages.content: The party witnessed two hobgoblins be slain by an owlbear; in the chest left behind by those two in the hollow at the base of a tree, a chest contained: enchanted iron manacles, some coinage, and a crystalline gem-like item bearing a crescent moon engraving. moon-gem.webp

pages.title: Road-Encounter-May-10-406-PR
pages.content: Road Encounter: The Dead Man’s Toll A narrow stretch of road passes through a shallow, wooded ravine. Ahead, the Seekers of the Lost find an old timber tollgate spanning the road. It is clearly abandoned—except that a corpse in rusted mail is sitting upright beside the gate , one skeletal hand resting atop a small iron cashbox. A weather-beaten sign reads: TOLL: ONE SILVER PENNY PER SOUL The dead travel free. The corpse does not move. At least, not until someone attempts to pass without paying. What’s really happening Years ago, this was a legitimate toll station. The tollkeeper and his guards were murdered by brigands, who buried their loot beneath the station rather than risk carrying it immediately. The brigands never returned. Now a small band of goblins has discovered the site . They have rigged the corpse with cords running through holes in the ruined tollhouse, making it appear to move and speak. If someone approaches, the "dead tollkeeper" slowly raises one arm. A hollow voice calls: “One silver for the living. The dead owe nothing.” The goblins are hoping frightened travelers simply throw coins into the box. The Goblins There are 7 goblins , which should make a lively but manageable encounter for six adventurers of levels 2–4. Goblin (7) AC 6 [13], HD 1–1, HP 5, 5, 4, 4, 3, 3, 2 Attacks: Short sword or short bow (1d6) Move 60' (20') Save D14 W15 P16 B17 S18 Morale 7 Alignment Chaotic Four hide inside the ruined tollhouse. Three lie concealed among the trees overlooking the road with short bows. They do not want a fair fight . If the party pays, the goblins let them pass and congratulate themselves on their brilliant scheme. If the PCs expose the trick, the goblins initially try intimidation: “You have disturbed the Keeper of the Road! Now the toll is ten silver each!” If attacked, the hidden archers fire while the others overturn a small cart across the road for cover. The complication During the second round of any fighting—or after several minutes of loud argument—a much more serious problem emerges. The goblins weren't the only creatures attracted to the abandoned station. An ogre named Grum Buckletooth lives farther up the ravine and considers the goblins his subjects. He comes lumbering down the hillside carrying a young pine tree as a club. Grum Buckletooth, Ogre AC 5 [14], HD 4+1, HP 19 Attack: Club (1d10) Move 90' (30') Save D10 W11 P12 B13 S14 Morale 10 Alignment Chaotic Grum isn't immediately hostile. He bellows: “WHO'S STEALING GRUM'S TOLL?” The goblins instantly point at the Seekers. This creates several possibilities instead of forcing a straight combat. The Seekers can fight Grum and the remaining goblins, bargain with him, convince him that the goblins have been stealing from him, or simply give him money. A clever PC examining the tollbox discovers that the goblins have collected 37 sp, 18 cp, and a cheap silver ring worth 15 gp . Grum has never bothered counting it. The buried secret This is where the encounter can become something more than a random fight. Inside the ruined tollhouse is an old floorboard bearing a nearly invisible carved symbol. Beneath it is a rotted leather satchel containing: 126 gp 340 sp a silver dagger worth 35 gp a potion of healing an old brass key a fragment of parchment The parchment contains only part of a message: "...the third marker lies beyond the standing stones. Do not take the king's road. They are watching it. Bring the key to—" The remainder has rotted away. The brass key bears an unfamiliar heraldic symbol. That gives The Seekers of the Lost a potentially literal mystery to seek later. One detail I'd emphasize at the table Make the corpse creepy. When the PCs first approach, don't reveal anything about cords or goblins. Describe the dead tollkeeper's jaw slowly opening as a dry voice says: “Six travelers. Six pennies.” If they pay six silver pieces, the skeletal hand slowly points down the road. Then let the players decide whether they're sufficiently unnerved to keep walking—or sufficiently curious to investigate. For this particular party, I like the encounter because it has combat, trickery, negotiation, exploration, treasure, and a campaign hook , while still being something you can resolve in roughly 20–40 minutes if you just need an interesting incident during a day's travel. heraldic-symbol-key.webp

pages.title: Brazen Strumpet
pages.content: An inn and tavern in Helix built in PR 08, burned up in a fire in PR 22, was rebuilt in 24. The establishment saw the addition of another wing in PR 30 that had two stories and housed 12 double-bed room (6 per level). Mordicar Justhand has lobbied the owner to change the inn's name, but Hourby Minutos has so far refused.

pages.title: Brokenhead Inn
pages.content: This inn is actually located in the Surface Ruins of Arden Vul itself, not in Gosterwick. It is run by Kronos Kettle-Belly and is the last stop for a meal before you descend into the dungeon.

pages.title: Brooknash Coster Inn
pages.content: An upscale inn in Threshold catering to adventurers.

pages.title: Circle K Inn
pages.content: The Circle K Inn is the name of an inn that was built onto the pre-existing tavern once known as Morgan's Morsels & Tankards . The tavern, rebranded as only Morgan's Morsels after the Red Laws came into effect, now has a large wing add-on with double-bed rooms enough for fourteen guests. Word is that the Prelacy financed the additional construction to assuage Morgan regarding the loss of income from alcohol sales.

pages.title: Griffon's Tongue
pages.content: A fairly nice pub and diner in Eastdale. The proprietor is Gaston Fellshroud, a middle-aged Gnome who also happens to be a psion. Given its location, the establishment necessarily observes the Red Laws' prohibition against drinking alcohol. But Gaston has been dosing this with calea and yerba, and the effects of the drink are very pleasant, so much so in fact that it is selling better even than the establishment's former alcoholic beverages.

pages.title: Kern's Rest & Revelry
pages.content: An apparently average-quality hostel jointly operated by House Ghallanda and House Thuranni in the city of Threshold. In addition to multiple performing stages and rooms for rent, the establishment incorporates a number of private rooms that have witnessed every sort of secret dealing. The private rooms are rumored to be magically protected against observation, though some believe they simply incorporate the more mundane approach of thin lead sheeting within the walls.

pages.title: Malaster's Eastdale Emporium
pages.content: The equipment supplies company owned and operated by Malaster Rendalis of Eastdale. The company caters to the needs of adventurers.

pages.title: Morgan's Morsels
pages.content: This tavern/inn in the hamlet of Kirkilston was originally called Morgan's Morsels & Tankards , but since the Red Laws took effect a few years ago '& Tankards' has been painted over. The establishment in run by Morgan Maynard Canden, a retired first level fighter who, due to a traumatic experience years ago, is no longer about to fight. Now, he is an Innkeeper. The prices charged are a pittance of what they were before the Red Laws were implemented. The Prelacy subsidizes these low prices. Keeping prices low, it is believed, will draw settlers.

pages.title: Retep’s Relics
pages.content: A shop in Eastdale that sells antiques and precious metal items. It is run by proprietor Retep Garnetstone.

pages.title: Silver Standard Trading Company
pages.content: A company that specializes in both providing and protecting caravans to and from thorpes, hamlets, towns, and cities across Slaytonthorpe, The Prelacy of Middenmark, the Duchy of Aerik, and the Principality of Brine. In addition to the exchange of goods, the company is often asked to transport persons or cargo of import. In these situations the rate of pay is triple or more. Members of the Ironguard family and select merchants always travel with additional protection. Earnest Thromb works for and owns shares in this company. This company's home base is Eastdale.

pages.title: Stonehill Inn
pages.content: The only inn in the frontier town of Phandalin. Somewhat confusingly, there are identically named inns in Eastdale and Helix; in the latter village, an entire wing has been added and now serves to host visitors who come to treat with the Seekers. The inn in Eastdale had a pair of suites that are always reserved from envoys from Citadel Silver and the Gauntwood Galleries.

pages.title: The Broken Hilt
pages.content: Nestled along the main cobbled street of Raven's Pass, The Broken Hilt stands as a sturdy, soot-stained building with a low stone foundation and dark timber walls blackened by years of fire and smoke. The scent of hot iron and coal hangs heavily in the air, mixing with a faint tang of oil and metal polish. Outside, a swinging wooden sign depicts a bent sword over an anvil, weathered by sun and rain but still legible. Sparks occasionally fly from the open front forge, visible through the wide doorway, hinting at the constant hammering within. the-broken-hilt.webp Inside, the shop is dimly lit by hanging lanterns, the walls lined with racks of finished weapons, shields, and armor. The forge dominates the back of the workshop, always alight, with bellows puffing and flames licking the air. Samuel Armstrong, the shops proprietor, is a stocky man with a perpetually furrowed brow and a gruff, sour demeanor. His hands are calloused and blackened from years of hammering metal, and he rarely offers more than curt responses to customers. Yet, beneath his cantankerous exterior lies a craftsman of unparalleled skill: his specialty equipment - custom swords, reinforced armor, and finely balanced axes - are sought by adventurers and mercenaries alike. Even the most hesitant visitor quickly realizes that while Samuel may scowl and grumble, his work speaks for itself , and a weapon forged at The Broken Hilt is a prized asset worth every coin. Shelves and tables are cluttered with half-finished projects, intricate metalwork, and tools arranged in precise, albeit chaotic, order, a testament to the blacksmiths devotion to quality above courtesy.

pages.title: The Mason's Apron
pages.content: A small tavern in the Raven's Pass thorpe, this establishment is run by Nimba Armstrong, a sister to Nuanda Nemere, and the wife of Samuel Armstrong who runs The Broken Hilt. In addition to a small restaurant, this establishment has a wing of rooms available for five silver coins per night, or 3 gold coins per week if paid in advance.

pages.title: The Saucy Tart
pages.content: A tavern in Eastdale that is permitted to serve alcohol for two hours on Mondays, Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Fridays, beginning two hours after sunset.

pages.title: Turgen's Trade Goods
pages.content: A general goods store in the village of Helix, run by Billworth Turgen, a middle-aged man.

pages.title: AD & BC
pages.content: The idea to count years from the birth of Jesus Christ was first proposed in the year 525 by Dionysius Exiguus, a Christian monk. Standardized under the Julian and Gregorian calendars, the system spread throughout Europe and the Christian world during the centuries that followed. AD stands for Anno Domini, Latin for "in the year of the Lord", while BC stands for "before Christ". CE stands for "common (or current) era", while BCE stands for "before the common (or current) era". These abbreviations have a shorter history than BC and AD, although they still date from at least the early 1700s. An important reason for adopting BCE/CE is religious neutrality. Since the Gregorian calendar has superseded other calendars to become the international standard, members of non-Christian groups may object to the explicitly Christian origins of BC and AD. Particularly problematic is AD ("in the year of the Lord"), and its unavoidable implication that the Lord in question is Jesus Christ. Religious neutrality was the main rationale behind Jewish academics„¢ adoption of BCE/CE over a century ago, and continues to be its most widely cited justification. However, others object to the BC/AD system on the basis that it is objectively inaccurate. It is widely accepted that the actual birth of Jesus occurred at least two years before AD 1, and so some argue that explicitly linking years to an erroneous birthdate for Jesus is arbitrary or even misleading. BCE/CE avoids this inaccuracy since it does not explicitly refer to the birth of Jesus, removing some of the baggage associated with our dating system while also acknowledging that the starting point for 1 CE is essentially a convention.

pages.title: Festival of Forging
pages.content: An annual two-day festival held in Threshold yearly on May 13th and 14th to honor the best smiths of the land and to put their creations on display ” some for sale, some not.

pages.title: Grimtidings
pages.content: Annual observance of the Duergar on December 21 in which they lay down their tools and gather to hear stories of their voluntary exile and the decadence of other dwarves. Laduguer is praised for his great skill, and the Duergar swear vengeance against those who have insulted their god and their people.

pages.title: Human Pre-History
pages.content: Prehistory, also called pre-literary history, is the period of human history between the first known use of stone tools by hominins c. 3.3 million years BC and the beginning of recorded history with the invention of writing systems. The use of symbols, marks, and images appears very early among humans, but the earliest known writing systems appeared c.3,000 BC.

pages.title: The Colonial Period
pages.content: Some commentators identify three waves of European colonialism. The two main countries in the first wave of European colonialism were Portugal and Spain. The Portuguese started the long age of European colonization with the conquest of Ceuta, Morocco in 1415 The second wave of European colonialism commenced with Britain's involvement in Asia in support of the British East India Company. The third wave ("New Imperialism") consisted of the Scramble for Africa regulated by the terms of the Berlin Conference of 1884-1885. Only fourteen 20th century independent countries escaped formal colonization by European powers: Afghanistan, Ethiopia, Bhutan, China, Iran, Japan, Liberia, Mongolia, Nepal, North Korea, Saudi Arabia, South Korea, Thailand, and Turkey as well as North Yemen.

pages.title: The Disaster
pages.content: A regional even that occurred in Issenda in PR 105, April 18th. It inverted magic in a considerable area, but historians debate where that area exists on the map. Many believe it must be near Arden Vul and that it was somehow linked with that mega dungeon.

pages.title: The Great Declension
pages.content: The Great Declension was set off on July 2nd, 2080 CE, by intercontinental and space-based missile attacks that sparked World War III. Approximately 5% of the world's nine billion humans were killed in the initial blasts. That figure rose to 50% in the next several months, due to radiation sickness and the violence of societal anarchy that predictably ensued. By March 1, 2081, 4.5 billion people comprised the totality of humanity on planet earth. Conventional warfare among survivors of the nuclear holocaust took place from July 3rd, 2080 to Feb 16, 2082, CE, lowering the Earth's human population to 3.8 billion by October 22, 2082 CE. Global production, relations, the sciences, and other areas declined rapidly. In Europe and North America hardened subterranean bunkers were employed by surviving leadership and by some of the formerly most affluent or influential individuals, while many other survivors drew together in enclaves in the least affected regions ” which included the Rocky Mountains, the Swiss Alps, the Everglades, and other areas in South America and Eurasia. This great decline continued through the remaining decades of the 21st century and the first half of the 22nd century. International trade slowed to a crawl, space programs were moth-balled, medical care in many areas reverted to that of earlier centuries, due to a shortage of infrastructure and pharmaceuticals.

pages.title: The Industrial Age
pages.content: The Industrial Age is a period of history that encompasses the changes in economic and social organization that began around 1760 in Great Britain and later in other countries, characterized chiefly by the replacement of hand tools with power-driven machines such as the power loom and the steam engine, and by the concentration of industry in large establishments.

pages.title: The Information Age
pages.content: It is commonly believed that The Industrial Age was supplanted by the Information Age in the late 20th century A.D., a view that became common after the Revolutions of 1989, when much of the Third World economy was still based on manufacturing, although mobile phones were commonplace even in the poorest of African countries, enabling access to global information networks. Even though many developing countries remained largely industrial, the Information Age was increasingly on the ground by the late 20th century. The Information Age was also characterized by the digitalization of information and communication systems, and the widespread adoption of computing devices ” personal, mainframe, and embedded systems. It encompasses the era in which information and data are produced, shared, and accessed at an unprecedented rate due to the proliferation of computers, the internet, and other technological innovations.

pages.title: Adventure Outline
pages.content: Adventure Outline Source files inspected: Release/Posts/IC/ch-1.html Release/Posts/IC/ch-2.html Release/Posts/IC/ch-3.html Release/Posts/IC/ch-4.html Release/Posts/IC/ch-5.html Ch 1 - Kirkilston The party organizes roles before leaving Kirkilston: Mapper: Slip, tentative. Caller: Kelpie, tentative. Quartermaster: Urvan. Chronicler: Jelb, tentative and later confirmed. The immediate objective is to seek Nuanda the Good Witch, who lives less than an hour from Kirkilston. Kelpie takes the fore as the group leaves the village by the southeastern path. A wild boar charges the party in the forest. Kelpie holds the front line while Jelb commands Melbor and Kaybar to attack. The dogs badly wound the boar, and Urvan lands the killing blow. The party briefly butchers the enormous boar, prioritizing useful cuts and gifts for Nuanda rather than a full field dressing. The group reaches Nuanda's moss-covered cottage in the fog-laden forest. Nuanda welcomes the party, asks them to help prepare stew, and recognizes their urgency. Kelpie explains that Jelenneth, daughter of Farmer Heldrith and Parker Laneworth, is missing from north of Kirkilston. Nuanda asks whether the party has an item belonging to Jelenneth, since that would make her search easier. The chapter closes by sending play to Chapter 2. Ch 2 - Supper With Nuanda Jelb produces Jelenneth's glove, given to him by her brother for tracking purposes. Nuanda is pleased because the glove lets her seek Jelenneth more effectively through the Dream World. The party stays overnight at Nuanda's cottage. During supper: Nuanda discusses white witches, black witches, and the destructive powers used by the latter. Urvan asks careful questions from the perspective of the Red Bannermen. Jelb speaks about law, good, and the kind of god he seeks. Kelpie shares elements of his difficult past and his devotion to Demetra. Nuanda prepares wards and instructs the party in words meant to call her back from the Shadow or Dream World if needed. Morrow, Nuanda's black cat, is sent outside to guard against elves and other threats. Jelb carefully observes the magic and repeats Nuanda's return phrase. The night passes safely. In the morning, Nuanda reports what she learned: Jelenneth was abducted by bandits while picking berries near her family's property. She was taken northward. Nuanda contacted Kuiper, a ranger ally who ranges between Raven's Pass, Threshold, Slaytonthorpe, the Coal Hills, Coalscuttle, and nearby settlements. Multiple communities have suffered abductions and disappearances. Nuanda identifies the Blanryde Hills as a likely destination or lead, west of the Coal Hills in the Slaytonthorpe area under Count Parlfray. Nuanda gives the party a map and asks them to obtain ritual components: An amethyst. A sprig of Hwyanthemon. Hair from a slain orc. Nuanda recommends joining a caravan from Kirkilston to Raven's Pass instead of traveling alone. She gives the party hard biscuits and honey for the road. She advises them to ask Nimba at The Mason's Apron in Raven's Pass for an introduction to Samuel the blacksmith. The party agrees to take caravan guard work and continue the search. The chapter closes by sending play to Chapter 3. Ch 3 - Joining the Caravan to Raven's Pass The party is traveling with Billworth Turgen's caravan toward Raven's Pass. The available chapter file opens with the party responding to signs of orcspawn activity and a horn call. Kelpie argues for moving toward Blightstone Pit rather than racing to Raven's Pass with incomplete information. Thurgan sends woodsmen to locate Urvan, Maximilian, and Narinza and guide them toward the quarry rendezvous. Melbor and Kaybar alert Jelb and help locate the separated companions. The party reunites and pushes the caravan hard toward Blightstone Pit. Billworth drives the mules faster while Thurgan coordinates the rear guard. Near the abandoned quarry, at least two dozen orcs emerge from the forest behind the caravan. The caravan attempts to outrun the ambush. Jelb casts an illusion of a rockslide at a choke point to disrupt the pursuit. Thurgan and caravan guards fire into the attackers while the wagons rush forward. Some caravan guards are killed by orc arrows. Urvan and Narinza are cut off by orcs as the wagons swing wide of the pit. Kelpie, Geoffroy, Maximilian, Jelb, and the dogs prepare to hold a defensive position near the rock wall. Jelb distributes flasks of oil to guards and prepares fire as part of the defensive plan. The chapter closes by sending play to Chapter 4. Ch 4 - Battle at Blightstone Pit The battle continues at Blightstone Pit. Jelb throws a rock, then sends Melbor and Kaybar against orcs threatening Thurgan. The dogs flank and kill an orc. Kelpie kills another orc. Geoffroy and Fluffy fight aggressively at the line. Maximilian uses his sling, eventually killing an orc with a headshot. Jelb casts Color Spray against two orcs near the western end of the wagons, disabling them for several rounds. Kelpie swaps forward to protect Maximilian, who is poorly suited for melee. The party works to clear the northern path while holding off the remaining orcs. A huge tentacled creature begins climbing out of Blightstone Pit. The orc leader orders a retreat, saying they can find others to offer to "The Deep Friends." The creature snatches remaining orcs from the quarry floor. The party shifts from fighting to escaping before the creature fully emerges. The caravan begins turning away from the pit. Kelpie helps drag and force the wagons clear while others scramble aboard or help the flight. The chapter closes by sending play to Chapter 5. Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape The party has escaped the immediate danger at Blightstone Pit and studies a scroll Jelb recovered from a slain orc. Thurgan identifies the Toothbreakers as a large orcish clan from the hills above Milborne. The scroll references "Deep Friends" and a "Red Tusk," suggesting an organized power behind the orc activity. The group discusses whether Urvan was killed, taken by orcs, or otherwise separated, and whether Narinza might be involved. Thurgan mentions old suspicions that the drow were involved in the departure of the surface elves from places like the Glittering Canopy and Aelith-Calaer. Algorn Druff arrives from the south, sent by Nuanda's magic after she scried the party's progress. Algorn examines the scroll and concludes it had two authors: One knowledgeable author who listed desired captives such as a Red Bannerman, a Drow of Night Below, and a half elf or elf of the ancient line. One less sophisticated orcish author handling more direct orders or additions. Kelpie argues that the orcspawn may be connected to Jenny's disappearance and that following Jenny's trail may also reveal what happened to Urvan and Narinza. The group chooses to continue toward Raven's Pass rather than return to the pit. Geoffroy speculates about treasure in the tentacled creature's lair. Algorn notes that making Blightstone Pit safe again could be enormously valuable because the quarry still contains years of usable stone. Thurgan leads the surviving caravan into an overnight camp with the wagons circled in a defensible clearing. Around camp, Algorn discusses possible surface factions using orcs as muscle or fodder, including: The Basilisk's Claw. The Cult of the Dragon. The Zhentarim. Jelb searches his memory for what he knows about those factions and studies the scroll for clues about authorship. The caravan passes safely through the night. By late morning, the group reaches outlying farmsteads near Raven's Pass. Local farmers report that town authorities have sent runners south to Milborne and Threshold for aid against orc problems. The caravan reaches Raven's Pass and delivers the remaining goods. Billworth Turgen treats the party to a meal at The Mason's Apron and pays each adventurer fifteen gold coins in thanks. Kelpie prepares for the next leg into the Blanryde Hills. Maximilian worries about Urvan, Narinza, and the growing scale of the opposition. Active Leads and Open Threads Jelenneth "Jenny" remains missing after being abducted by bandits and carried north. The Blanryde Hills are the next major destination for the search. Nuanda's requested components remain outstanding: Amethyst. Hwyanthemon. Hair from a slain orc. The recovered orc scroll links the Toothbreakers, the Deep Friends, Red Tusk, and a second non-orc author. The enemy appears interested in specific valuable captives, including a Red Bannerman, a Drow of Night Below, and someone of ancient elven blood. Urvan and Narinza's fate remains uncertain. The tentacled creature beneath Blightstone Pit is a major unresolved threat and possible treasure site. Surface factions may be manipulating the orcs, with Algorn naming the Basilisk's Claw, the Cult of the Dragon, and the Zhentarim as possibilities. Raven's Pass, The Mason's Apron, Nimba, and Samuel the blacksmith are immediate support points.

pages.title: Jelb Orphan Note
pages.content: not intended for publishing DM Note made 6.2.2026: awarded Jelb +400 XP ad-hoc for player's reworking of Mystic Theurge DM Note made 6.2.2026: On the morning of May 07, PR 406, Jelb encountered a Couatl. The creature was surprised that Jelb could detect its true form, given that it had been posing as Nuanda's cat familiar for several years. In the couatl's wizened view, this was evidence of something quite extraordinary about Jelb, something the creature referred to as Jelb's ' soul-spark ': "I have heard your thoughts, and you have my thanks. This power I see flickering in your core; I have not seen its like in centuries, not since the Phaerimm incursion during the era of the Helvecians. The purity of your soul-spark... it's the brightest I've seen in a mortal. We will be able to communicate, be'times, even from great distances. I will communicate with you again if certain conditions I deem likely actually do occur." I've not let the player know this, but my thought is that he could rise to become one of the three most powerful illusionists in all Issendran history. Why? How? Perhaps there is Visitor blood flowing in his veins from an ancestor's flirtation with an Occupier...

pages.title: Lineages
pages.content: Lineages of Issenda This note separates established campaign lore from connective interpretation and new material proposed for Scarlet Horizons. The old sources do not describe a clean family tree. They describe repeated acts of making: the Throiki seeded servitor peoples, the Sarrukh altered living bodies, and later cultures bred, crossed, worshipped, and misunderstood what remained. The useful model is a set of branching lineages rather than a single ladder: Far Ancients / Throiki influence elder servitor stock / \ Aelves Draega Turtaqua Dhaelves true and aquatic lesser branches dragons Visitors + humans -> Sarrukh -> yuan-ti and other saurian lines Sarrukh techniques + draconic remnants + later breeding -> unstable hybrids The named survivors below are either established figures or proposed additions. A name marked “proposed” is campaign material, not a claim about existing canon. 1. The Throiki servitor stock The oldest surviving lineage is not a race but a design family. The Throiki appear to have seeded Issenda with several servitor peoples, including the Turtaqua, Draega, and Aelves. The Throiki did not need every branch to remain genetically identical. Their work could be directed through magical mutation, selective breeding, geomancy, and environmental pressure. This explains why distant peoples can share traits without sharing a recent ancestor. Aelf, dragon, and Turtaqua features may be echoes of a common program, while their bodies and cultures remain completely different. Likely survivors include: Modern Turtaqua, who retain a visible transformation between quadrupedal aquatic form and a temporary bipedal shape. Dhaelves, descended from Aelves through a long series of subraces. Their magical aptitude and cultural horror of servitude preserve distorted memories of an ancient servitor origin. True dragons and their lesser descendants, whose bodies retain the deepest and most durable Throiki adaptations. Isolated, unclassified populations still living near old installations, menhirs, or buried biological systems. The strongest surviving members of this root are not necessarily the oldest creatures. A dormant Throiki system could preserve a young specimen with a complete inheritance while an ancient surface population carries only a few damaged traits. 2. The Aelven to Dhaelve lineage The Aelves are extinct as a distinct people, according to Maelin's Hûl Hildresu research, but their subraces survive. The Dhaelves are the clearest surviving branch. They have retained unusual magical traditions and an intense cultural refusal to serve anyone. Their society has converted an ancestral condition into its opposite: the Aelves served, so the Dhaelves will never serve. The Dhaelves are therefore a living memory of the old lineage even when they reject the interpretation. Their spellcraft may preserve techniques that began as Throiki interfaces or biological controls. Their oldest archives could contain records that describe the Aelves as a people without understanding why those records use the language of maintenance, deployment, and function. Established surviving individuals and groups: The Dhaelven priesthoods of Arcantryl and Imperiosa, whose rivalry preserves two competing interpretations of ancestral power. The Hûl Hildresu, who study the Aelves and other Throiki servitor lines. Maelin Vey's testimony gives the party an unusually direct account of this research. Ancient or isolated Dhaelven houses that still preserve pre-civilizational rites, especially subterranean Beltarist communities. Proposed key individual: Vaelith Sorn, an Arcantrylite archivist who has discovered that several Dhaelven “spell forms” are not spells at all. They are command protocols designed to communicate with living Throiki systems. Vaelith is powerful enough to open a dormant archive but lacks the moral certainty to decide whether the archive should be awakened. She could become an ally to Maelin, a rival to the Hûl Hildresu, or the first Dhaelve to learn that her ancestors were made to serve. Power and campaign significance: Dhaelven magic should be sophisticated rather than merely destructive. A surviving Aelven-derived device might recognize a Dhaelve as a valid operator, while rejecting humans and even Sarrukh. This gives the party a reason to protect, distrust, or bargain with Dhaelven factions during the search for Throiki sites. 3. The Draega and the Draconic Kindreds The Draega began, according to Maelin, as small winged snakes. Over later millennia some grew into creatures that resemble the dragons known in the present age. This branch contains the clearest distinction between true dragons and lesser dragonkind. The Weighty Eight are recorded as the eight original and still extant True Dragons: Riothamus, Glaurthogos, Pryrates, Inzeldrin, Balagos, Claugiyliamatar, Iymrith, and Mornauguth. All later dragonkind is said to have come from these oviparous creatures, though Ocineroth's account warns that resemblance does not prove ancestry. Some lesser dragons may instead descend from failed Sarrukh work, native animals marked by draconic influence, or later cross-breeding. Established likely survivors: Inzeldrin, the ancient green dragon associated with Thundertree, Misty Mire, and the lizardfolk of Shrieken Mire. Inzeldrin is a living political power, not a monster waiting in isolation. The lizardfolk's protection and worship give the dragon influence over a regional population. Doneldun, the dragon turtle of Lake Donally, whose lineage may be an aquatic Draconic Kindred rather than a direct member of the Draega line. The last verified conversation with Halathra Moonbeam occurred in 368 PR; the silence since then is itself a campaign mystery. The other members of the Weighty Eight, whose survival makes them potential ancestors, patrons, enemies, or custodians of ancient knowledge. The lesser dragons, wyverns, cave wyrms, swamp drakes, and other diluted descendants that the Cult of the Dragon treats as possible raw material. Proposed key individual: Serakh Veyr, a young swamp-drake descended from a line exposed to a standing-stone network. Serakh is not a true dragon, but its breath weapon can alter memory in living plants. The Cult wants to breed it with a more powerful specimen. The Red Thicket may already be responding to its presence. Power and campaign significance: A true dragon's power is more than hit dice, breath damage, and treasure. Its long residence changes the land. Plants, weather, dreams, minerals, and magic begin to reflect the dragon's presence. A true dragon near an old menhir complex could be the reason the stones were built, the reason they still function, or the reason someone is trying to invert them. 4. The Sarrukh, yuan-ti, and elder saurian branches The Sarrukh were produced through Visitor-human breeding experiments and later developed their own ability to reproduce. They became magically powerful saurian humanoids and, according to the current lore, used gene-splicing and geomancy in the development of the first dragonkind. Most scholars agree that the yuan-ti either descended from or were created by the Sarrukh. This does not make Sarrukh and dragons the same lineage. It makes them neighboring branches with a history of exchange. Sarrukh techniques may have copied, modified, or combined draconic traits without reproducing the deeper Throiki architecture. Established surviving figures and groups: Sseth, god of the four-armed yuan-ti and an older saurian people from whom the yuan-ti descended. The yuan-ti, who may preserve the clearest living cultural memory of Sarrukh biological arts. The suspected Sarrukh survivors who have taken permanent dragon form to observe their experiments. The rumored cult of Sseth in the Northern Reaches. Proposed key individual: Ssavax the Unfinished, a Sarrukh who has maintained a humanoid form for centuries but has never completed the transformation into a stable dragon form. Ssavax can alter flesh, suppress poison, and force temporary adaptations in living creatures. Each alteration leaves a memory echo that can be read by a powerful psychometrist such as Maelin. Ssavax wants the Throiki acorn because it may contain a template stable enough to finish the transformation. Power and campaign significance: Sarrukh power should feel surgical. A Sarrukh does not need to win a battle by force if it can remove a creature's ability to breathe, give a human gills for one hour, or make a dragon's scales grow in the wrong pattern. Their presence connects the yuan-ti, dragonkind, Throiki artifacts, and the biological archive hidden in the Red Thicket. 5. The Turtaqua branch The Turtaqua are another known Throiki servitor lineage. They hatch from eggs, mature rapidly, become large and powerful in adulthood, breathe water, and can assume a temporary bipedal humanoid form. Their biology is stable enough to produce a living people, but strange enough to preserve its origin in design rather than ordinary evolution. Likely surviving members include established Turtaqua communities in freshwater, bog, fen, and coastal environments. Most have no reason to think of themselves as an experiment. Their physical adaptations have become ordinary life: swimming, trampling, egg-laying, and changing shape when dealing with other peoples. Proposed key individual: Orro of the Deep Shell, an elderly Turtaqua cartographer who has mapped old submerged stone arrangements. Orro believes several “natural” lake formations are damaged Throiki control stations. He is physically formidable, with the strength and durability of an ancient adult, but his greatest power is geographic memory. He could lead the party toward a submerged archive connected to Doneldun's silence. Power and campaign significance: Turtaqua give the campaign a lineage that is neither draconic nor humanoid in appearance but still tied to the same ancient makers. They can reach sites that the party cannot, and their temporary humanoid form lets them act as interpreters between surface settlements and older aquatic powers. 6. The Red Thicket memory lineage The warm acorn Maelin identifies is a seed from one of the Red Thicket's oldest surviving lineages and a biological archive key. The forest appears to possess a distributed memory. Individual trees die, but impressions can survive through roots, fungi, and connected living systems. This may be a native lineage altered by Throiki influence, or a Throiki biological network that has become a forest. The lineage is not a race in the ordinary sense. It is a continuity of living memory. A tree, root mass, mandrake, treant, or other plant creature may carry fragments of the same ancestral record without sharing a body or a single mind. Likely surviving members: The oldest trees of the Red Thicket, which may remember events no living humanoid witnessed. Mandrakes and treants whose bodies are descended from or altered by the ancient forest system. Root-bound creatures created when a living animal is absorbed into the network and later returned with incomplete memories. A hidden intelligence that the Deep Friends are trying to locate through Maelin, the acorn, and the pulsing root. Proposed key individual: Morrowbark, a mandrake who appears to be an ordinary old forest guardian but carries memories from several dead trees. Morrowbark is not omniscient. It confuses seasons, faces, and locations, yet it remembers the shape of Throiki devices and the sound of people who entered the forest before the current kingdoms existed. Power and campaign significance: Morrowbark and related beings can reveal history without behaving like an archive. They may answer a question with a smell, a recurring dream, a borrowed voice, or a memory belonging to someone else. The acorn is dangerous because planting it could create a new node in the network, overwrite existing memory, or allow an outside intelligence to enter the forest. 7. Cult-bred crossbreeds: the false kindreds The Cult of the Dragon has preserved fragments of genuine knowledge but does not understand the original system. Its members trace bloodlines, steal eggs and hatchlings, expose creatures to relics and menhirs, and call their experiments sacraments. Most attempts fail. Some create monsters. A few produce creatures that are powerful enough to frighten their makers. The false kindreds are therefore cross-breeds and mutations rather than a single species. Possible ingredients include: Lesser Draega or dragonkind blood. Sarrukh flesh-working techniques. Human, lizardfolk, or yuan-ti stock. Exposure to a standing-stone network. Concentrated influence from a true dragon or an ancient Throiki installation. Proposed key individual: Haskara, called the Brass-Winged Daughter by the Cult. Haskara was bred from a winged serpent line and a lizardfolk lineage protected by Inzeldrin. She has a short-range flight ability, a poisonous breath that induces obedience dreams, and an instinctive response to menhir alignments. She escaped before the Cult could complete the final ritual. Haskara's history should remain uncertain. She may have killed her makers, or they may have released her deliberately to follow her to a forgotten site. She is intelligent enough to bargain, frightened enough to lie, and powerful enough to become a campaign antagonist without being a world-ending threat. Power and campaign significance: The false kindreds make the Cult's threat concrete. The party can encounter a creature that is both victim and danger, then decide whether to kill it, hide it, cure it, or use it to find the next standing-stone site. Haskara also forces the party to distinguish the creature's guilt from the Cult's responsibility. What may still be alive The most plausible surviving lineages are those that preserve themselves without requiring a functioning civilization: True dragons and their descendants, because the original design made them self-repairing and self-reproducing. Turtaqua, because their reproductive cycle and aquatic habitats protect them from many surface collapses. Dhaelves, because an Aelven branch survived by becoming a civilization rather than remaining a servitor population. Sarrukh or Sarrukh-derived beings, because long life, transformation, and concealment make them difficult to count. The Red Thicket memory network, because its survival does not depend on any single organism. Cult-bred hybrids, because the Cult keeps rediscovering enough old knowledge to produce new branches even when older branches die. The most important surviving individuals are not necessarily the strongest. Inzeldrin can threaten a region. Sseth can shape a religion. A hidden Sarrukh can alter a body. But Maelin, Orro, Morrowbark, or Haskara can carry a piece of evidence that changes what the party believes about the world's ancestry. The central campaign question is therefore not “which creature came first?” It is “who still possesses the ability to make, alter, or remember living things?” The answer may lead from the Red Thicket to the standing stones, from the standing stones to the Cult, and from the Cult to the buried works of the Throiki. Source anchors and continuity notes Established sources: Intentional Orphans/Ocineroth-On-True-Dragons — true dragons, lesser draconic kindreds, the Cult's breeding experiments, and the standing-stone networks. Intentional Orphans/Maelin Vey — the Throiki servitor lineages, the Draega, Turtaqua, Aelves, Red Thicket memory, and the biological archive acorn. Races/Sarrukh — Visitor-human origins, Sarrukh breeding experiments, dragonkind, and yuan-ti ancestry. Races/Turtaqua — Turtaqua biology, transformation, and powers. Powers/Gods/Sseth — Sseth's relationship to yuan-ti and the elder saurian people. Powers/Factions/The Weighty Eight — the eight named True Dragons. Powers/Gods/Dhaelven Deity Worship — Dhaelven ancestry, magical inheritance, and the cultural rejection of servitude. Meta/Far Ancients and Meta/Throiki — the older civilization and modern evidence concerning the Visitors/Throiki. New material proposed in this note: Vaelith Sorn, Serakh Veyr, Ssavax the Unfinished, Orro of the Deep Shell, Morrowbark, Haskara, and the specific histories and powers assigned to them. These can be promoted into dedicated NPC or creature notes when they enter play.

pages.title: Memorable IC Passages
pages.content: Shade posted on 8/05/2026 as part of Chapter 7 Message #70: Of course, in the Underdark they wouldn't be getting rained upon in the first place. Eaten, maybe. Caught, tortured, dismembered, and their brains sucked out by nameless abominations, possibly. But rained on? Unheard of. --- Neria posted on 7/28/2026, as part of Chapter 7 Message #11: Neria is the first cleric to whom Cromm has spoken, without aid of a Commune spell, in half a century. How does she feel about that? She has always been emotionally and spiritually sensitive. What does her intuition suggest? She listened carefully to the drow, taking as much note of what he said as she had of the countryside around them. "Collective will," she mused, and looked around at the forest with still greater interest. With great care, she also reached out to touch one of the nearby trunks, head tilted. "And together all these trees are greater than the sum of their parts," she guessed, glancing at Shade for confirmation. "Yes, we must be certain to take care. To make no assumptions. There are... there are things of great import happening, I believe, and we are caught up in them." ---
