pages.title: Aelith-Calaer
pages.content: An elven city inhabited from AR 698 to PR 392, its population peaked in PR 288 at more than 15,000 elves. As of PR 406, Aelith-Calaer is an uninhabited shell of its former glory, though many dwellings, monuments, and permanent enchantments remain.

pages.title: Altgrimmr
pages.content: A dwarven stronghold in the Western Threshold Range mountains a dozen miles northeast of Thundertree and ten miles northwest from the city of Threshold. In centuries past, there was warfare between Altgrimmr and the Duergar city of Barakuir ” over a hundred miles of winding tunnels connected the latter with the surface fortress of Altgrimmr. Barakuir lies eight-five miles south of Altgrimmr, and is a surface stronghold.

pages.title: Araurilcaurak
pages.content: The immense cavern housing the Drow city of Menzoberranzan.

pages.title: Arden Vul
pages.content: A mega dungeon somewhere in the expanse once known as Arandia during the Chalrassan Era.

pages.title: Barakuir
pages.content: Barakuir, also known as the Iron Kingdom, was a part of the dwarven realm of Shanatar, dominated by the shield dwarf Clan Duergar, whose inhabitants would eventually be transformed into the gray dwarves. The kingdom venerated Laduguer and was ruled by a priest-king who was known as the Iron Shield. Barakuir lies in the Middledark, eighty-five miles north of Altgrimmr and about six miles beneath the Surface.

pages.title: Barrowmaze
pages.content: An extensive warren of barrow tombs beneath the marsh that is sometimes called The Barrow Bog, southwest of Helix. These tombs are remnants from an earlier civilization in the area ” the Cumerians. In recent years, more and more undead have been boiling out of this area into the surrounding marsh and sometimes even to the southern edge of Helix and into the streets of Bogtown. barrowmazeMap.png

pages.title: Benediction
pages.content: A fabled ancient town or city that supposedly predated even ancient Undalan and may (it has never been confirmed) lie in ruins below Undalan, which lies beneath Phandalin.

pages.title: Blacktooth Keep
pages.content: Built in the years 21 to 32 PR, this small fortress was erected on the site where Kurg Blacktooth slew the Shou witch-priestess Golnadeg Grue-Spitter and her elite Bugbear unit, putting an end to the swath of destruction they had carved through Smokeshadow, Dolecherry, and Silent Diamond. Blacktooth joined Smokeshadow and Moonwall in fielding men-at-arms to patrol the Farground Road against incursions by Gnoll, ogres, and occasional giants from the surrounding hills.

pages.title: Blingdenstone
pages.content: An upper Middledark svirfneblin city, located approximately forty-five miles west of Menzoberranzan.

pages.title: Bogtown
pages.content: A town of 1,932 people located approximately seventeen miles southwest of the Deep Ones' Bridge and twenty-four miles south and slightly west of Ironguard Motte. The Barrowmoor is an extensive warren of barrow tombs beneath the marsh that is sometimes called The Barrow Bog, southwest of Helix. These tombs are remnants from an earlier civilization in the area ” the Cumerians. In recent years, more and more undead have been boiling out of this area into the surrounding marsh and sometimes even to the southern edge of Helix and into the streets of Bogtown. Bogtown is a rough frontier settlement in the Duchy of Aerik , positioned where the more settled parts of the Northern Reaches begin to give way to marsh, old forest, and increasingly dangerous wilderness. It functions less like a conventional town and more like a swamp-side trading post, waystation, and last dependable stop for travelers pushing into the harsher country beyond. Hunters, trappers, prospectors, adventurers, drovers, charcoal burners, guides, and dubious merchants all have reason to pass through. Its economy would naturally revolve around supplies, marsh products, hides, timber, salvage, ferrying, and whatever unusual goods come out of the wilderness. Geographically, Bogtown sits near an important transition zone. The Darkwood lies generally west or northwest , and trails heading that way deteriorate quickly from roads into tracks and then into little more than remembered routes beneath ancient trees. Farther west lies Westkeep and its watchtower, which watches movement between the Darkwood and the more settled reaches of Middenmark. Bogtown also lies near the northern Moon Peaks and the edge of the Blackened Forest , with Hammerhand dwarves established in the northernmost reaches of the Moon Peaks nearby. Politically, Bogtown belongs to the Duchy of Aerik , but Aerik is best understood as a soft-bordered frontier duchy rather than a tightly administered feudal territory. Its core is associated with the Barrowmoor–Helix region, while Bogtown lies toward the duchy's northern fringe. That means ducal authority in Bogtown is real but thin: taxes, proclamations, and occasional patrols reach it, while everyday order depends much more heavily on local personalities, armed townsfolk, merchants, innkeepers, and whoever has enough influence to make rules stick. The settlement therefore occupies a useful campaign niche: Bogtown is where civilization starts becoming negotiable . A traveler coming from Helix or another settled community can still buy food, hire a guide, hear rumors, find lodging, and perhaps appeal to some nominal authority. Beyond Bogtown, those assurances become progressively weaker. Its character also makes it an excellent information hub. Stories coming into Bogtown concern: missing hunters or caravans along the Darkwood trails, strange things emerging from the Blackened Forest, dwarven activity in the northern Moon Peaks, movements observed from Westkeep's watchtower, smugglers and fugitives using the marsh country, old ruins or barrows exposed after flooding, and travelers who entered the western wilderness but never returned. It's a muddy, timber-built, smoky, damp, and defensive rather than picturesque town—boardwalks over the worst ground, buildings raised slightly above the muck, tethering posts crowded with pack animals, and locals who pay close attention whenever strangers arrive. Helix feels like an adventuring settlement adjacent to danger, while Bogtown feels like a settlement that danger has already partially swallowed .

pages.title: Branderscar Prison
pages.content: Branderscar is prison built into the base of the easternmost mountain in the Fangorran Range north of Rosen. where the mountain meets the western edge of Lake Illitar.

pages.title: Brookhollow
pages.content: A village in the southeast quadrant of the Southern Reaches that sits in a valley nestled in the shadow of Mount Dragonspire.

pages.title: Camp Eastscarp
pages.content: A beastmen encampment in Darkforest.

pages.title: Caverns of Achaia
pages.content: Lost for generations. If the PCs can find this location, and choose to explore it, we'll use this map. Back to Maps & Travel Index? cavernsAchaia-opt.png

pages.title: Ched Nasad
pages.content: A Drow city some twenty-six miles southwest of Menzoberranzan and a few hundred feet deeper in the Middledark, separated from Menzoberranzan by a portion of Araumycos.

pages.title: Citadel Silver
pages.content: A dwarven stronghold held in readiness by Regent Baraguld Crumwich, for the dwarven king, Xavamros Battlebeard II. The stronghold lies southeast of Eastdale and is situated in the western Spine Mountains. Dhardofhell , better known as Citadel Silver yet sometimes referred to by (mostly) dwarves as Silverhame (population: 2,154), is a dwarven enclave eighty-five miles southeast of Slaytonthorpe and thirty-three miles northeast of the village of Helix. In 27 PR, it's leader, King Crumwich Ironfist, financially backed an expedition led by Xavamros Battlebeard I, who'd discovered Underdark tunnels beneath Tornspire Keep in Slaytonthorpe. This led to the Xavamros' reclamation of the Gauntwood Galleries, an ancient complex of deep caverns that dwarves mysteriously abandoned centuries earlier. Citadel Silver's leadership is embodied in a hereditary kingship. Industry and Trade: Mining (Iron, Silver, Gold), Metal working, Weapon and Armor Smithing. The dwarves of Citadel Silver trade almost exclusively with Eastdale and their raw materials and finished goods filter across the rest of the region from that point. The dwarves and men of the region maintain strong relations for trade and defense. The regent's sons Grimshaw, Pelk, and Zingren directed and protected caravans from the citadel to other points in the Northern Reaches, but on June 3rd 404 PR, Pelk and Zingren, as well as all hired guards, were slain in a flind-led gnoll ambush that struck the caravan at approximately the halfway point between Kirkilston and Raven's Pass. Only Grimshaw Crumwich and Billworth Turgen survived. Since then, no fewer than a dozen able-bodied travelers accompany the caravan. Thurgan Newl is usually present, unless he's off hunting, exploring, or doing reconnaissance.

pages.title: Coalscuttle
pages.content: A mining camp of 200-225 workers (at any given time) working to harvest coal from the Coal Hills.

pages.title: Cranstonthorpe
pages.content: A thorpe of 288 souls situated in low hills northwest of Smokeshadow. It's primary export is silver from a nearby mine, though several farmers do bring produce to markets in Padoar and Silent Diamond during the growing season.

pages.title: Darkforest
pages.content: Darkwood Forest ” A dense forest known for its rough terrain rich in timber, stone and charcoal. It is rumored that trolls roam the forest. The Darkwood Forest (often shortened to 'Darkforest') is known for its density of vegetation and roughness of terrain. The forest consists of a tall canopy of oaks, beech, and birch trees that nearly blocks out the sun. The terrain is difficult to penetrate due to rolling hills and escarpment ridges. Located between these spaces are small dangerous bogs. The rugged and densely-wooded nature of the terrain limits agriculture but the forest is rich in timber, stone, and charcoal (the latter serves as a fuel source). The forest is also abundant in game (deer and moose, in particular). The villages of Eastdale, Kirkilston, and Westkeep, as well as the dwarven holdfast of Silverhame, all benefit from their proximity to the Darkwood Forest. The largely human towns also tend cattle, goats, and sheep in the shadows of the wood. A treacherous caravan route cross-sects the forest from Eastdale to Westkeep. Merchants pay double wages to men-at-arms who run "The Gauntlet" through the Darkwood Forest. Most refuse to take that route, as they fear the trolls and other monsters that ambush caravans. The local folk believe that mischievous sprites, fairies, and will-o-the-wisps live in the wood. There are also stories of an ancient giant's tomb, and other magical oddities, hidden somewhere in this forest. A tribe of beastmen lives in the depths of this forest, at a location known as Camp Eastscarp.

pages.title: Deep Chaymyn
pages.content: The deepest known dwarven hold, located almost a dozen miles beneath Seven Cities, in the very bowels of the Middledark. Deep Chaymyn is sealed off from the rest of the Underdark by massive bulkheads forged by its inhabitants, and by powerful wards. It is rumored that its inhabitants never venture outside their city, that they have ample food and water supplied naturally, and that none of the inhabitants of the hold have perished in more than three hundred years.

pages.title: Dinling Stream
pages.content: A brook that runs northeast to southwest and cuts across the northern portion of the MacMan Farm, one of the plantations that lies between Kirkilston and Raven's Pass. In a field of that farm, near the stream, a teen-aged NPCs/Borca Sintarn found a Throiki artifact in 396 PR.

pages.title: Dolecherry
pages.content: A village located twenty-one miles southeast of the origin of the Ash River in the Soot Mountains. Dolecherry is remarkable for its river fisherman and for the very high-grade cherries that they export ” many of which eventually make their way to Tien Lung, destined to be incorporated into some restaurant delicacy or alcoholic beverage. Dolecherry is a dozen miles south of the town of Smokeshadow, and eleven miles west of the village of Silent Diamond in western Middenmark.

pages.title: Doors of Galduhr
pages.content: The fabled entrance to the dwarven kingdom of Gundgathol, lost now for generations. For three decades, Bran Hammerspike (PR 140-219) sought the Doors. He never found them.

pages.title: Duchy of Aerik
pages.content: An area in southeastern Stigrix that extends from the Greenlands in the south to just north of the re-built ruins of Ironguard Motte in the north, and from the Isenduin River in the east to the River Merisc to the west. This duchy lies to the west of Middenmark.

pages.title: Eastdale
pages.content: eastdale.png open the image in another browser tab for a larger image Eastdale ” Population: 2,057 Alignment: Lawful Good and Lawful Neutral Demographics: Primarily humans with a smattering of halflings, elves, and dwarves. Political Structure: Ecclesiastical law (St. Ygg); His Venerable Mercy and Prelate of Middenmark, Mordicar Justhand (Human Cleric) Industry and Trade: Trade and Financial Center, Lumber, Charcoal, Livestock (Cattle, Pigs, Sheep), Agriculture (Corn) The Saucy Tart Town Annex (seat of govt.) Ridyard Kupling's blacksmith shop The Red Temple of Ygg Dome of Knowledge (church venerating both Oghma and Arcantryl Sawbones Charlie (town chirugeon) Hudson's Grey Company (Mercenary Guild) Home of Mordicar Justhand Covered well house Arford's Mill Marketplace Warehousing and mercenary hiring Office for militia sergeants Eastdale is located on the eastern tip of the Darkforest. Eastdale is a stockade-surrounded town, it's double gates flanked by two stone towers with wooden roofed observation posts above each. Each tower is emblazoned with the symbol of St. Ygg - a large red cross. The town consists primarily of humans and dwarves from Citadel Silver. There is a smattering of elves, half elves, and halflings. The dwarves of Citadel Silver trade almost exclusively with Eastdale and their raw materials and finished goods filter across the rest of the region from that point. The dwarves and men of the region maintain strong relations for trade and defense. The local men o dale as they are called, are hardy folk drawn from the nomadic tribes that migrated across the Northern Reaches long ago. The church of St. Ygg holds political and administrative control of the town, though ostensibly the heads of the merchant guilds form a ruling council that controls the town. The clerics both lead and employ men-at-arms to defend the town's wooden palisade. They also serve as civil and religious authorities. Eastdale is not only an economic hub of human/dwarven trade, but also a religious center ” providing everything from the training of new adepts to barracking a small company of Red Bannermen, St. Ygg's order of sacred paladins. Due to ecclesiastical law, Eastdale has a reputation as a stern and somber place.

pages.title: Erelhei-Cinlu
pages.content: One of the most infamous cities of the Underdark, located in the subterranean cavern known as the Vault of the Drow.

pages.title: Fangorran Range
pages.content: A narrow range of mountains marching in an almost perfectly straight line, emerging from the Rauth Desert and across the Martel Plains, to its endpoint at the western edge of Lake Illitar.

pages.title: Far Reach
pages.content: The original home of Dwarves and originator of the Eight Great Dwarf Holds in the roll of centuries which followed. Those eight are (1) Kharaz-Ankor, (2) Khalidheroneth, (3) Gundgathol, (4) Citadel Silver, (5) Golbrandur, (6) Forge, (7) the Deep Chaymyn, and (8) Altgrimmr. Note: The Gauntwood Galleries, though a few centuries old, are not among the very first dwarf holds.

pages.title: Far Realm
pages.content: A plane of madness situated very far from the planes of the standard cosmology. This maddening realm is feared for its power to twist unfortunate visitors into gruesome Monsters, and it is from here that aberrations come.

pages.title: Farground
pages.content: padoar-dolecherry-moonwall.webp open the image in another tab for a larger view

pages.title: Farrod's Lake
pages.content: A lake whose center lies sixteen miles east-northeast of Rosen and thirty miles north-northeast of Helix.

pages.title: Forge
pages.content: Second oldest dwarven hold in the Reaches, after Khalidheroneth, Forge lies in the southern tip of The Black Peaks, twenty-five miles east (and slightly south) of Raven's Pass. Currently ruled by Prince Xavamros Battlebeard III on behalf of his father, who reigns in the Gauntwood Galleries.

pages.title: Forgehome
pages.content: The City of Mines, home to a large community of dwarves who make their living underground. Forgehome is believed to hold about 8,000 dwarves. It is located in the Shallows, approximately 1.5 miles beneath and some dozen miles southwest of Citadel Silver. The inhabitants of both locations are on friendly terms. Forgehome supplies much smelted ore to the citadel dwarves, who in turn produce masterwork items with it and ensure that their kin in Forgehome receive a portion of the profits. Forgehome is a common waypoint for dwarven travel between the Citadel Silver and Deep Chaymyn.

pages.title: Garen's Way
pages.content: Garen's Way is a smaller halfling settlement nestled into the surrounding hills. The 200 plus residents here mostly herd sheep for their wool and grow vegetables and such to eat and sell or trade with. The Gauntlet Tavern has the finest mutton and venison in the region. The local chapel is run by Sharvon Underdew , Yondalla, though the halflings have a small shrine to each of the gods in the chapel. garens-way.webp

pages.title: Gauntwood Galleries
pages.content: A long-lost dwarven enclave deep beneath the Gauntwood forest in Slaytonthorpe. These caverns were discovered in 27 PR by Xavamros Battlebeard I, and reclaimed and resettled over the next thirty years.

pages.title: Glickstonehome
pages.content: Glickstonehome is a rock gnome warren in the hills in the Blanryde Hills just to the west of the Eelhold with a gnome population of 620 souls. There are 8 clans that share the warrens, with two of the clans specializing in mining the vast emerald deposits in this section of the hills. The others have their own specialties including lapidaries and 'white' smiths, working gold silver, and tin that they trade emeralds for the metal from the dwarves of the mountains and the mines to their east. The Larganetind Clan is a mining clan of 47 souls that mine in the mine on the south side of the warrens. The vein they mine is a fairly rich one that yields emeralds of up to 3 to 4 carats in great numbers, plus a few smaller and larger ones in smaller numbers. Vorlin Larganetind is the patriarch of this clan, a gnome in his early 270th winter. Glickstonehome.webp The Whistlerest Clan is a clan of lapidaries that are among the best gem cutters around the region. They will cut any gem brought to them, by whoever for a small fee, but specialize in their emeralds for sale and for fine jewelry from the silver and gold smiths of the 'white' smith clans, who also work tin and steel into usable items for households and for sale to others. The clan has 62 members and are led by Rasbar Whistlerest a gnome of 252 winters. Umner Picklepackle is the patriarch of the Picklepackle Clan . He is a gnome of 282 winters and his clan mines the northern mines of the warrens. Their vein is rich in a vast quantity of smaller emeralds of from 1/4 to 2 carats. This mine pulls out about 40% more stones than the southen mines, but mostly of the smaller sizes. There are 67 gnomes in this clan. Zanimyn Nemblelemble is the matriarch of the Nemblelemble Clan , which is the largest clan in the warrens of Glickstonehome with 104 gnomes residing in their warrens. This clan runs smelters and forges that work ore into gold, silver and tin and smith fine rings and other jewelry as well as wares for tables and plates, cups and such for the town and for trade. Zanimyn is the mayor of the town under the hills, and is aged 221. Eilikasys Wibbloborick is the patriarch of the Wibbloborick Clan , a clan of 82 farmers and herders and weavers that grow food for the warrens both on the surface, and mushrooms and other edible fungi in underground farms as well. They herd sheep and goats and grow vegetables and grain in their fields and pastures and are also weavers of wool and goat hair to clothe the gnomes in bright colored cloth. Eilikasys is 290 winters old and is a very powerful Illusionist as well. Vordon Longnose of the Wibbloborick clan is the town miller. Jelbys Flickerdiggles is the matriarch of the Flickerdiggles Clan . This clan is a clan of warriors and foresters that mostly protect the warrens from outside threats. The 73 members of this clan are good with their magic as well as their bows, shortswords and slings. They run patrols within 5 miles of the warrens to protect them and their fields and pastures from brigands and beasts alike. Jelbys is a young gnome of just 165 winters with a daughter, Mayvvis , that she is grooming to follow in her footsteps in time. Dorpip Fizzlefeast is the patriarch of the Fizzlefeast Clan . This clan runs the entertainment establishments, the temples, and the gaol for the town. The 178 year old Dorpip is the sheriff of the settlement and his brother Wardri is the judge of the courts. Lorrykka Fizzlefeast is the priestess that attends to the Temple of the Gods in Glickstonehome. The clan has 96 members, all performing some service or working in the service industry in the town. Waryur Fappletwist is the patriarch of the Fappletwist Clan . This clan includes 89 members that are mainly masons and carpenters building homes and furniture in the warrens for the clans. They also work as labor with the other clans and apprentice in the industries of the town. Warvur is an old gnome of 365 winters, very old for a gnome indeed. His late wife and he had 5 children and 3 cousins included in their original clan. The clans intermarry, trying to keep the bloodlines far enough apart to discourage inbreeding as well as intermarry with gnomes of other clans in the hills to inject new blood throughout the hills to diversify the pool. They are known to hire workers of the halfling, dwarven and human races and the occasional good goblin as employees to fill out the needs in the fields and warrens and for some of the heavier labor that they aren't always able to perform. At any one time there are generally another 100 to 150 folks living in a small village on the surface with their own inns and such for the populace and travelers. Dorryan Wibbloborick , eldest son of Eilikasys runs the Glickstonehome Inn that employs a halfling chef, Zenemin Elderdew , whose cooking is renowned throughout the hills.

pages.title: Glittering Canopy
pages.content: The Glittering Canopy is a tree-top city of elves some 800 miles north of Kirkilston. Unfortunately, the city is abandoned. Nobody knows why, or perhaps those who do know aren't talking.

pages.title: Golbrandur
pages.content: An ancient subterranean dwarven city-fortress east of Slaytonthorpe that Xav II's III's brother, Elbramoth Battlebeard, is waging a drawn-out campaign (198 PR to the present) to repossess. Efforts have so far been largely stymied by a dracolich and dragon cultists, who are firmly entrenched therein.

pages.title: Gosterwick
pages.content: Gosterwick (referred to a Vertucaster by imperials) is the essential "home base" where most adventuring parties lick their wounds and spend their hard-earned gold during downtime between delvings into Arden Vul. The Logothetes of Gosterwick These officials were personally selected by Lady Alexia. They are often viewed with a mix of respect and fear because they report directly to the Azure Keep. Valerius Scaurus (Logothete of Trade): Role: He manages the town's economy, taxes, and the influx of artifacts coming out of Arden Vul. The Vibe: He is a shrewd businessman who doesn't care much for "adventuring glory"”he cares about the 10% tax on all treasure recovered from the Halls. Domitius Afer (Logothete of Public Works): Role: Responsible for the rapid construction and infrastructure of Gosterwick. The Vibe: A man under immense pressure. Hes the one who has to make sure the walls are reinforced and the roads can handle the massive merchant caravans. Theodora Komnene (Logothete of Records): Role: She manages the towns archives and the registry of "Wardens." The Vibe: If you want to become an official Warden of Vetucaster, you have to go through her. She is famously detail-oriented and likely knows more about your party's background than youd prefer. The Knights of the Azure Shield These aren't just your average town guards; they are an elite military order dedicated to the Green Lady. The Commander: Sept Commander Horatius Gesellion. He is a veteran warrior who commands about 60-70 knights stationed at the Azure Keep. Their Jurisdiction: They generally don't patrol the streets for petty crimes (that's for the town watch); instead, they deal with high-level threats, dungeon-delver riots, or external attacks. Equipment: They are recognizable by their polished plate mail and bright blue shields emblazoned with a golden sun. Rumor: The Green Ladys Secret "Logothete" There are whispers in the back corners of the Yellow Cloak that Lady Alexia has a fourth Logothete whose name isn't on any official ledger. This individual supposedly handles "special acquisitions"”meaning they hire adventurers to go into Arden Vul to retrieve specific items that Alexia wants for her private collection. In Gosterwick, justice is a tiered system based on the Archontean legal code. While the Thesmothete Eusebia Phokas handles day-to-day civil and criminal disputes, the Green Lady (Lady Alexia Basileon) reserves "High Justice" for herself. If you are a Warden or a prominent figure, you do not want to end up in her court. Here is how the punishments break down: High Justice (The Green Ladys Jurisdiction) This is reserved for treason, murder, arson, or any crime against the state”which includes breaking a Wardens oath. The Sentence: Fines followed by death. The "Inventive" Part: Lady Alexia is notorious for making executions "public and slow." Rumors suggest she uses magical or alchemical means to prolong the process, ensuring the condemned serves as a visceral warning to the rest of the town. For a Warden who betrays her, this is often viewed as a "breach of contract" that requires an "equalizing" of the debt through suffering. Justice of the Body (Thesmothete's Jurisdiction) Handled by Eusebia Phokas, this covers assault, slander, and wounding between citizens. The Sentence: Punishments vary based on the severity of the harm but frequently involve amputation (losing the offending hand) or heavy fines. If the crime is severe enough to border on High Justice, the death penalty is on the table. Justice of the Domus (Property Crimes) Handled by the proedroi (Eusebias assistants), this deals with theft, burglary, and inheritance disputes. The Sentence: This is where the punishments get particularly Archontean. Depending on the value stolen (usually over 50 gp), you can expect: Fines: Often triple the value of the stolen goods. Mutilation: Specifically blinding (for peeping or spying) or castration (for certain domestic crimes). Amputation: Standard for repeat thieves. Low Justice (The "Commoner" Courts) Handled by the chartoularii (clerks) in the public square, this is for petty crimes and disputes involving non-citizens (non-Wardens). The Sentence: Usually swift and summary. Expect time in the stocks, a public flogging, or immediate expulsion from the town. For non-citizens, the law is far less patient; if you can't pay a fine, you might find yourself "recruited" for dangerous labor details. In Gosterwick, the specific official you need to see for real estate depends on whether you are looking for the right to buy land or the actual purchase and registry of that land. As a Warden of Vetucaster, you should focus on these two officials: Aedelwine the Fair (Logothete of the Private House) While other logothetes handle trade and public works, Aedelwine is the official responsible for the Private House. The Role: In Archontean bureaucracy, the Private House traditionally manages the properties and estates of the imperial family (or in this case, Lady Alexia). The Function: If you are looking to purchase land or a house, Aedelwine is the one who handles the administration of these holdings. He ensures the property is vacant, legally cleared for sale, and that the transaction aligns with the Green Ladys interests. Theodora Komnene (Logothete of Records) You cannot close a deal without her involvement. The Role: She maintains the town's official archives. The Function: Once Aedelwine has brokered the sale, Theodora registers the deed. More importantly, she verifies that you are a Warden in good standing. Without her "stamp of approval" on your citizenship status, the sale cannot be finalized. Key Financial Tip: The Wardens Discount Don't forget that one of the primary perks of being a Warden of Vetucaster is a massive 50% discount on the purchase of land within the town walls. Standard Price: Real estate in a boomtown like Gosterwick is incredibly expensive due to high demand from merchants and adventurers. Warden Price: Lady Alexia uses this discount to ensure the "elite" of the town (the adventurers she can call upon in a crisis) are the ones who actually own the physical buildings, keeping the towns defense in capable hands. Where to find them? Both officials operate out of their respective offices near the Thesmothete's Townhouse, located in the more affluent northern section of Gosterwick, moving toward the Azure Keep. A small town (2,211 persons) lying close to the cliff of Arden Vul and under the shadow of the Azure Keep. Lady Alexia Basileon has sponsored this new town in an effort to oppose her half-brother, Lord Burdock. Although small, it is consciously organized to appeal to adventurers, who can pursue training, buy supplies, and dispose of their loot in the town. Due to its size, however, it cannot fully compete with Newmarket for such services.

pages.title: Greenlands
pages.content: A vast swath of arable farmland on which relatively few trees grow. Sages are unable to explain why no forest has grown in the Greenlands in the past three centuries of men's history in the area ” despite the fact that no efforts have been made to prevent forest growth, and that crops grow just fine if planted there. The governor of Threshold and the Prelate of Middenmark cooperate to keep a garrison stationed in the Greenlands, for this large area produces much grain and vegetables for the populations in the Northern Reaches.

pages.title: Guardians' Rest
pages.content: The Guardians' Rest is a fortified caravan station located strategically at the halfway point along the road running from Kirkilston to Eastdale. The compound consists of a large, enclosed area with reinforced wooden walls and watchtowers at each corner. At its center lies a spacious courtyard, surrounded by various facilities designed to cater to the needs of caravans and travelers. This fortified rest-stop and resupply depot is administrated by Father Zistrus, a sixth level cleric of Imperiosa. Mordicar Justhand is displeased at not having his own pick of administrator, but he hasn't pushed the issue ... yet.

pages.title: Gundgathol
pages.content: A vast and sprawling dwarven kingdom beneath the Moon Peaks fifty miles southwest of Slaytonthorpe and approximately forty-five miles south-southeast of the village of Helix, lost centuries ago to a Duergar and Derro incursion.

pages.title: Hamelet
pages.content: When the surviving dwarves of Gundgathol fled to the surface almost three millennia ago, they were befriended by local humans. Jointly, the two races established the town of Hamelet, which became well-known for its citizen militia, it's cyclopean component, and the extremely high quality metal goods its smiths produced. Eventually, Hamelet grew into the city Threshold.

pages.title: Helix
pages.content: A village of some five-hundred souls that lies along the northern boundary of the Duchy of Aerik. Helix' claim to fame is that it is the chosen site for the headquarters of the Chapterhouse of the Seekers. helix-colored.webp Population: 632 Demographics: primarily human with a few dwarves, elves, half-elves, and halflings. Political Structure: (Noble Family—Hereditary) Krothos Ironguard (Level 3 Fighter) Industry and Trade: Dried Peat, Livestock (goats), Agriculture (subsistence) Imports: wine, ale, fine clothing, armour, food stuffs (corn and wheat), metal ingots Village Square & Marketplace Turgen's Trade Goods The Axe & Anvil Mercenary Guild The Silver Standard Merchant Caravan Company Shrine of St. Ygg The Rosy Quartz Jeweler and Money Lender The Brazen Strumpet (Tavern & Inn) The Foul Pheasant Wizard's Spire Bowyer/Fletcher Hendon's Mill Barrowmaze Statue of Herne Ancient Ruins Ironguard Motte

pages.title: Horgrim Tunnels
pages.content: Ancient tunnels beneath the Darkforest. It's believed they were carved ages ago by an underground river, a river no longer present. Perhaps it was diverted or eventually dried up. It is rumored that these tunnels lead to various points in the Underdark ” to deep beneath Citadel Silver, to a crumbling ruins in The Forbidden Zone, and northward to tunnels lying beneath Slaytonthorpe.

pages.title: Hoskighee
pages.content: A town of some 400 souls nestled in the foothills of the Moon Peaks. This town exports coal and limestone quarried in the hills. It maintains trade relations with Wyrdwood, Helix, Bogtown, and Ironguard Motte.

pages.title: Icepeak Mountains
pages.content: A range of mountains north of the Blackened Forest and northwest of Rosen. The Keep on the Borderlands sits in the foothills of one of these mountains.

pages.title: Inkwell
pages.content: A village which lies a league or two to the west of Lindendale, Inkwell is a community of 98 halflings settled into barrows in a ridge line. There is no true 'mayor', though Quinlan Teabarrel , the richest man in the thorp seems to run things here. inkwell.webp]

pages.title: Ironguard Motte
pages.content: The seat of power in the Duchy of Aerik. Population roughly 700 souls. Ironguard Motte is the major trade and political center of the district. It's ruling family received this vassal holding from Duke Derric Winterberry of Threshold in PR (-)06.

pages.title: Isenduin
pages.content: The river separating the Duchy of Aerik from the Middenmark.

pages.title: Isenton
pages.content: A town of 3,000 located eighteen miles southwest of Westkeep and thirty-three miles south and a bit west of Phandalin. The town's chief exports are tobacco, corn, and whiskey.

pages.title: Kesloril's Scarp
pages.content: A high, craggy hill near the center of Darkforest from which Donally Brook descends, flowing south to Donally Lake ” which is bordered by forest along the majority of its twenty-six miles of shoreline.

pages.title: Khalidheroneth
pages.content: The northernmost dwarven outpost located in the Spine of the World Mountains beyond even the Salt Marches and Threshold, some hundred miles north of Slaytonthorpe. Ruled by King Grongan Drakeslayer, this enclave of mountain dwarves is the largest known single dwarven domicile at over 6,000 beards. Khalidheroneth is on cordial terms with the other dwarven outposts and exports platinum, marble, gems, mead, metal goods, and labor while importing grain, meat, textiles, and papyrus. Note: The belief that the dwarves of Khalidheroneth pre-dated the dwarves of the The Spine is a cultural claim within the Khalidheroneth community. It is not supported by archaeological evidence found in the Spine region and is considered a myth by historians and sages of the Northern Reaches.

pages.title: Kharaz-Ankor
pages.content: An ancient, lost dwarven stronghold; it's entrance may be beneath the Keep on the Borderlands. Some say this was the very first dwarven stronghold; others, that this distinction belongs to Gundgathol, or to Khalidheroneth.

pages.title: Kirkilston
pages.content: settlement kirkilston-hamlet.webp Kirkilston (Hamlet, sometimes alternately spelled Kirkliston ) Founded: October 23, 107 PR Population: 362 Alignment: Lawful Neutral Demographics: Human, approximately 50 elves, half-elves, and halflings Political Structure: Ecclesiastical Law (St. Ygg); Petre of St. Ygg (Human Cleric) Industry and Trade: Primarily Livestock (Sheep) and Agriculture (Corn), Mead, Lumber. Kirkilston is named after the church, or kirk, at its center. The church, alongside the Red Temple in Eastdale and the Watchtower in Westkeep, provide the three key centers of faith, administration, and governance in The Prelacy of Middenmark. However, unlike the more puritanical stance of the clerics in Eastdale, The Red Laws are more relaxed in Kirkilston and the immediate surrounding area. Governed under Ecclesiastical Law of St. Ygg, Kirkilston is led by Petre, a seasoned Priest. The church is the centerpiece of the hamlet and, alongside the Red Temple in Eastdale and the Watchtower in Westkeep, forms a triad of religious and administrative authority in The Prelacy of Middenmark. The implementation of the Red Laws in Kirkilston is notably more lenient, reflecting the hamlet's more relaxed and less rigid approach to religious doctrine. The hamlet's economy revolves around livestock, primarily sheep, and agriculture, with corn being the chief crop. Additionally, the production of mead and lumber contributes significantly to its local economy and trade. Being a key stop on the caravan route, Kirkliston also benefits from trade and interactions with travelers and merchants. Lacking a formal wall or significant defensive structures, the hamlet relies on a small group of brave, albeit untrained, men known as the Hamlet Watch. They are responsible for safeguarding the community against threats, particularly from the forces of chaos emerging from the nearby wilds. Their bravery is a testament to the rugged and resilient spirit of Kirkliston's inhabitants. Daily life in Kirkliston is marked by a hardworking ethos, with most residents engaged in farming, shepherding, or local trades. The hamlet has a few essential amenities like a blacksmith, a tavern, and a small market area. Social life often revolves around the church and communal gatherings, with festivals and fairs being focal points of celebration and social cohesion. Living in the shadow of the Blackpeak Mountains and the Darkforest, the people of Kirkliston are no strangers to hardship and the dangers posed by the wilderness. Their resilience, however, presents opportunities for adventurers and travelers, be it aiding in defense, exploring the nearby wilds, or engaging in the hamlet's modest but vital trade activities.

pages.title: Lake Donally
pages.content: This lake is also known as Doneldun's Den, so named for the massive Dragon Turtle that is said to live in its depths. The last verified sighting of Doneldun was in 368 PR, when the Demetran druidess Halathra Moonbeam, along with a ranger ally whose name is lost to history, held palaver with the dragon turtle. The details of their conversation and how it was achieved is unknown, but a scroll positively linked to the druidess definitely describes a conversation with the behemoth. From AR 698 to PR 392, elves inhabited Aelith-Calaer, the city that partially encircled Lake Donally.

pages.title: Lake Illitar
pages.content: A freshwater lake located at the northern tip of the Fangorran Range, watched over by a swanmay ranger. The prison, Branderscar, is built into the base of the mountain that abuts that lake. This lake is located about fifty-four miles northwest of Threshold and about fifty miles northeast of Rosen.

pages.title: Lindendale
pages.content: Lindendale is the largest of three halfling villages in the hills, named after a beautiful copse of linden trees in the center and around the town. The mayor of Lindendale is Fatty Grasshare , a rotund halfling of 105 years, and the town has about 680 other halfling residents in the and around it's environs as well. Oribul Reedwhistle is the proprietor of the mill shown below. He runs it with his wife Mirabelle and his son and daughter, Daryon and Eliwyth respectively. Lalan Summerbranch is the sheriff and law of the town and area around it. He has a human deputy named Vurth Twohide . Lindendale is mostly a farming community that raises crops to eat and share as well as dairy cows and sheep for their milk and wool. The baked goods of Isaris Fastwillow , the lady that runs the Lindendale Bakery, is famous for her pies, pastries and bread. Folks come for many miles to eat her goods, which are also sold in the inn, The Dewdrop Inn . Lindendale.webp

pages.title: Lower Dark
pages.content: areas of the Underdark more than thirteen miles beneath the surface world are said to lie in the Lowerdark.

pages.title: Menzoberranzan
pages.content: The City of Spiders, a drow city located some two miles below the surface and about fifty miles southwest of Citadel Silver, in the cavern Araurilcaurak, a massive cavern some three miles by two, and one-thousand feet in height in most places. Menzoberranzan is situated in the upper Middledark, about forty-five miles east of Blingdenstone. Menzoberranzan is a Drow city some twenty-six miles northwest of Ched Nasad, and not quite as deep in the Underdark as its sister city. menzo.webp

pages.title: Middenmark
pages.content: Once a lawless frontier, Middenmark has been ceded to the church of St. Ygg, who have established law and order through force of arms and the implementation of the Red Laws, a strict moral code that the Middenmarkers are starting to resist. Middenmark is a theocratic vassal to the ruler of Threshold. Middenmark is ruled by His Venerable Mercy, Prelate Mordicar Justhand, a cleric of St. Ygg. The priests of St. Ygg established their political and administrative center at the Red Temple in Eastdale, as well as sending priests and building small shrines in the villages of Kirkilston, Westkeep, and Raven's Pass. Middenmark lies several miles southeast of Slaytonthorpe. The Middenmark lies to the east of the Duchy of Aerik. Middenmark is bounded at its northwest corner by the city of Threshold, on the west by the Isenduin, and in its southeastern corner by the The Spine, and by Westkeep in the southwest.

pages.title: Middledark
pages.content: Areas in the Underdark which lie at depths below the surface of more than three miles but less than thirteen are said to be in the Middledark.

pages.title: Misty Mire
pages.content: A fen in Slaytonthorpe that is ruled by the green dragon, Inzeldrin.

pages.title: Moon Peaks
pages.content: A mountain range in southeastern Locations/Stigrix, home to the second oldest dwarf hold, Gundgathol ” in the hands of duergar, derro, and kuo-toa in recent decades.

pages.title: Mordoom Keep
pages.content: A ruined citadel in The Prelacy of Middenmark. It was once a prosperous, vibrant stronghold or citadel, but it is now abandoned because of its closeness to the Forbidden Zone and, more importantly, because it has become the apparent origin point of the Soul Fungus outbreak. The keep is now described as being tainted by an unnatural fungal infection that can transform living creatures into mindless fungal zombies or Plaguewalkers. The infection is associated with eerie purple-glowing eyes, soul-like wisps trapped in luminescent green mold, and the belief that exposure through the eyes may transmit the corruption: the eyes are the window to the soul. The site is officially off-limits by order of the Church of St. Ygg, and a secretive group called the Sporebane Brotherhood appears to be working against the fungal scourge. They are said to possess protective magic and some healing ability during the infection's incubation period, though after incubation there is reportedly no cure. The Sporebane Brotherhood is made up of druidic healers, rangers, and arcane scholars. Their hidden base is the Sporebane Sanctuary, and their leader is Eldreth, the Moss-Walker. Elowen Starshadow is one of their wizards/researchers. Known approaches include the main gate , a postern gate reached by a dangerous narrow path near the cliff face, and a sewer pipe in the cliff face leading into sewers and caverns beneath the keep.

pages.title: Northern Reaches
pages.content: Are you a Dungeon Master interested in the regional Northern Reaches overview map? You can download a Paint.net PDN file here that contains all the various layers of map information. Back to Maps & Travel Index? The newest area of population within the Northern Region is the Farground Expanse, having been settled only about 500 years. Refers to the region at its southern edge as the Greenlands.. The map of this region is 44 x 36 hexes, each hex five miles on a side: northernreaches.webp

pages.title: Pado Brook
pages.content: A tributary of the Ash River that tracks northeast from Padoar to the river just south of Wizard's Tower.

pages.title: Padoar
pages.content: A village thirty-six miles south-southeast from Ironguard Motte, eight miles southwest of Dolecherry, and thirteen miles southeast of the southernmost of the Soot Mountains. As the crow flies, Helix lies forty-three miles northwest of Padoar.

pages.title: Pellon Field
pages.content: A large field just south of Helix. Beneath several feet of soil lies an ancient Walmart parking lot from the Most Ancient of Times.

pages.title: Phandalin
pages.content: A small town of about two hundred people, Phandalin is still considered a frontier town. It is built on the ruins of a much older settlement that was contemporaneous with the ancient, now lost Netheril Empire. Breldik Blackbeard and Barclay Festerton were notable residents in the early decades of the PR 200s.

pages.title: Phultarr's Pool
pages.content: A lake in the south of the Rauth Desert. Though called a 'pool', the lake is almost six miles across at its widest point. Nobody can explain the freshwater lake's presence in this desert, and none still living can remember a time when the lake wasn't there. Some call it Demetra's Tears, others term in Oaxus' Blood.

pages.title: Principality of Brine
pages.content: The Principality of Brine occupies the colder northwestern frontier region, beyond or west of Threshold, bordering areas like the Fargone Forest and the northern wilderness.

pages.title: Rauth Desert
pages.content: rauth-desert.webp A vast desert whose eastern extent extends into the western portion of the Northern Reaches. It is inhabited by sand wurms, dervishes, thrikreen, and other creatures. Heat exhaustion and dehydration are ever-present hazards in this environment.

pages.title: Raven's Pass
pages.content: Population: 110 Alignment: Chaotic Neutral Demographics: Human, Elf, and Half-Elf Political Structure: Ecclesiastical Law (St. Ygg) Industry and Trade: Lumber Raven's Pass is a small village on the southern edge of the Red Thicket. The village was established as a layover location for merchant caravans heading to and from Threshold. As such, it is frequented by caravans from Phandalin, Kirkilston, and Eastdale. Over time, it became home to a few hardy souls who support themselves by logging the giant red and white birch trees of the Thicket Wood. The village has no means of defense and is merely a small collection of homesteads, stables, and a tavern called The Mason's Apron. Although there is a statue devoted to St. Ygg in Raven's Pass, only a single young acolyte is stationed in the village. The Red Laws are (at best) loosely observed. Ravens Pass: Settlement Overview Ravens Pass is a small, rugged settlement nestled within a narrow mountain corridor in the Northern Reaches. The town occupies a strategic location along a winding mountain path, serving as both a waypoint for travelers and a hub for local craftsmen and traders. Its population is modest, likely numbering around 500 residents , including families of artisans, traders, and a small contingent of militia tasked with guarding the pass. ravens-pass.webp open image in another tab to see it full size --- Layout and Structures Main Thoroughfare: A rocky, uneven road runs through the center of town, connecting the entrance from the lowland approaches to the deeper mountain paths. Buildings cluster along this route, generally constructed from local stone and timber, giving them a sturdy, functional appearance. Blacksmiths and Craft Shops: The most prominent is The Broken Hilt , a stout stone-and-timber blacksmith with an open forge, stacked firewood, and tools visible from the road. Its proprietor, Samuel Armstrong, is a middle-aged, broad-shouldered craftsman with a stern expression, known for producing high-quality specialty equipment. Other craftsmen include carpenters, leatherworkers, and armorers, all working in practical, workmanlike spaces. Residences: Small, functional homes of stone and wood line side paths and terraces along the mountain slopes. Most have steep roofs to shed snow, small hearths for warmth, and gardens or pens for livestock. Public and Communal Buildings: A modest tavern or inn offers meals and shelter for travelers, often doubling as a meeting place for locals. There may be a watchtower or small guard hall overseeing the pass, hinting at its strategic importance. Storage and Workshops: Barrels, crates, and firewood stacks are common near homes and shops. Open-air work areas and small sheds indicate active trade and production. --- Surroundings and Environment Ravens Pass is defined by its mountainous terrain: Topography: Steep cliffs rise around the settlement, with dense pine forests clinging to the slopes. Fog or mist often drifts through the valley, and narrow trails lead further into the mountains. Climate: The pass experiences cold, wind-swept weather, with frequent rain and snow depending on the season. This has shaped the rugged, practical architecture of the town. Strategic Location: The pass itself is a chokepoint; the towns position allows it to monitor and control access through the mountains, making it important for both trade and defense. --- Atmosphere and Mood Life in Ravens Pass is practical, hard-won, and self-reliant . The settlement has a gritty, frontier-like charm. Its residents are hardy, accustomed to harsh weather and isolation, and value craftsmanship, skill, and resilience. The town exudes a sense of timelessness, as though it has endured generations of travelers, traders, and mountain hardships. Daily Life: Work dominates daily routines”smithing, crafting, trade, maintenance of roads and defenses, and tending small gardens or animals. Markets are small but functional, with goods coming from both the surrounding mountains and lowland trade routes. Safety and Security: Despite its modest militia, the settlement is alert to mountain threats”bandits, wild animals, and unstable weather.

pages.title: Reaches
pages.content: The combined Northern Reaches and Southern Reaches ” an area spanning approximately 60,000 miles 2 ; two-thirds of that area comprises the Northern Reaches.

pages.title: Red Thicket
pages.content: The Red Thicket is unique. The wood consists of gigantic white and red birch trees, the white trees have red leaves throughout the year and the red trees have the reverse. The forest is a distinctly beautiful, and yet sublime and otherworldly feature of the Northern Reaches. These trees live for approximately 600-1000 years. Raven's Pass, a small thorp, is found on the southern edge of the forest. A pass about fifteen miles long extends from Raven's Pass to the Ford-at-the-River-Isenduin. The ford must be crossed to reach Threshold. The first human settlers logged the forest immediately around Threshold. Gnolls and orcs know that the Red Thicket Pass, and the Ford at- the-River-Isenduin, provide excellent points to ambush caravans and waylay merchants seeking to conduct trade. Caravans must be well-armed and there is always work for a strong sword-arm. Giant eagles, giant spotted owls, black bears, owlbears, and other monsters wander the forest. Some say giant treants protect the forest and attack those who cut down the trees. It is thought that wood elves dwell here. The Red Thicket lies east of the Isenduin, in northwestern Middenmark. The Thicket Wood is the portion of the Red Thicket where the trees grow tallest and strongest. The Red Thicket stands out as a unique forest, characterized by its towering giants - both white and red birch trees. The white birches are notable for their year-round crimson foliage, while the red ones maintain their hue throughout the seasons. This uniqueness makes it a distinctly beautiful feature of the Northern Reaches. Raven's Pass is nestled at the southern edge of this enchanting forest, forming a pass approximately fifteen miles long that extends from Raven's Pass to Ford-at-the-River-Isenduin. Crossing this ford is essential for reaching Threshold, where human settlers first began logging immediately surrounding areas. The Red Thicket and its associated ford have become notorious ambush points for caravans and merchants seeking trade routes. Caravans must be well-prepared with robust defenses against potential attacks by gnolls and orcs who exploit these strategic locations. Inhabited by various creatures, the forest is home to giant eagles, spotted owls, black bears, owlbears, and other monstrous beings. Some legends suggest that giant treants may protect this verdant realm from those who would harm its trees. It is also believed that wood elves might reside here. The Red Thicket lies east of Isenduin in the northwestern Middenmark region. The Thicket Wood represents the heart of the forest, where the tallest and strongest birch trees flourish.

pages.title: Rimbling Brook
pages.content: A creek that the road from Kirkilston to Raven's Pass must cross at about four hours' march northwest of Kirkilston. It is sometimes a site selected to ambush caravans while they are midstream and most vulnerable.

pages.title: River Isenduin
pages.content: river-isenduin.webp

pages.title: Rosen
pages.content: A city (population 55,000) three days' march or one day's ride west of Helix, ruled by a Merchant Council.

pages.title: Sammeister
pages.content: A small lake just south of Isenton that is home to a small band of sahuagin. This band, led by 'Sammy', often preys upon caravans that are enroute from Eastdale to Raven's Pass and vice versa. This lake is rather small, taking up less than 0.75 square miles.

pages.title: Seven Cities
pages.content: A clustering of what were once, long ago, seven separate cities. This population center of some 300,000 souls is located about three days' march or two days' easy riding to the northwest of Slaytonthorpe.

pages.title: Shallows
pages.content: The Shallows are the upper portion of the Underdark, sometimes also called the Upperdark .

pages.title: Shallowtown
pages.content: A sizeable cavern, with floor area approximately equal to 1.5 football fields, located in the Shallows beneath the southern edge of Lake Sammeister just outside of Kirkilston.

pages.title: Shrieken Mire
pages.content: A swamp located in Slaytonthorpe that is reputedly home to a very large tribe of blue goblins. A flourishing tribe of Lizardfolk dwells here, under the protection of Inzeldrin the ancient green dragon, whom they worship.

pages.title: Silent Diamond
pages.content: A village in western Middenmark where the dwarf Thoras Goldpanner discovered a fist-sized diamond in PR 46, a find he kept secret until the year of his death in PR 73.

pages.title: Silverhame
pages.content: Dhardofhell , better known as Citadel Silver yet sometimes referred to by (mostly) dwarves as Silverhame (population: 2,154), is a dwarven enclave seventy-five miles southeast of Slaytonthorpe and thirty-three miles northeast of the village of Helix. In 27 Post-Ravaging, it's leader, King Crumwich Ironfist, financially backed an expedition led by Xavamros Battlebeard I, who'd discovered Underdark tunnels beneath Tornspire Keep in Slaytonthorpe. This led to the Xavamros' reclamation of the Gauntwood Galleries, an ancient complex of deep caverns that dwarves mysteriously abandoned centuries earlier. Citadel Silver's leadership is embodied in a hereditary kingship. Industry and Trade: Mining (Iron, Silver, Gold), Metal working, Weapon and Armor Smithing. The dwarves of Citadel Silver trade almost exclusively with Eastdale and their raw materials and finished goods filter across the rest of the region from that point. The dwarves and men of the region maintain strong relations for trade and defense.

pages.title: Sizemordicus
pages.content: A city many miles southeast of Helix. Ruled by a wizard autarch, this city is famous for its fences, cutthroats, and politicians. It has a population of over 100,000 people. The city is surrounded by a stone wall thirty feet high and ten thick, fashioned of cut limestone blocks quarried from the Soot Mountains in the years 06 to 24 PR. The circular Mordician Park at the center of the city is a mile in diameter, featuring numerous trails, various open areas, and considerable old growth forest. It is home to numerous treants and mandrakes.

pages.title: Slaytonthorpe
pages.content: A subregion in the northern quadrant of Southeastern Locations/Stigrix on the northeastern border of the Duchy of Aerik. Slaytonthorpe is famous for its Baron of Mutton inn and tavern. It is said to have the best mutton and beef brisket in the known world. Slaytonthorpe is also famous as the region in which a group of heroes famously recaptured Tornspire Keep in 25 PR. slaytonthorpe.png Slaytonthorpe lies about three days' march or two days' easy riding to the southeast of Seven Cities.

pages.title: Smokeshadow
pages.content: A town that arose in the decade of PR 50 to support trade between the dwarves of Smoketower Mountain and the Soot Mountains. Smokeshadow lies southeast of Cranstonthorpe.

pages.title: Soot Mountains
pages.content: A triad of mountains located roughly fourteen miles south and slightly east of Phandalin, thirteen miles west-southwest of the town of Smokeshadow, and twenty miles north of Sizemordicus.

pages.title: Southern Reaches
pages.content: The region bounded upon its northern edge by the southernmost points of the Northern Reaches. Not far across that border to the north lies the southernmost of the Moon Peaks. At the base of one of these mountains, shrouded in coniferous trees, is a shrine to the mysterious, ancient entity known as Zorgon. The Principality of Brine stretches across the Southern Reaches, ruled over by the Triarchs of Archaia.

pages.title: Spiral Shrine
pages.content: A shrine to St. Ygg in Helix overseen by Brother Othar (Level 5 Cleric) and his under-clerics, Cella (Level 2 Cleric) and Gamdar (Level 2 Half-Orc cleric).

pages.title: Ss'zuraass'nee
pages.content: The City of Abominations, a large yuan-ti city in the Underdark, half a mile under the lizardfolk kingdom of Kalran.

pages.title: Stigrix
pages.content: The southwestern quadrant of the nation of Westmark, once ruled by Stigrix Vandenheim during the Age of Renewal. EastWestStigrix.png

pages.title: The Bauthwaf
pages.content: The term drow use to reference the network of 100 or so tunnels surrounding Menzoberranzan. The Bauthwaf is vigilantly patrolled by drider-riding elite drow.

pages.title: The Black Peaks
pages.content: The Black Peaks are a mountainous range along the western border of the Forbidden Zone. The mountains have numerous named peaks of various sizes and elevations including Mount Yst, the White Mount, The Fang, and Mount Desolate. These range from 9,000 to 12,000 feet high. Sages believe there are at least two passes, likely on either side of the articulation with the Coal Hills, through the mountains to the badlands of The Forbidden Zone. Monstrous humanoids use the passes to raid north of the peaks. There is also at least one Orc stronghold, maybe more, somewhere in the range. Lead, iron, copper, and silver can be found in the mountains but they have not been mined by humans, as of yet.

pages.title: The Coal Hills
pages.content: The Coal Hills extend twenty miles northwest of the The Black Peaks toward Threshold. These Highlands are mined for coal and iron ” key resources for the nearby city. However, there are Goblin tribes that live in the hills closest to the Black Peaks and they occasionally raid the small mining camps set along the northeastern edge of the ridge. The hills are rocky and they possess very little arable land. The hills have game: deer and rabbits in particular. Sheep are also shepherded in the hills immediately adjacent to Threshold.

pages.title: The Forbidden Zone
pages.content: The Forbidden Zone is a major badland region in the Prelacy of Middenmark, tied to the dangerous, frontier character of the Northern Reaches. The public Middenmark material describes it as a central feature of the region: a wasteland created after a cataclysm destroyed an ancient city , leaving behind ruined wealth, dangerous remnants, and a power vacuum where Law and Chaos continue to struggle. In campaign terms, it functions like a haunted scar on the map: not just wilderness, but a place where something civilization-shattering happened. The fact that the region contains partially destroyed bounties to be looted suggests treasure, ruins, old structures, and relics, but also instability and danger. It also appears to affect nearby sites. Mordoom Keep is said to have remained uninhabited partly because of its proximity to the Forbidden Zone, and that same keep is now associated with the Soul Fungus , a supernatural fungal infection that turns victims into fungal undead or Plaguewalkers. The area east of the caravan road is described elsewhere as having chaotic energies that are being monitored by local powers, including the Red Bannermen, because of fears that the chaos could disrupt the natural and magical fabric of the region. It is a post-cataclysmic ruin-field : blasted earth, unstable magic, half-buried towers, broken roads, warped wildlife, sinkholes into ancient vaults, lingering undead, and strange lights at night. It feels different from normal wilderness - less like dangerous woods and more like crossing into a cursed exclusion zone where the rules of nature and magic are damaged.

pages.title: The Gauntwood
pages.content: An area of forest in the vicinity of Slaytonthorpe. Beneath this forest lies the ancient dwarven settlement known as the The Gauntwood Galleries. The Gauntwood is the southerneastern-most portion of the Thornwood. This woods bounds Slaytonthorpe to the northeast, east, and south.

pages.title: The Spine
pages.content: A mountain range that runs from the eastern edge of Darkforest to the northern edge of The Forbidden Zone. It also represents the eastern edge of the Middenmark region. The mountains in the center of The Spine are ice-capped. The range is known to be rich in minerals and gemstones. The dwarves of Citadel Silver (Silverhame) mine iron ore, silver, and gold. Bards still sing songs about the first dwarves and how they built a great kingdom in the mountains. Waves of monstrous humanoids, orcs, goblins, trolls, and giants from the far north, pushed them out and they fled to the southern tip of The Spine. Some say the dwarves even found a single vein of Mithril, the most rare and precious of metals, running through the mountains. The dwarves of Khalidheroneth insist they pre-dated the dwarves of the Spine.

pages.title: Thicket Wood
pages.content: A forest of immense red and white birch trees in the Red Thicket, and the site of much ranger activity, as well as carefully controlled logging.

pages.title: Threshold
pages.content: Population: 25,021 Alignment: Any (predominantly Lawful Neutral) Demographics: Any (Primarily Human) Political Structure: Hereditary Kingship Industry and Trade: Financial, Political, and Trade Threshold is the capital of the Northern Reaches. In PR 386, the city was attacked by a horde of monsters from the The Black Peaks. The army included orcs, goblins, and hill giants who nearly leveled the city and destroyed the stone fortifications. The warriors of Threshold, alongside support from the high clerics and wizards, barely repulsed the army. Currently, only half the city is habitable. The other half was completely destroyed and remains under construction. Threshold developed from its humble beginnings as a hamlet named Hamelet.

pages.title: Thundertree
pages.content: Now a ruins, Thundertree was a thriving village from CY 68 to PR 82, destroyed by the green dragon Inzeldrin. Thundertree's ruins lie atop the deeper ruins of an ancient Netherese community. The ruins of Thundertree lie thirteen miles northeast of Slaytonthorpe and nineteen miles west and a bit south of Threshold.

pages.title: Tien Lung
pages.content: An ancient city far, far away from the Northern Reaches that is a center for trade, political intrigue, and every form of indulgence. In very ancient times, Chinese lived here. Now, millennia later, their descendants, many The Shou, and even legacies of the Visitors dwell here.

pages.title: Undalan
pages.content: The name of the original failed settlement atop which Phandalin is built. Undalan may have been built atop an even older location, the town of Benediction. There are references to it in some old surviving scrolls, which hint that a Tivuld-Gho resided in a cavern beneath Benediction. In PR 203 the band styling themselves the Singing Swords successfully penetrated the ruins of Undalan, but met their end before finding a way downward into Benediction.

pages.title: Underdark
pages.content: The world-spanning subterranean realm that underlies all the surface lands. Some sages believe that the Underdark is bottomless ” or rather, that it eventually impinges upon and then gives way to the Far Realm.

pages.title: Upperdark
pages.content: Those portions of the Underdark that lie between 500 feet and three miles beneath the surface world.

pages.title: Watchtower
pages.content: The Watchtower is a fortified monastery in Westkeep that serves as a means of protection but also a place of study and training for young apprentice clerics and monks. The door to the watchtower is 20 feet above the ground and accessed by a temporary wooden staircase. In the event of an attack the guards retreat to the watchtower and the staircase can be destroyed or burned to ensure their safety. The Red Laws are observed in Westkeep, but not as strictly as Eastdale.

pages.title: Westkeep
pages.content: Westkeep (Village) Population: 649 Alignment: Lawful Neutral Demographics: Human, Elf, Half-Elf, and Halflings Political Structure: Ecclesiastical Law (St. Ygg); Endra of St. Ygg (Human Cleric) Industry and Trade: Horses, Bison, Livestock (cattle, pigs, sheep), Lumber, Charcoal. A village on the far western edge of the Middenmark, Westkeep draws its name from a single watchtower-monastery built by the local populace and the clerics of St. Ygg. The watchtower serves as a means of protection but also a place of study and training for young apprentice clerics and monks. The door to the watchtower is 20 feet above the ground and accessed by a temporary wooden staircase. In the event of an attack the guards retreat to the watchtower and the staircase can be destroyed or burned to ensure their safety. The Red Laws are observed in Westkeep, but not as strictly as Eastdale.

pages.title: Wizard's Tower
pages.content: wizardstower.png A small bucolic community and home and stronghold of the mage Tauste, located in the Farground Expanse about forty miles northeast of Threshold.

pages.title: Yvoth-Lened
pages.content: A drow city some five leagues west of Menzoberranzan and a quarter-mile deeper. It is connected to the better-known city of Erelhei-Cinlu by a subterranean passage described as a long journey. It is a dense, dark metropolis dominated by an enormous temple of Lolth. Great stone bells ring from the temple to announce religious rites, making Lolth’s worship part of the city’s daily rhythm. A crowded bazaar occupies the city center beneath the looming temple. Drow merchants and slave traders bargain and cheat one another amid non-drow captives, servants, and occasional foreign traders. Goods specifically mentioned include: Mushrooms and lizard eggs Rothé meat Spider-meat used in ceremonial meals Lichen wine Slaves and livestock Expensive silks, leathers, and other status goods The noblewoman Velthura Vae lives in a tall, narrow residence overlooking the market. Instead of an ordinary window, she uses an enchanted crystalline mirror that allows her to observe the streets without permitting anyone below to look back at her. Her household contains numerous servants, male drow attendants, cooks, and bugbear bodyguard-slaves. The city also possesses a major amphitheater. Its spectacles include ritual sacrifice, giant-lizard racing, gambling, and private viewing boxes for nobles. The opening ceremonies witnessed by Velthura include the sacrifice of a captured surface elf upon an altar of Lolth. The arena appears to function simultaneously as entertainment venue, religious theater, political meeting place, and gambling establishment. Violence is so commonplace that when an assassin attacks Velthura in the bazaar, the crowd barely reacts. The incident is treated less like a public emergency than an inconvenience delaying her shopping. Government and noble politics No single ruler of Yvoth-Lened is named. Its politics appear to follow the decentralized drow model described elsewhere in the sourcebook: Lolth’s priestesses and the matrons of powerful houses exercise authority through influence, wealth, religious position, soldiers, slaves, and personal alliances rather than through a stable civic government. Three houses are particularly relevant. House Role in Yvoth-Lened House Vae Velthura Vae belongs to a local branch and intends to establish herself as matron of the Vae families residing in the city. Senior Vae relatives are traveling from Erelhei-Cinlu for a major family gathering. House Inlindl A powerful branch is ruled by Reverend Mother Dultha, both a senior priestess of Lolth and a house matron. Inlindl maintains enough distance between its branches that matrons in different cities might each claim to be the house’s true leader. House Eilservs The house is involved indirectly through a proposed marriage alliance that Velthura and Dultha are conspiring to destroy. These relationships indicate that Yvoth-Lened is not isolated. Noble relatives, messengers, conspirators, merchants, and marriage negotiations travel between it and Erelhei-Cinlu, even though the journey is lengthy and dangerous. The wider significance of House Vae In the Living Greyhawk treatment of Erelhei-Cinlu, House Vae is described as a formerly landless, wandering noble family that gained status through political opportunism. Its emblem is an iron chain, it controls Erelhei-Cinlu’s slave district, and its prosperity depends heavily upon an active slave trade. Other aristocratic families still regard the Vae as social outsiders despite their wealth and usefulness. This suggests—though it is not explicitly stated—that the Vae families in Yvoth-Lened may be one branch of a dispersed slaving and mercantile network. Their elders, merchant clans, guards, and agents could operate along the passage between the two cities. Velthura Vae and the defining story The sourcebook follows Velthura Vae through an apparently ordinary day. She awakens to the bells of Lolth’s temple, performs her private devotions, has servants clean and dress her, and magically checks her breakfast for poison. She then visits the bazaar to purchase food for the impending arrival of her relatives from Erelhei-Cinlu. During her shopping, a disheveled drow attacks her with a dagger. Velthura easily incapacitates him with magic and orders him taken away for interrogation. She is more insulted by the assassin’s incompetence than frightened by the attempt. At the amphitheater, Velthura meets Reverend Mother Dultha. Their conversation reveals several conspiracies: Dultha has arranged for one of Velthura’s rival relatives to die during the journey from Erelhei-Cinlu. Velthura is holding a mixed-heritage child whose existence will publicly disgrace a woman named Shenthral. Revealing the child during an upcoming wedding will destroy Shenthral’s planned alliance with House Eilservs. Velthura is already considering murdering Dultha once Dultha is no longer useful. Afterward, Velthura returns home, punishes her guards for failing to react quickly enough during the assassination attempt, checks her food again, and prepares for her relatives’ arrival. Despite all her precautions, Velthura has misunderstood the real plot. Her maid, Ashirza, arranged the clumsy assassination as a distraction. During the confusion, Ashirza poisoned the decanter of lichen wine Velthura had been drinking throughout the day and added a substance that delayed the symptoms. Velthura dies only after retiring to trance. The next day, it will be Ashirza—not Velthura—who greets the arriving Vae elders. That story is effectively Yvoth-Lened’s thematic statement: everyone expects betrayal, but familiarity with treachery does not make anyone safe. A servant who understands her mistress’s routines can be more dangerous than an enemy matron commanding an army. What remains unknown The published material does not provide: A city map A population figure A precise location beneath the surface The city’s founding history A definitive ruling matron or council A complete list or ranking of noble houses Military strength Named districts beyond the market, temple, and amphitheater The length or route of the passage to Erelhei-Cinlu Consequently, Yvoth-Lened is far less developed than Erelhei-Cinlu. Its canonical foundation consists primarily of its Lolthite temple, central market, amphitheater, intercity noble politics, and the deadly succession struggle surrounding Velthura Vae. The most natural interpretation is that Yvoth-Lened is a secondary drow metropolis and commercial crossroads, important enough to support multiple noble branches but not as politically dominant as Erelhei-Cinlu. Its temple would represent the entrenched religious establishment; House Inlindl would embody the local old guard; and House Vae would represent aggressive outside wealth built upon trade and enslavement. The amphitheater would be neutral ground where matrons negotiate, gamble, exchange hostages, and arrange murders under the cover of public spectacle. Ashirza’s assassination of Velthura also leaves an excellent unresolved situation. The Vae elders are about to arrive, the intended matron is dead, her rival cousin was murdered enroute, a politically dangerous child is being held somewhere in the city, and Reverend Mother Dultha knows enough to threaten everyone involved. Thus, the small amount of published lore already contains the beginnings of a major drow succession crisis. Yvoth-Lened is therefore valuable precisely because it is unfinished: it has a canonical name, atmosphere, route to Erelhei-Cinlu, factions, and political crisis, while leaving nearly all of its geography and deeper history available for development.

pages.title: Armstrong's Chamois
pages.content: This soft chamois was gifted to Kelpie on the evening of May 8th, 406 PR. This is a limited-use item that makes use of a usage die mechanic: When a slashing, bludgeoning, or piercing weapon is swiped with Armstrong's Chamois, the very next attack made with it within twenty-four hours gains a +1 bonus that stacks with any other to-hit bonus(es). If the attack connects, damage done with that first blow also receives a +1 bonus. These bonuses do not apply to second and subsequent attacks with the weapon. A given weapon can only benefit from Armstrong's Chamois once every twenty-four hours. When Armstrong's Chamois is used, roll it's usage die. If the result is a 1 or 2, the usage die decreases by one die-step. When given to Kelpie, the chamois' usage die was a d20. If Armstrong's Chamois' usage die is ever a d4 and a result of 1 or 2 is rolled, the cloth's magic is used up.

pages.title: Swift - Dorn's Longsword
pages.content: In the Shadowdim setting, sometimes (though rarely) when a loved one dies tragically, their soul inhabits an item of someone to whom they were especially close in life. Such a spiritual investiture”a Remnant Bond”transforms a mundane object into a "Soul-Bound Relic." Upon Exodore Swift's death, Dorn's serrated longsword ” already an item of high quality ” becomes a Soul-Bound Relic. Since the bond is rooted in their eternal love, the serrated longsword will no longer behave like a cold piece of steel. It becomes a protective, reactive extension of Exies will to keep Dorn alive. Beyond the +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls, Swift (for that is now the sword's name) has these qualities: The Phantom Guard (Defensive) Exie was always watching Dorn's back in life; in death, her spirit guides the blade to intercept blows. Effect: While wielding (not sheathed) the sword, Dorn gains a +1 bonus to Armor Class. Exie's Vitality (Defensive) Whenever Dorn draws Swift from its scabbard, if it has not been drawn in the past hour, it confers temporary hit points. These do not stack, and only apply if previously bestowed temporary hit points have been depleted. Swift Vengeance (Defensive) Whenever Dorn is wielding Swift and he sustains injury from a beastman, the spirit of Exodore inhabiting the blade lashes out, inflicting 3 hp (or 1 HD) of damage on the offending beastman. Swift functions only as a mundane, though high quality, sword when anyone other than Dorn wields it. It's powers will scale with Dorn as he becomes more experienced: Dorn's Level Phantom Guard Exie's Vitality Swift Vengeance --- --- --- --- 1-4 +1 AC +1d4 temp HP 3 hp (or 1 HD) 5-9 +2 AC +2d4 temp HP 6 hp (or 2 HD) 10-14 +3 AC +3d4 temp HP 9 hp (or 3 HD) 15-19 +4 AC +4d4 temp HP 12 hp (or 4 HD) 20 + +5 AC +5d4 temp HP 15 hp (or 5 HD)
