He added sadly. =========================================================== Message #49 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 397621 Nimba (NPC) Mon, 13 Jul 2026 00:57:34 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- Three hours later, the supper crowd has cleared out of The Mason's Apron. Nimba has finished sweeping and mopping the dining room. You can still hear the clink of pots and utensils as people in the back scrub and wash. Nimba has brought everyone piping hot mugs of a cinnamon-apple drink in thick porcelain mugs. The aroma they emit is soothing. Your sinuses open further upon inhaing the vapor. And when you sip and swallow, the warm glow in your innards tell you this is an alcoholic drink -- but Nimba avows that it is not . The three potential hirelings have left but agreed to talk further with Kelpie and Jelb the next morning, early. Nimba has joined an evening conference with her drinks, and serves pastries with them. In addition to her, the Drow who calls himself Shade is seated, as are Maximilian, Geoffroy, Kepie, and Jelb. Nimba's husband has joined you, a very tall and muscular blacksmith with a deep voice, a thick black beard, and a commanding presence. "Nimba tells me you're heading further north. Do any of you need a fresh edge put on a blade?" =========================================================== Message #50 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 396949 Geoffroy Morin Human, Fighter 1 6 hp Mon, 13 Jul 2026 03:07:27 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- "Me!" Geoffroy shouts, and he pulls out his sword and axe and tosses them on the table. =========================================================== Message #51 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 396653 Jelb Garrick Mon, 13 Jul 2026 03:41:03 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- Jelb thought he had missed something between the "not alcohol" and the multiple conversations. He tried to engage the mercenaries, completely missed Max's side conversation, and then spoke with the new drow. He first prioritized getting the most needed help first and laid things out for the mercenaries, then bidding them goodnight and hoping they actually did return in the morning. To Shade he said, "Jelb Garrick, well met. And thanks for being willing to listen. We know that the orcs were trying to take prisoners, so there is a chance that Narinza will be getting taken to the same place we seek. You're welcome to come with us in the search. You can have an equal share of any material goods we find, as long as you're willing to shoulder the danger we face alongside us." --- Later, when offered a sharpening, Jelb put his dagger up as well. "If I ever need to actually use this in combat... we are pretty well doomed. But all the more reason to make sure it's sharp. It must not fail us then." =========================================================== Message #52 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 396648 Kelpie Lawfuller Fighter 3, AC 2, HP 12/12 Mon, 13 Jul 2026 06:05:56 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- With the three potential retainers agreeing to return in the morning, Kelpie finally allowed himself a moment to relax. He turned to the elf with a slow nod “well met, Shade. Name’s Kelpie” the hedge knight’s voice was calm, his toothless grin friendly despite the long road ahead. To Nimba, he confirmed their plans “aye, we head north in the mornin’” then he turned to Samuel, and dipped his bald head in gratitude “aye, my sword saw plenty o’ use against the orcspawn. I’d be grateful if ye could oil it and sharpen the edge.” =========================================================== Message #53 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 397594 Shade D:12;W:13;P:14;B:15;S:16, AC4;HP4 Mon, 13 Jul 2026 14:50:29 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- Shade took a seat at the table. After a week and a few days on the road, part of it hunted by mysterious men in black, the sudden rush of information was disorienting. "Narinza was with you...?" he ventured, his voice thoughtful, the question wasn't looking for an answer. Instead, Shade's mind turned over the possibilities. If they traveled with her—and he had only their word for it, but something told him that could be trusted in this case—then they were not averse to the company of Drow. At least, not averse enough to invest in roasting forks or putrid vegetables. Small mercies, Shade. More importantly, this was the closest he'd come to finding her since he fled the Underdark. Until now all he'd had were whispers and rumors, ephemeral hints that proved wrong more than they did right. But this troop were actually with her. At least until they were separated by that confrontation with some beast. Or she chose that moment to slink away. He listened as Jelb expanded, sipping his cinnamon drink and nodding at the enchanter as he laid out his case. Taken prisoner? Narinza had avoided every snare the bloodlines laid for her, he doubted she would fall so easily into the hands of some orc warband or other. But if there was a chance, even the slightest one, he had to take it. "I'm your man. Or elf," he added with a twist of his lips too fleeting to be called a smile. "Maximilian, Jelb, Geoffroy, Kelpie. I'll remember. My name you know. I'll gladly travel with you, and share the risk in exchange for the reward." If nothing else, it would provide him cover against whoever was hunting him. "And if we're leaving so soon, I too could use an edge on my blade..." Drow blades were unequaled in the darkness, but sunlight eroded their edge much as it did his. =========================================================== Message #54 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by Samuel Armstrong () Mon, 13 Jul 2026 18:53:14 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- Samuel Armstrong is an imposing figure, at 6'4" and about 230 lbs. His face is lined and seamed by the heat of the forge and by years of squinting against the heat. After he has finished touching up your weapons, he removes a leather satchel from his shoulder and sets it on the table. "Caltrops," he says, by way of explanation. "Because sometimes retreat is the best option." Nimba's map of the area is spread wide upon the table. Samuel leans over the map. "The road from here to Threshold is crawling with orcs and bandits. If you think your experience en route to Raven's Pass was harrowing, the direct route north is three times worse." Nimba makes a moue with her mouth, her head nodding agreement. "Aye, but they value speed over safety." Samuel searches your faces. "Are any of you wanted; hunted, I mean? If so, that would be reason enough to avoid the northern road, even if the danger of combat were not enough to dissuade you. You could travel west through the Thicket Wood, then travel by boat most of the way, only turning due west for Slaythonthorpe when Threshold first becomes faintly visible on the horizon. You are far safer on the river than on the road." []( This message was last updated by the GM at 13:53, Mon 13 July. =========================================================== Message #55 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 396958 Maximilian Yragerne mystic theurge, of Arcantryl Mon, 13 Jul 2026 18:59:02 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- "Slaytonthorpe?" Max asks in question. =========================================================== Message #56 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 397621 Nimba (NPC) Mon, 13 Jul 2026 19:04:03 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- "Aye, if I understood rightly, you're making for the Blanryde Hills. Those are in the Slaytonthorpe demense. You'll want to present yourselves to the local lord there, Count Parlfray. But given the urgency of your quest, you might could delay that until after you scour the Blanrydes." =========================================================== Message #57 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 396958 Maximilian Yragerne mystic theurge, of Arcantryl Mon, 13 Jul 2026 19:08:36 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- "Ahh! Thank you very much! Notifying the lord will smooth things too. Perhaps we can do that quickly on our way through. Do you know Count Parlfray well? Would an introduction letter help if you do?" Max replies to Nimba and Samuel. This message was last edited by the player at 16:42, Mon 13 July. =========================================================== Message #58 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 397621 Nimba (NPC) Mon, 13 Jul 2026 20:01:32 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- "The count and I haven't met, no, although he and his son ate here a few years back, while traveling back to Milborne after a trip to the Southern Reaches. But I could send a tray of sweetmeats. The way to a man's heart is by way of one of two organs, and one of them is his stomach. I will whip up something tonight before bed. And don't worry, they'll not spoil on the road, so long as it takes you less than a week to reach the count." =========================================================== Message #59 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 396686 Dungeon Master (GM) Mon, 13 Jul 2026 20:49:13 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- A loud rapping sounds at the door to The Mason's Apron, and Samuel crooks an eyebrow, pausing in his weapon sharpening. "Sam, would you be a dear?" Nimba asks, nodding toward the door. The lumbering blacksmith carries Geoffroy's axe rather nonchalantly, and unlatches and opens the door with his other hand. There, an armored and shield-bearing dark-haired woman stands at the threshold. =========================================================== Message #60 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 396648 Kelpie Lawfuller Fighter 3, AC 2, HP 12/12 Tue, 14 Jul 2026 06:06:21 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- When Nimba laid out the map, Kelpie leaned over it, tracing a thick finger first to Kirkliston, then to Slaythonthorpe “Jelenth was taken from here and then brought here” he murmured, the pieces fitting together in his mind “from what we know, it took ’em about nine days o’ travel” Samuel’s question drew his gaze “we’re huntin’, not hunted” Kelpie replied firmly “we need to find the trail o’ the kidnapper or someone in Slaythonthorpe who can help us. Do ye know the ranger Kuiper, or where they might be found?” Then a sharp knock sounded at the door. When Samuel reached for his axe. Kelpie’s hand went instinctively to his sword hilt. He remained seated but ready, muscles tightening beneath his tunic as the door opened to reveal the mysterious armoured woman standing on the threshold. Kelpie watched her closely, jaw set, waiting to learn whether she was dangerous or here to help. =========================================================== Message #61 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 397594 Shade D:12;W:13;P:14;B:15;S:16, AC4;HP4 Tue, 14 Jul 2026 13:35:04 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- "I am," said Shade quietly before the rap on the door interrupted. "Hunted, I mean." When Samuel raised the danger, Shade debated whether to mention it or not. It wasn't the best way to introduce yourself to a new group. Hello, I'm Shade and I'm hunted by skilled killers who will probably murder you just for being with me. Not a great sell. Still, probably better than trying to explain it when a dozen horsemen rode up demanding his hide. In the end, the better side of his nature had won out. Bad enough that his being drow made everyone suspect he was a liar without actually confirming it. He needed the group's help, but he wouldn't pay for it by betraying the principles that forfeited his life with his own people. "No," he went on before anyone could ask. "I don't know by whom. In point of fact, it's more likely Narinza they want, not me, but they've been dogging my trail for two weeks and more. Ever since they got wind of my asking about her." He rubbed his chin. "Thought I'd lost them more than once, but each time, a few days later, they were back." And then the knock cut across him. He fell silent. For a horrible moment, the coincidence of mentioning the hunters and the knock persuaded him he'd somehow summoned the men. He quickly dismissed it. Were it them, they would hardly be likely to introduce themselves with a polite knock. Still, he breathed a sigh of relief when the door opened to reveal a dark-haired woman and not a score of black-armored strangers. He stood slowly, frowning. Something about the woman compelled him to speak, despite not long before arriving himself. "Well met," he offered. =========================================================== Message #62 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 396958 Maximilian Yragerne mystic theurge, of Arcantryl Tue, 14 Jul 2026 13:48:10 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- "Greetings M'Lady. Is there something we can do for you?" Max asked the woman in the door once Samuel had opened it. He also stood and bowed his head slightly in greetings to her. May I ask folks, if they haven't already, to include height and weight and hair and eye color in your descriptions if I may? Thank you. =========================================================== Message #63 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 397605 Nerissa Sedgefry Acolyte 1, AC 16+1 MV 60'/20' HP 6/6 Tue, 14 Jul 2026 14:39:28 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- "Good evening", says a low voice, as the door opens to the figure of a tall black haired woman. She wears a large brown cape, and one can see chain rings appearing from below the cape. A shield hangs from her arm, with a stag drawn on top of it, a mace is attached to her belt. The green eyes seem to escape a direct look as she enters the warm environment. "I am looking for a place to stay for the night, if you have one. And as I see some adventurers, maybe Herne listened to my prayers, as I am searching for companions to assist in battle." =========================================================== Message #64 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 396653 Jelb Garrick Wed, 15 Jul 2026 00:43:07 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- Jelb nodded to Shade. "Thank you for your honesty about the trouble you would bring to us. We know that the orcs bent on kidnapping are in league with other named and unnamed foes, so it is not unlikely that those who hunt you are in fact ones that we already hunt ourselves. It will be good to have one more ally with us." When yet another well-armed person came into the inn, Jelb was drawing near elation. Perhaps the gods were, in fact, watching out for them. When he heard the woman's words, however, his expression flattened. In fact, the earth under the large rock in the lawn would not be flatter than Jelb's gaze at that point. "Miss, I'm sorry. Normally almost every person present here would be glad to hear your story and give strong consideration to helping you. We ourselves are pursuing bandits who took a young lady some days past, and have now found ourselves also engaged against orc hordes, monsters from the deep, several other potential foes, as well as whatever murderers or kidnappers pursue this man. I am sorry, though." After a moment his gaze softened, "Your battle isn't figurative, is it? Because that we could manage. Or if it's against those we already fight. Or if it could wait until... Oh, I suppose you should tell us your story - the story itself can't turn into another blade aimed at us... hopefully." He took an exceptionally long pull of his definitely-not-alcoholic but probably-alcoholic beverage. =========================================================== Message #65 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 397621 Nimba Armstrong (NPC) Wed, 15 Jul 2026 00:55:55 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- Nimba goes to the woman and takes both her hands. "Come in, child? At the very least, we can provide you a hot meal and a room for the night. Oh! You are a warrior or holy orders?" =========================================================== Message #66 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 396686 Dungeon Master (GM) Wed, 15 Jul 2026 01:53:35 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- No sooner has Samuel closed and latched the door -- Nerissa isn't even halfway to the table where possibly-non-alcoholic beverages are served alongside pastries -- than there is another rap at the door. The look on Samuel's face ... well, you'll just have to picture it in your imagination. He turns back to the door and repeats his former performance: unlatch, open, Geoffroy's axe ready just in case. =========================================================== Message #67 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 396648 Kelpie Lawfuller Fighter 4, AC 2, HP 23/23 Wed, 15 Jul 2026 05:41:11 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- “Praise be to Herne” Kelpie offered as he greeted Nerissa, dipping his bald head with respect “we were only just speakin’ of huntin’” he mused, a smile touching his toothless mouth. He shifted his weight, leaning on the table with the slow care of a man whose bones had seen too many battles “mayhaps ye might offer us Herne’s blessin’ on the morrow before we leave?” he beseeched the cleric, his voice warm but edged with the seriousness of the road ahead. Before Nerissa could answer, another unexpected knock sounded at the door. Kelpie’s hand drifted instinctively toward his sword hilt. He did not rise, but every line of his body settled into readiness, the calm vigilance of a hedge knight who had learned never to trust a quiet evening. He waited, eyes fixed on the door, to see who sought them now. =========================================================== Message #68 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 396958 Maximilian Yragerne mystic theurge 2, of Arcantryl Wed, 15 Jul 2026 08:57:47 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- Max sat quietly now in anticipation of what was coming next. He slowing sipped his drink wondering about these insane 'red laws' they spoke about. Why would any community ban alcohol? It warmed your belly on a cold night, and when it stopped burning, it was good when you poured a bit on a wound as it seemed to help in keeping it from getting putrid with puss and getting gangrenous and killing you. It seemed everyone wanted in now as well. Folks kept knocking on the door. Then he nibbled a bit more of his food and took another drink, fairly unconcerned about danger at the door as there seemed to be enough armed folks to handle any threats real or perceived that might come upon them. =========================================================== Message #69 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 397594 Shade D:12;W:13;P:14;B:15;S:16, AC4;HP4 Wed, 15 Jul 2026 11:04:08 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- Shade breathed a sigh of relief. He hadn't even realized he'd worried so much about the group's reaction—he barely knew them, after all—but the prospect of being forced back onto the road alone had seemingly undermined his courage. By contrast, the feeling of being accepted felt like a weight from his back. He watched the newcomer curiously, sipping his peculiarly relaxing apple drink. Shade felt he possessed no right to speak for the group, having joined it only a heartbeat before her arrival, but the presence of an adherent of Herne, others of whom had helped him before, seemed auspicious. As she crossed the room, her restless gaze seeming to take them all in and rest on none, it occurred to him that the sudden arrival of disparate strangers at this inn together might be more than one of the many odd coincidences of the road. Maybe the hidden powers moving in their world were acting here, now? If so, the significance of the presence of Shade, the dark-haired paladin, and of whoever lay behind the latest knock on the door might not reveal itself for some time, if ever. Satisfied there was no need for his newly honed blade, Shade followed Maximilian's lead and lowered himself into his seat. The apple drink was making him oddly unsteady and maybe a little more of the food might help. He pushed another of Nimba's delicious pastries into his mouth and chewed thoughtfully. =========================================================== Message #70 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 397605 Nerissa Sedgefry Acolyte 1, AC 16+1 MV 60'/20' HP 6/6 Wed, 15 Jul 2026 12:51:53 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- Answering to Jelb , Narissa said "Oh, you misunderstand me, sir. It is not to ask help for battles of mine I am here. My creed - yes, I am of the horder of Herne", she added, looking at Nimba , "my creed, I said, compels me to great honors and to assist others in battles. You speak of pursuing bandits? That sounds like a holy quest to me!" She then took a sit, ordered some food, and looked at the door for the newcomer. =========================================================== Message #71 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 397622 Neria Silverdale Wed, 15 Jul 2026 23:53:59 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- As Samuel opened the door -- rather wearily, perhaps, but still warily -- the form of an armed and armored young woman was revealed beyond. Her friendly smile quickly turned wry at the sight of the axe at the ready, and she nodded respectfully. "Well met," she began, letting the man and those beyond see the shield she carried. It bore the distinctive sign of Cromm Cruach, a snowy mountain topped by a silvery crown. "You're wise to take care, but you have nothing to fear from me," she said, as she stepped into the room. She was not a tall woman, but wiry and with the look of a warrior... and a traveler, her boots and cloak dusty from the road. Besides the shield she also wore plate armor -- old but fine, well cared for -- that gleamed faintly in the firelight. A sword was sheathed at her side as well. Yet despite this, she looked around at those gathered inside as though she was stepping into a room filled with old friends and neighbors. Long, wavy red hair framed a kind face. "This inn's reputation must be well deserved," she went on. "Might I trouble you for a meal? Stew, perhaps?" she asked Samuel, before turning back to the others. Her hazel eyes glanced around the room once more, before pausing at the sight of Shade. A thoughtful frown replaced the smile, though only for a moment. "I've seen you before, sir, I believe," she ventured after a moment, questioningly. "On the road, not long ago? Neria Silverdale," she introduced herself, both to the drow and to the room at large. =========================================================== Message #72 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 396653 Jelb Garrick Thur, 16 Jul 2026 03:39:50 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- Jelb replied with relief to Nerissa, "That is excellent news. We would be very glad to have your aid." As the new woman entered, he silently wondered if Oceneroth or some other power for good had been exceedingly busy in the past day or so, or if chance were just being as kind to them today as it had been harsh the previous one. He was especially uncertain whether it was chance or providence when the most recent additions' names differed so little. He smiled and stood, his eyebrow raising when he recognized the sign of Cromm. While he usually didn't have much use or devotion for Cromm personally, he appreciated the god's general - if too straightforward - reputed pattern of thinking. Today, however, a warrior god's warrior follower was exactly what they could use. He extended a hand as he welcomed Neria. "Jelb Garrick, of Kirkilston. Make my evening complete: tell me you're spoiling for a just cause to fight for, and I'll tell you about a kidnapped young woman and an alliance between bandits, orcs, and possibly things even more foul... or just that you like Shade here and would love to see him not get taken by the murderers or assassins on his tail. I'd drink to either." With his other hand he picked up his mug of obviously-not-alcohol-because-that'd-be-illegal, really hoping he hadn't missed his guess. =========================================================== Message #73 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 396648 Kelpie Lawfuller Fighter 4, AC 2, HP 23/23 Thur, 16 Jul 2026 06:14:52 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- As the table grew crowded, Kelpie shuffled himself around, making space for the newcomers with the slow, he offered his toothless smile to all “praise be to Demetra for bringin’ all folk to her hearth” he said, voice warm and steady “may we all travel under her protection.” He nodded to each of them in turn, welcoming faces old and new alike. For a moment, despite the dangers waiting in the Blanryde Hills, the room felt safe. A small circle of firelight and fellowship held together by Demetra’s grace. =========================================================== Message #74 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 396958 Maximilian Yragerne mystic theurge 2, of Arcantryl Thur, 16 Jul 2026 10:06:35 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- Max rises to greet the two women finally, Max Yragerne, at you service. Wizard." He holds out his hand in greetings and moves to pull out and hold a chair for the ladies to each sit. =========================================================== Message #75 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 397594 Shade D:12;W:13;P:14;B:15;S:16, AC4;HP4 Thur, 16 Jul 2026 12:31:09 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- Shade scratched his neck and peered at the red-headed knight. He recognized her straight away, what he was puzzling over was what odd coincidence had made her appear in his life once more. "On the road," he said after a beat. "Two, nearly three weeks ago. You helped me. Outside that village... Kirkilston, was it?" He took in the others with a glance. "The men I mentioned? They overtook me on the road before I could cut into the forest. Only outriders, but I was hard pressed. It would have gone badly if not for the help of this woman." Shade stood, straining surreptitiously to make himself appear taller. "Well met, Neria Silverdale. The fight left no time for introductions. I am Shade, and I owe you my thanks." He bowed his head, then, suddenly self-conscious, he cleared his throat and sat, taking a hurried draft of the apple drink. There must be something more than apples in this, he thought. Shade was seldom so forthright, preferring to remain in the background. That might have been the longest speech he'd given since—he looked at the cup with its now cool contents and raised a skeptical eyebrow—well certainly since he'd stopped drinking. =========================================================== Message #76 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 396949 Geoffroy Morin Human, Fighter 1 6 hp Thur, 16 Jul 2026 16:49:11 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- "Getting crowdy in here." Geoffroy mumbled, then perked up. "Maybes there be enough peoples now to kill tent-ick-cols monster?" he says hopefully. =========================================================== Message #77 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 396958 Maximilian Yragerne mystic theurge 2, of Arcantryl Thur, 16 Jul 2026 17:32:12 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- Max looked at Geoffroy when he suggested going for the tentacled monster, "Perhaps after we find the girl we can look into that Geoff. Opinions on that afterward?" He asks the rest of the group. =========================================================== Message #78 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 397605 Nerissa Sedgefry Acolyte 1, AC 16+1 MV 60'/20' HP 6/6 Thur, 16 Jul 2026 19:14:13 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- "Oh, wow! You have even more than one quest!" Nerissa 's tone stayed calm, but she was clearly intrigued, both by the idea of heroic holy quests, but also by knowing that more people of faith seemed to be part of her newly-found group. "I believe saving a young lady in peril is a good deed to begin with, for us," she then added, nodding toward Max . This message was last edited by the GM at 14:26, Thu 16 July. =========================================================== Message #79 Ch 5 - A Betentacled Escape by 396686 Dungeon Master (GM) Thur, 16 Jul 2026 22:11:14 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- Please continue in Chapter 6: link to a message in this game ===========================================================

pages.title: Chapter 6 - At the Mason's Apron
pages.content: ========================================================== Message #1 Ch 6 - At The Mason's Apron by 396686 Dungeon Master (GM) Thur, 16 Jul 2026 22:10:40 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- An hour later, Samuel Armstrong has bid you a goodnight and has left the inn. The blacksmith is tired. His work is physically taxing, and customers will begin seeking him as soon as the sun rises. Nimba, Samuel's wife and Nuanda Nemere's sister, stays at the inn, but she busies herself in the kitchen to afford your company some privacy. She has refilled mugs with her delicious brew, and a fresh tray of tarts and other pastries adorns the center of the table. It is now perhaps two hours after full dark has fallen -- the time for heroes to collaborate, align in purpose, and perhaps forge a league. =========================================================== Message #2 Ch 6 - At The Mason's Apron by 397622 Neria Silverdale Fri, 17 Jul 2026 00:07:03 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- Neria does her best to learn everyone's name, offering smiles and nods as she greets them all. Jelb's sentiments almost make her laugh, though his mention of a kidnapped woman stops her. "If the cause is just, then I will always offer my help to it," she says, simply and seriously. "Such is my vow. And such is the reason for my travels -- to use whatever skills I have to aid those in need. "As I was fortunate enough to be able to do for Shade," she adds, turning back to the drow. "Near Kirkilston," she confirms. "I thought the men bandits, preying on a lone traveler... but there is more to it, it seems? Certainly I'd not wish to see him killed or taken, however, after all the trouble I went to to save him," she adds, her smile turning impish. "You see, you may drink to both of your hopes, Jelb. "In short, lady, gentlemen, if you have need of my sword to come to the rescue of any suffering at the hands of this fiendish alliance you mention, then you shall have it," she promises, with a little bow before she settles herself at the table. "You seem to have found more than your share of trouble. There seem to be many different skills here. Tell me where your strengths lie, and perhaps we can form a plan." =========================================================== Message #3 Ch 6 - At The Mason's Apron by 396648 Kelpie Lawfuller Fighter 4, AC 2, HP 23/23 Fri, 17 Jul 2026 07:45:59 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- Prepared for another long day’s travel, Kelpie declined the offer of more drinks and pastries “we should be ready for a long journey in the mornin’” the old hedge knight counselled the others “we fought many o’ the orcspawn to reach here, and there’ll be more dangers ahead.” At Neria’s request, he nodded his bald head and gave a slow, toothless smile “like my father before me, I travel the road in search o’ work” he said, settling into the tale as naturally as breathing “some call me sellsword those more courteous say hedge knight” he left it to them to decide which fit. Kelpie’s gaze softened as he spoke of his father “my pa taught me that honour is a true man’s armour. He helped those in need, whether they could pay or not. Loyal to those he served, grateful for every hearth that gave warmth. He thanked Demetra for the harvest, and for the good folk who tended it” He touched his brow, then his heart “my pa’s memory sits here and here. I try to honour it. I was his squire, and when he passed, I took up his sword to follow in his footsteps” Kelpie stretched his legs beneath the table, easing the stiffness from sitting “since then I’ve walked the road, fought when fightin’ was needed, laboured when work was required. A simple life but it’s the only one I’ve known these many years.” He looked around the crowded table, meeting each face with quiet resolve “in the mornin’ I go to the Blanryde Hills in search o’ the missing girl, Jenny. Any who can help are welcome to come.” =========================================================== Message #4 Ch 6 - At The Mason's Apron by 396958 Maximilian Yragerne mystic theurge 2, of Arcantryl Fri, 17 Jul 2026 10:30:02 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- "I'll be joining you Kelpie. I'm not sure how effective I'll be, but I'll be by your side in any case. Before I said wizard, I'm actually what they call a mystic theurge, I'm both wizard and priest to my god Arcantryl," he adds. This message had punctuation tweaked by the GM at 16:48, Fri 17 July. =========================================================== Message #5 Ch 6 - At The Mason's Apron by 397594 Shade D:12;W:13;P:14;B:15;S:16, AC4;HP4 Fri, 17 Jul 2026 12:21:48 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- "I don't think they were mere bandits," he replies to Neria's comment. "But I'm not sure who they were. I suspect what they want is caught up with what I want, to find Narinza, and I fear for her if they find her before I do..." He looks around at the others from beneath his brows. "...before we do, perhaps. It seems—those of us who stay—we are in the business of rescuing individuals in peril." Shade takes another swallow of his apple drink, listening to Kelpie's story with a wistful look on his face. Hearing the knight speak so openly about his father reminds Shade of what he left behind. He may not have had much choice in his fate, not after that one irrevocable decision, but it doesn't mean the loneliness is any less. He blinks smoke from his eyes and looks suspiciously at the drink once more. His head is beginning to swim and he has to take several deep breaths before he feels able to speak without his tongue dragging on the words. "You have my sword and bow, too, Kelpie. It will be good to be among comrades once more, though like Maximilian, I fear I may not be as effective as you need." Another breath and he pushes the cup away. "I am a ranger, but one more used to the tunnels and caverns of the Deep Kingdoms than your forests and mountains. Still, if you'll have me, for good or ill, I am with you." pages.title: Lair
pages.content: In tabletop roleplaying games (TTRPGs), a Lair is much more than just a monster’s home or a fancy word for a dungeon. It is a specialized, high-stakes environment tailored entirely to the strengths, themes, and defensive strategies of a specific boss or creature. Nixies tend to lair in underwater environments, wyverns in cliff caves or mountainous locations. Whether you are playing modern systems or classic, old-school mega dungeons, a lair serves several critical narrative and mechanical purposes. 1. Mechanical Advantages: "Lair Actions" In modern systems like Dungeons & Dragons 5e , a lair is a mechanical engine that actively fights against the players. The Environment as an Enemy: On a specific initiative count (usually 20), the lair itself acts. This could mean the walls erupt in magma, a freezing fog blinds the party, or the ambient gravity shifts. Leveling the Playing Field: These actions help solo bosses survive against a full party of heroes by shifting the "action economy" (how many moves the monsters get versus the players) back in the monster's favor. 2. The Sandbox & Ecosystem In Old School Renaissance (OSR) and classic dungeon crawls, a lair represents a major strategic milestone and a living ecosystem. The "Lair Chance" Roll: Classic monster manuals often include a "In Lair %" stat. If players encounter monsters wandering a dungeon, a high roll might mean they’ve stumbled directly into the creature's heavily fortified home base. The Reward Zone: A monster's lair is where it keeps its hoard. While wandering monsters might only carry pocket change or a single minor item, finding the lair is how a party hits the jackpot with massive coin stashes, ancient scrolls, and rare magic items. Active Defense: A lair isn't just a room; it's a gauntlet. It is designed around the creature's native abilities. A green dragon’s lair will be choked with toxic thorns and narrow tunnels; a beholder’s lair will feature vertical shafts to exploit its flight, and a rogue-like thief guild's lair will be absolutely riddled with hidden traps and escape routes. 3. Narrative Significance Narratively, entering a lair signals to the players that the kid gloves are off. It transforms a standard combat encounter into a set-piece boss battle. The architecture, the lighting, and even the local wildlife (or lack thereof) reflect the corrupting or dominating influence of the master creature, telling a story through the environment before the actual fight even begins. The Core Difference: You fight a wandering monster on your terms. You fight a monster in its lair entirely on its terms.

pages.title: Lakes
pages.content: Lakes are large bodies of water, usually freshwater. Notable lakes include Lake Donally, Farrod's Lake, Phultarr's Pool, Lake Sammeister, and Lake Illitar.

pages.title: Level Loss
pages.content: I particularly dislike level-loss mechanics, both as a player and a DM. My preference in implementing level-draining undead is for ability drain to be temporary (hours or days to recuperate), unless a key stat is drained to 0 ” for instance, Constitution reaching 0 would mean death. Alternatively, perhaps each successful attack by very powerful undead removes 250 XP from the PC's accumulated experience, not to fall below the minimum XP for the character's current level.

pages.title: Luna
pages.content: Earth's (and, therefore, Issenda's) moon. Also, the name of Prince Xavamros Battlebeard III's pony.

pages.title: Magic
pages.content: Many of the smartest people alive today disagree as to the specific nature and definition of magic . A consensus among a sizable minority of sages holds that magic is the application of extremely advanced technology that was gifted to Earth during the Visitation. The belief is that this technology (or, perhaps, these technologies) enable the marshaling of geomantic forces to bend and sometimes alter reality. Enchanted items have a Dweomer.

pages.title: Mithrilantine
pages.content: An alloy of adamantine and mithril, the secret of whose forging was long thought gone forever, but which the dwarves of the Gauntwood Galleries have reclaimed from the great crevasse of past history. Nearly as hard as adamantine, this allow is only two-thirds its weight and can much more readily accept enchantment.

pages.title: Mortalkind
pages.content: A mortal is any creature that is vulnerable to death, as opposed to immortal creatures. The Material Plane is considered the realm of mortals. Mortals as a collective are referred to as mortalkind. The state of being mortal is called mortality.

pages.title: Mythalvane
pages.content: A powerful relic, or perhaps artifact, taking the form of a globe of bright, shifting colors of magical energy that sits atop an old stone tower on a hillside overlooking the village of Helix in the Principality of Brine.

pages.title: Nabblat
pages.content: A Goblin term describing a non-goblin accorded the trust, respect, and friendship of the tribe. For instance, Chief Scarface has named Matthias D'Slaytonthorpe to be nabblat .

pages.title: Necromancer
pages.content: A mage (or, sometimes, cleric) that focuses on negative energy magic to control undead and deal generally unpleasantly with opposition. In some locales, necromancers must hide their focus out of fear for reaction from religious and/or civil authorities. Within the Middenmark, the punishment for necromancy is death.

pages.title: Neshralk
pages.content: Created using different materials depending on the wealth of the individual or family, neshralk are funerary figures that represent family members, servants to assist the wealthy in the afterlife, or soldiers to serve as tomb guardians. Many possess simple inscriptions devoted to eternal service. Generally, neshralk are 6" to 12" tall. Some are made of precious materials and/or are quite valuable to collectors. Some neshralk have magical effects. The barrows of the Barrowmaze contain numerous instances of these figures.

Here is a technical answer: I’m building the English-to-Orcish dictionary/translator as a structured lexicon rather than a flat word list: each entry preserves part of speech, sense, register, grammar tags, plural/possessive forms, and usage nuance so the translator can choose context-aware matches instead of collapsing unrelated meanings into one token. New terms should extend existing roots, compounds, affixes, and inflection patterns when possible; fixed phrases or compounds get explicit entries when composition would lose meaning. Before adding vocabulary, I check for exact and near collisions with existing terms and affix patterns, keep noun/verb/adjective distinctions separate, and verify representative translations so that the dictionary stays internally consistent, reversible where intended, and useful for both direct lookup and natural-sounding Orcish output. I'm using Chat-GPT-5.5-Pro to help guide lexicon formation. The translator will eventually be able to convert Issenda Orcish to English, as well. quote: At some tables, at some times, the XP is given not based on how well the party has done, but how well the boss has recently eaten. For the new people, I just finished writing my first edition of our Chronicles, which might be a nice quick read for what's gone on so far - any of the other players can add to it if they'd like: The party, consisting at the time of Jelb Garrick, Kelpie Lawfuller, and Urvan Hall met up by happenstance one night at Morgan's Morsels & Tankards in Kirkilston. Hearing of a missing young woman named Jeleneth. The three were bound together in a desire to see her saved. They spent the night at the Garrick home and set out the following morning. They met Nuanda, a local white witch, who divined after the young woman, determining that she was part of a rash of bandit abductions and disappearances in an area to the north. She recommended the party speak with the ranger, Kuiper, who dwells in that area and gave them a letter of introduction to him. Nuanda also recommended taking a caravan to Raven's Head to start the journey, and that in Ravens Head they should meet up with Nimba at The Mason's Apron Tavern and in addition to speaking with her, ask to see her husband Samuel who is a blacksmith and could help with gear maintenance. Nuanda also personally requested that the party provide her with the following if they should be willing and able: (1) an amethyst of at least 50 golden coins' value, (2) a rare herb called Hwyanthemon, and (3) the hair of a slain orc. =========================================================== Message #17 OOC May 25th Forward by 396648 Kelpie Lawfuller Fighter 2, AC 2, HP 8/8 Sat, 30 May 2026 06:26:08 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- Been really busy with other stuff this month and this will likely continue through out summer. I've been using the rule: OSE: Equipment: The weight of the character’s armour and weapons is also tracked (the weight of these items is listed in the equipment list). Miscellaneous adventuring gear (backpack, spikes, sacks, etc.) may be counted as 80 coins of weight. Do you need us to track weight of miscellaneous adventuring gear? =========================================================== Message #35 OOC May 25th Forward by 396648 Kelpie Lawfuller Fighter 2, AC 2, HP 8/8 Sun, 31 May 2026 07:11:03 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- As an observation and some feedback looking at the Mystic Theurge. I would think the XP requirement needs to be increased. A normal Magic-user learns one spell per level, the rules implies that the Mystic Theurge starts at level 1 with knowing all the spells! That’s a massive advantage on top of gaining Cleric spells as level 2. The only downside is the change from 2500XP to 3000XP, that hardly a downside at all. Given the power level I would suggest more like 4000XP or even higher. As written the class is arguably stronger than an Elf, Elves pay heavily for their hybrid casting. The example given doesn't line up either. Mystic Theurge: Example at Level 3: Slots: 2 first level spells + 1 second level spell Possible Preparation: Cure Light Wounds (Cleric) + Sleep (Wizard) + Bless (Cleric) If the class follows Cleric spell progression they will not have access Bless at level three, because Clerics don't get 2nd level spells until level 4. If instead they gain Cleric spells at level 1, that’s another massive advantage. Either way, the current Mystic Theurge: Have more spell choice than a Magic-User Casts more spells than a Cleric Has access to both lists earlier Pay almost no XP penalty for it That effectively makes both core classes redundant. =========================================================== Message #36 OOC May 25th Forward by 396958 Maximilian Yragerne mystic theurge, of Arcantryl Sun, 31 May 2026 08:23:50 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- Very true. Should the Cleric spells follow the Cleric spell progression? First level spell at 2nd level too? =========================================================== Message #37 OOC May 25th Forward by 396653 Jelb Garrick Sun, 31 May 2026 10:57:40 GMT ----------------------------------------------------------- Looking later in the page, I think that was a typo and that it meant 2 level one spells of one class and one level one spell of the second class (rather than one of second level). I say that not just because of balance, but the class is still casting level one spells (though 5 of them) at level 5. With the high XP cost, I would think they should have level 2 spells from one side starting at level 5. Then get their second class a level 2 spell at 6. They would still be adding a spell per day each level, just reaching higher levels much more slowly in exchange for the versatility (which seems extra important in an otherwise no-multiclassing game). At that rate, it'll be level 9 before they get a third level magic user spell, and 10th when they get that sweet double advance of a 3rd and 4th level cleric spell. And at that point, they should possibly start gaining access to higher levels faster. 2nd level Spells and both lists at 3 seems strong. But not getting 4th level MU until 15 (or even higher if they're still only throwing level 1's at level 5 as the other example) seems tough as well. If no one minds, I could write up a proposed full example of spellcasting progression along this line this afternoon. Edit: highlighted proposed because I want to continue discussion and help one side get to play what they like and have it be effective, while not making everyone else feel like they're held to one class while others get an even better-than-multiclass progression. OSE: In the classic Advanced game, there is a tendency for classes’ abilities to overlap significantly, leading to classes that have, for example, all of the abilities of a standard fighter or thief plus extra abilities of their own. Such classes are very powerful and tend to out-shine the classes whose abilities they share. The new classes in this book are designed with their own unique abilities and avoid encroaching on the niches of the standard classes described in Classic Fantasy:Genre Rules. That’s the core issue: any new class needs to avoid overshadowing the four pillars of B/X play, Fighter, Cleric, Magic User, and Thief. OSE caps all classes at 14th level. I don’t think we need to worry about anything beyond that. If we ever do need higher level progression BECMI exists as a reference, but that’s a problem for later. So I suppose all I’m saying is as stated above, any new class needs to not overshadow the basics of Magic-user, Cleric, Thief and Fighter. As an observation Magic-users are deliberately difficult to play especially as lower levels. 1 spell per day 1d4 hp Only daggers No armour Slow XP progression Spellbooks are vulnerable They don’t get 6th level spells until very late Anything that grants Magic-user spells without those restrictions needs to be balanced i.e. the elf, has two prime requisites, needs much more XP and doesn’t get level 6 spells. The Mystic Theurge has the advantage of more weapon choice, a Magic-user can only use a dagger for 1d4 damage, anything doing more than 1d4 or has greater range is an advantage, they have both. Turn Undead is the Cleric’s strongest class ability and the class Niche of a Cleric. pages.title: Orojiam
pages.content: A dark, smooth liquor with overtones of cinnamon, honey, and nutmeg.

pages.title: People
pages.content: generally the term people is used to collectively refer to humanoid Surface races that tend to congregate and live together for mutual protection, education, reproduction, and safety. The more broad-minded person might also consider Drow, Goblins, and even Illithids people, too.

pages.title: Perk Planning
pages.content: The awarding of Perk Points could involve an activity-based two-week cycle: Participation: 1 PP at the end of each two-week cycle when the character made a meaningful IC contribution. Major milestone: 1 PP for completing a quest, resolving a significant objective, or surviving a major expedition. Class expression: 1 PP for an exceptional solution strongly associated with the character’s class, limited to once per four weeks. OOC contribution: 1 PP for a substantial campaign contribution—recap, map, rules research, character art, scheduling work, or useful worldbuilding—limited to once per four weeks. Cap: No more than 4 earned PP in any four-week period unless the DM explicitly grants a special award. Routine posting, repeated actions, or manufactured “thematic” activity should not qualify. Expected pace: Typical active character: 3–4 PP per month. Standard individual perk: approximately 1–2 months. Three-rank tree: approximately 3 months. Occasional players still progress, but inactivity does not produce passive points. If we decide to go with a weekly award, retain 1 PP per active week but cap total earnings at 5 PP per four weeks? Tree structure Use trees for abilities representing sustained training, doctrine, or a developing supernatural tradition. Suggested structure: Rank Cost Function ------------------- ------ --------------------------------------------------------- Foundation 3 PP Introduces the tree’s defining option Specialization 3 PP Improves or broadens that option Mastery 4 PP Provides the signature tree ability Optional capstone 5 PP Requires all previous ranks and a narrative achievement A standard three-rank tree therefore costs 10 PP, rather than 9 PP. The slightly higher final cost reflects its greater power. Good existing trees include: The Three Stances of General Vask Spell Secrets of a Deity The Codex of Transmutative Alchemy Faith of the Shieldbearer Shadows of the Underworld Frontier Tactics Veteran Disciplines Weapon Masteries Arcane Research Sacred Authority Pathfinder, Hunter, and Survivalist Trees can branch instead of always being linear: Foundation ├── Offensive specialization └── Defensive specialization └── Mastery requiring either specialization This allows investment in a particular discipline without making every Fighter, Cleric, or Ranger follow the same sequence. Commitment to a tree The “one started but incomplete tree” rule is a good way to make specialization meaningful, but it needs an escape valve. Recommended rule: A character may invest PP in only one incomplete tree at a time. Completed trees do not prevent starting another. Individual perks can still be purchased while a tree is incomplete. An incomplete tree may be shelved after appropriate downtime, training, or a narrative change. Shelved ranks remain owned, but no PP can be added to that tree while another tree is active. No PP are refunded merely for shelving a tree. The DM may permit a respec if a perk is materially rewritten or proves unusable. This preserves commitment without permanently trapping someone in a tree that no longer fits the campaign. Individual and one-off perks Use individual perks when the ability comes from a singular event, relationship, discovery, scar, blessing, reputation, or strange experience rather than a trainable discipline. Suggested prices: Type Cost Examples --------------- -------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------- Minor utility 3 PP Rumor access, language, cartographic intuition Standard 5 PP Once-per-day reroll, situational defensive option Major 7 PP Extra spell use, borrowed class ability, permanent save bonus Story-granted Free or specially priced A blessing, mutation, title, or consequence earned in play Strong candidates for one-off status: Gripper of the Grody — singular character history; probably a 7 PP major perk or a free story award. Nildor’s Nudge — a self-contained once-per-day ability; 5 PP. Ancient Cartography and other Lost Secrets — discovery-gated one-offs, generally 3–5 PP. Slayer’s Eye — 3 PP utility perk. Scribe’s Intuition — 3 PP utility perk. Anointing of the Dead — 3–5 PP depending on how absolute its protection is. Light Fingers, Fast Sleeves — 3 PP. Deadfall Instinct — 5 PP. Beast Mastery: Signals — 3–5 PP. Abilities that grant another class’s feature, an extra daily spell, or an always-on numerical bonus should usually cost 7 PP, require a narrative unlock, or become part of a tree. Granted versus unlocked perks Use two distinct terms: Granted perk: The character receives it for free because of events in play. It may be accepted or declined, but declining grants no PP. Unlocked perk: The character has discovered a teacher, secret, or opportunity and may now purchase the perk with PP. A player should receive substitute PP only when the DM grants a perk that is mechanically unusable for that character—not merely unwanted. Recommended compact rule Characters earn 1 PP after each two-week period in which they meaningfully participate in play. The DM may award 1 additional PP for major milestones, exceptional class-themed accomplishments, or substantial OOC contributions. A character normally earns no more than 4 PP in a four-week period. Tree perks cost 3 PP for foundational and intermediate ranks and 4 PP for a mastery rank. Ranks must be purchased in prerequisite order. A character may invest in only one incomplete tree at a time but may purchase individual perks while developing that tree. Individual perks cost 3 PP for minor utility, 5 PP for standard abilities, and 7 PP for major abilities. Some perks must first be unlocked through play. Story-granted perks cost no PP, and declining one does not produce PP. This would give us predictable progression, reward participation without encouraging farming, and would make a completed tree feel like a meaningful character investment.

pages.title: Phandalin Three
pages.content: This trio was an adventuring band comprised of Lancaster Fox, Feyre Archeron and Celaena Sardothien. This band became active in the Northern Reaches in PR 204 and remained so until 207. This was approximately four centuries prior to the events portrayed in the Scarlet Horizons RPOL game. After Whiteheart Stiffwhiskers joined the group, this adventuring band became known as The Phandalin Four .

pages.title: Plaguewalkers
pages.content: Humanoids turned into shambling fungal husks by the Soul Fungus, which seems highly concentrated at Mordoom Keep but probably originated generations ago in Arden Vul. Plaguewalkers are slow, but they don't require sleep or any apparent form of nourishment. They seem driven to spread fungal spores and can do so either through physical contact or through generating a spore cloud.

pages.title: Plast
pages.content: A substance produced in the time of the Far Ancients, plast can be hard or flexible. It is prized for its durability and insulative qualities.

pages.title: Player Character
pages.content: In the tabletop version of a roleplaying game, there are usually two or more people who take on the role of players, and each player controls and makes decisions for a character . These characters are the actors in the unfolding adventure or story. The players are the people sitting around the table, each player assuming the role of his or her character ” in essence, stepping into that character's shoes, living in their skin. Because of this intimate connection between the player and her character, that character is often known as a PC ” a player character .

pages.title: Post-Ravaging
pages.content: Also sometimes designated as P.R. , this signifies Post Ravaging , a period of history following the great ravaging of western Westmark by the Shou. Ancient Westmarch included areas that are now known as the Northern Reaches, Southern Reaches, and Arandia.

pages.title: Querma
pages.content: A hot drink made with cow or goat's milk, sugar, and cinnamon. Some people put other ingredients in as well. Querma is 3% to 4% alcohol by volume.

pages.title: Red Laws
pages.content: The Red Laws of the Prelacy of Middenmark are instituted, ostensibly, by the ruling council of guild masters in Eastdale. In truth, these Red Laws are instituted and ultimately enforced by Mordicar Justhand, the true power in Middenmark. The Red Laws place harsh sumptuary restrictions on the populace. They make it illegal for clerics of gods other than St. Ygg to preach or make converts in the Middenmark. And they require that felonies by tried by a court whose judge is appointed by the Prelate, Mordicar Justhand. St. Yggs faith tends to be puritanical on matters of morality, and the Red Laws forbid gambling, prostitution, and alcohol (with a notable exception, see The Saucy Tart). The Red Laws also promote Sabbath observance and worship. It is rumored that these religious edicts have created an illegal underground network, facilitated by a small thieves guild, that traffics in forms of contraband. Prohibitions Gambling: All forms of gambling are banned. Brothels: Outlawed within the town limits. Alcohol: Consumption Restricted, with The Saucy Tart being an exception after 8 PM. Mordoom Keep: Off-limits to the public. Mandatory Practices Sabbath Observance: Required participation in religious services. Dress and Decency Codes: Prescribed standards for public appearance. Censorship: Control over arts and literature. Property And Economy Property Acquisition: Governed by official documentation and witness validation. Taxation and Guild Fees: Varied based on profession and income, mandatory for guild maintenance. Crime And Punishment Thievery and Crime: Ranging from public shaming to imprisonment or hard labor. Public Shaming: Utilization of the pillory in the market square for minor offenses. "In closing, let us remember that our adherence to the Red Laws is not a burden but a privilege, a manifestation of our unwavering faith in St. Ygg. As we navigate the trials and tribulations of our times, let these laws be our guiding light, leading us to a future graced by righteousness. May St. Ygg's wisdom continue to illuminate our path, and may his strength fortify our resolve in upholding these sacred decrees." - His Venerable Mercy, Mordicar, the Just Hand The Red Laws influence every aspect of life in Eastdale, from daily activities to moral behavior, shaping the town's cultural and social fabric. This strict legal framework presents challenges and opportunities for storytelling, character development, and gameplay within the Prelacy of Middenmark.

pages.title: Remnant Bond
pages.content: A spiritual investiture that transforms a mundane but high-quality object into a Soul-Bound Relic.

pages.title: Residuum
pages.content: A rare magical substance coveted for its ability to catalyze magical transformations and transmutations.

pages.title: Ritual
pages.content: A scripted act, usually involving speech, one or more focus items, and sometimes sacrifice of life or of other valuables. A ritual takes at least five rounds, and some may even last hours . Most only take a few minutes. A ritual enacts some outcome, affects reality in some way. It may give everyone involved certain status effects, or ward an area, or extend or shorten the duration of some process.

pages.title: Roleplay
pages.content: Roleplaying occurs when real-life people assume the role of a character within an evolving, jointly-created story ” as story usually directed by a dungeon master but to which the individual players significantly contribute over time. Generally, these Players attempt to roleplay their respective characters based upon various statistics, background information, personality traits, and motivations that are recorded on a character sheet, a living document that changes over time.

pages.title: Runic Tablets
pages.content: Runic Tablets were often interred with the dead in Barrowmaze to ward off tomb-robbers. Folk tales say the tablets curse those who read them.

pages.title: Sage
pages.content: A very learned person whose expertise typically lies in a single area. Some sages are historians, some archaeologists. Others may specialize in monster lore, or in arcana. To consult a sage is to consult a topic expert.

pages.title: Soul Fungus
pages.content: A relatively recent plague whose first known outbreak occurred at Mordoom Keep. The infection rapidly consumed the keep and its inhabitants, transforming them into "Plaguewalkers"—undead fungal thralls whose bodies and souls have been overtaken by the fungus. The fungus itself appears as a faintly glowing green mold. Witnesses report seeing soul-like wisps trapped within its growths, leading to the belief that the souls of its victims become imprisoned within the fungal mass rather than passing on normally. Effects of Infection Known effects include: Transformation of living creatures into fungal zombies or "Plaguewalkers." Infection of wildlife, including wolves and other animals. Consumption or corruption of the victim's soul. Distinctive glowing purple eyes in infected creatures. Eventual incurability after an incubation period. One particularly disturbing belief recorded by investigators is that exposure may occur through the eyes: "Eyes are the window to the soul." The Sporebane Brotherhood believes looking directly upon certain fungal growths may be enough to initiate infection.

pages.title: Sources of Experience Points
pages.content: mapping on graph paper: variable XP upon sharing a copy with the Dungeon Master creating journal entries (here on RPOL) that reflect your character's experiences and thoughts: variable XP outwitting or slaying monsters forging a new alliance with an important NPC completing a quest (quests are assigned by important NPCs) funding and establishing a stronghold suggest world lore by posting about it as if it were true

pages.title: Spell
pages.content: A spell is a pattern of Magic energy held in readiness, akin to the potential energy of a boulder at the top of an incline. A spell is not only this pattern but also acts as the trigger to release that potential energy into reality-altering kinetic magical energy.

pages.title: Tangsin
pages.content: A mild, smoked drug popular throughout the Reaches, tangsin is a mixture of tobacco, ginseng, and the leaf of a hyoscyamine-containing plant. Tangsin tends to relieve intestinal and allergy symptoms in humans, elves, and half-elves. These effects are less notable in gnomes, halflings, an dwarves ” but it is significantly beneficial in treating hypertension in gnomes and halflings. No broadly effective treatment of hypertension has been discovered for dwarves. The majority of human, elven, and half-elven users choose to use tangsin for the pleasant taste and mild feelings of euphoric connection it engenders.

pages.title: Technology
pages.content: A contrivance of the Ancients, technology was the ability of said Ancients to harness scientific knowledge and principles and distill them into devices of convenience. Some of those devices went beyond mere convenience, fostering transmission of knowledge and security intergenerationally. The Visheat Device is a prime instance of such technology that has survived to the present day. The word technology may refer to specific devices or to this harnessing of science that makes them possible.

pages.title: THAC0
pages.content: To-hit-AC-zero. In the RPOL Scarlet Horizons campaign, we're using ascending AC, but for some players it may be easier to think in terms of THAC0.

pages.title: The Red Tide
pages.content: A phenomenon in which seawater coming shoreward on the tide is tinted scarlet, from the shore and seemingly out to sea even to the far horizon. Scarlet Horizons are much feared because they herald a period of madness among intelligent creatures that come within half a mile of this phenomenon, and aberrant behavior even across creatures of only animal intellect. It is rumored this phenomenon was first recorded in PR 196 and that it has even been found in some very large inland lakes since PR 201. Curiously, Shou seem highly resistant to the effects of this Red Tide. This tide always carries magical emanations, yet also seems to be a naturally-occurring phenomenon.

pages.title: The Shou
pages.content: A numerous off-shoot of humanity corrupted into variations of human-adjacent species by the Visitors and invested with hatred for non-Shou. These people are generally magic-resistant and particularly so to the Red Tide.

pages.title: Throiki
pages.content: For generations, ever since The Disc was discovered in the thickly vined jungle of Chult in PR 118, the Church of Arcantryl has had a faction known as the Hûl Hildresu that are a mashup of adventurers and archaeologists with either outright spellcasting ability or at least the aptitude. The Hûl Hildresu was formed in PR 120 after the archmage Tibeon Nhee failed to forge entrance into the 2-mile diameter Disc but did succeed in siphoning energies off the massive artifact -- energies that later powered his transformation into a lich. The Hûl Hildresu dubbed whatever people or creatures were responsible for the Disc 'the Throiki', based off word fragments found on an ancient scroll discovered in the ruins of long-abandoned temple near The Disc.

pages.title: Thuldor
pages.content: The dwarven word (meaning 'those who endure') for priests of Laduguer. Novices of Laduguer are known as the Untempered. Full priests of the Exile are known as Grimcloaks. In ascending order of rank, the titles used by Ladugueran priests are Deep Adept, Dark Craftsman, Invisible Artisan, Rune Weaver, Grim Guardian, and Doom Knight. High Old Ones have individual titles but are collectively known as the Ardukes of the Gray Gloom.

pages.title: Touched
pages.content: The Touched are those gifted with eldritch power that expresses itself in some manner other than spells. The expression might take the form of magical artifacts, uncannily accurate intuition, mutations, even seemingly impossible abilities.

pages.title: Tresendar
pages.content: The surname of a wealthy family from Threshold. In 100 PR, a second son of the then current generation of House Tresendar had a disagreeable taste left on his palate from city politics. He took ship on the Isenduin and traveled southwest, establishing his family in the fledgling community of Phandalin that was being built atop the ruins of Undalan. Tresendar Manor was erected in PR 100 and 101, and stood for over a century, abandoned when the original owner's grandchildren decided to return to Threshold in PR 199. The manor was burned to the ground by the Phandalin in PR 204.

pages.title: Triple Motte
pages.content: A triple-refined whiskey made in Ironguard Motte by the gnome apothecary, Athelbynson Lothaybin. This is not general knowledge. Those in-the-know suspect that Athelbynson probably makes more profit from this side business than from all the rest of his apothecarial endeavors. Athelbynson father, Athelbyn, is also an apothecary, but in some far distant town near a mega dungeon called Arden Vul.

pages.title: Undead
pages.content: The undead are beings in mythology, legend, or fiction that are deceased but behave as if alive. Most commonly the term refers to corporeal forms of formerly alive Human, such as mummies, vampires, and zombies, which have been reanimated by supernatural means, technology, or disease. In some cases (for example, in Dungeons & Dragons, the term also includes incorporeal forms of the dead, such as ghosts).

pages.title: ur'krik
pages.content: The Goblin word for abomination, most often used by them in referring to products of non-shamanistic magical, but also of unnatural creatures such as Undead.

pages.title: Vampiric
pages.content: A weapon with this property restores two hit points to its wielder ” up to the wielder's maximum hit points ” whenever the weapon draws blood from another creature. Only a weapon able to deliver piercing damage may have this property. While wielding or carrying a Vampiric weapon, the owner enjoys a +4 bonus to saving throws against undead. On a critical miss, the weapon's Vampiric property is suppressed for the next 1d4 rounds. On a critical hit, an injured foe will bleed for an additional two points of damage per round for the remainder of that encounter, or until healed. This extra bleeding damage doesn't cause the Vampiric weapon wielder to regain two hit points.

pages.title: Visheat Device
pages.content: A device which, according to legend, was gifted hundreds of thousands of years ago by an advanced species that visited Earth. The device is fueled by copper or copper-containing alloys. A single copper piece, when fed to the device, will cause it to emit sufficient heat to warm a 150 square foot area for two hours. The device is metallic and generally cubic in shape, although all edges are rounded. It is approximately six inches to a side, and weighs three pounds. No one has ever succeeded in disassembling a visheat , as they are known/called colloquially. The resistant to damage. It is a testament to the Visitors' technology that these devices are still functional after so many millennia.

pages.title: Visitors
pages.content: The Throiki (throw-ee-KIGH), aliens who visited Issenda hundreds of thousands of years ago during The Visitation , probably somewhere in the time period the Ancients would have dated 2004 to 2025 on the Gregorian calendar. The number of sages who hold to this theory is larger than one might surmise, perhaps because of the fair amount of certainty among scholars regarding the extrasolar origin of one other existing race not originating on Earth, the illithids. Although both analog and digital records of the event may all now be lost to history, The Visitors were first encountered by human beings on November 14, 2004, during a U.S. naval training mission near San Diego. Two Super Hornet pilots were the first homo sapiens to observe this alien visitation. This visitation was probably at least half a million years ago. The Visitors gave rise to various races and phenotypes, among them the Sarrukh, the yuan-ti, and true dragons such as Valashinaz.

pages.title: Wealth
pages.content: All of the below is from my homebrew RPG, and these rules are subservient to OSE RAW for the world of Issenda's Old School Essentials rules. Experience points (XP) are gained from quest completion, world-building, and another two sources: treasure and monsters. However, XP from treasure is only gained if it is spent . Thus, if a character brings 1,000 gold pieces worth of treasure out of a dungeon, he only gains one XP for every gold piece spent. This gold can be spent on anything, whether vital or frivolous, but it must be exchanged for something in order to earn the experience points. The design intent of this house rule is twofold. First, it keeps player characters cash poor and thus provides them with ample incentive to continue adventuring. Second, it forces characters to use their wealth rather than simply hoard it. Some will fritter it away on meaningless pleasures and trifles, while others will invest it into large projects, such as spell research or the construction of a stronghold. When treasure is spent properly to earn experience, a single gold piece (a royal ) ” or gold piece worth of objects d'Art, etc. ” translates to 1.0 XP. Therefore, chroma translate to 0.1 XP, and shiny cuprous to 0.001 XP. PCs should normally trade in red-, black-, and aquamarine cuprous for gold before spending treasure. Be sure to track treasure and wealth separately. Treasure represents valuables, including maps and information, which characters risk their lives to bring back to civilization. Wealth is acquired without danger. Only treasure generates XP when spent, which may also generate wealth . For example, characters who recover 20,000 gp from the dungeon record it as treasure and earn XP when they spend it on the deed to a gold mine. Gold mined from their new acquisition will be recorded as wealth, which can be spent like any other gold but will not earn XP in the process. It is fine for players to try to spend their treasure in ways that will make them richer and better able to seek treasure. Although treasure must be exchanged for something, this may be abstract. A party which bribes an intelligent monster for information, or to be allowed to pass unmolested, certainly gains something if the attempt is successful. If the bribe is subsequently regained by killing or robbing the monster, it should be recorded as wealth rather than treasure, and may earn the party a reputation that hinders future negotiations. The unambitious will be content to gather wealth, but those seeking advancement must be willing to risk their lives for treasure. Once gained, spending it before someone else takes it away becomes an urgent priority. One of the most common ways to spend treasure is to offer it as a reward in exchange for the completion of some task which can generate wealth or improve one's chances of survival.

pages.title: Xanderpetals
pages.content: A flower that grows in the vicinity of Raven's Pass known for its medicinal properties but also for an unfortunate side effect of its pollen: the Dream Fever. During its growing season, Xanderpetals can cause sensitive individuals to have trouble waking, and to experience feverish dreams in which they (according to later recollection) speak with ancient draconic beings known as The Seven. One in seven people who succumb to Dream Fever suffer long-term memory loss.

pages.title: Yggian Benediction
pages.content: From dissipation to service, from vanity to selflessness, from injustice to righteous deliverance! This benediction is used to end corporate prayers to St. Ygg and also to confirm the vows of a knight entering paladin service to St. Ygg.

pages.title: Yggian Pledge
pages.content: "Do you commit yourself to uphold the weak, to champion the helpless, to destroy the undead, to serve the Church, and to have lifelong, unflinching loyalty to Saint Ygg?" This pledge is made by those seeking to enter St. Ygg's service as paladins.

pages.title: Zekiran'hru
pages.content: Mire Friend , a title rarely given by the Lizardfolk of Shrieken Mire in Slaytonthorpe. These Lizardfolk serve the adult green dragon, Inzeldrin. In PR 25, Xavamros Battlebeard I and the other Lightbringers , were named Zekiran'hru .

pages.title: zhou'kast
pages.content: The Goblin word for decimation or annihilation.

pages.title: Aboleth Spawn
pages.content: No. Enc: 1 (2d3) ¢ Alignment: Chaotic ¢ Movement: 30' ¢ Armor Class: 6 ¢ Hit Dice: 4 (typically 23-28 HP), or by level if PC/NPC ¢ BAB +4, or by class and level if any adventurer ¢ Attacks: 1 pseudopod slap (and special), or 1 by weapon ¢ Damage: By single weapon attack or 1d4 via pseudopod slap ¢ Special: Constitution-based save vs DC 12 or slowed ¢ Save: F4, or by PC level if an adventurer ¢ Morale: 10 ¢ Hoard: 3d4 chroma, 1d4+4 royals, 1d4+8 copper (30% it's Red Cuprous ) abolethSpawn-optimized.png Anytime five or more aboleth spawn are found together, one of them will be a 5 HD specimen with 31 HP and with 2d4+4 royals, 3d4+4 chroma, 2d4+6 copper (35% it's Red Cuprous ). This leader will have the same Morale and saving throws as its fellows, but is BAB +5 and it's slap deals 1d4+2 (or 1d4 + adventurer aboleth-spawn Strength bonus, if greater than +2). A defeated leader aboleth spawn is worth 750 xp. Aboleth spawn appendages are coated with a sticky, numbing secretion. Unarmored creatures struck with a pseudopod must make a Constitution-based saving throw versus DC 17 or be stuck fast . Such a creature suffers a four-point penalty to AC and then a further penalty of loss of any Dexterity bonus to AC. There is a 33% chance that a humanoid so struck and stuck will have its weapon hand and arm immobilized. A stuck fast creature may make further saving throws at the beginning of each new round, with a cumulative -1 penalty. Armored characters must make the same type of saving throw, but at a DC 15. Any creature that begins its turn stuck fast may be automatically dealt 1d4 constriction damage by the aboleth-spawn, so long as its other appendages remain free for this purpose. In lieu of its stuck fast ability, the aboleth-spawn may instead choose to attempt to Slow a struck victim.
