pages.content: Aboleth Spawn Beastman Bugbear Couatl Geppettin Goblin Dragonbone Golem Dragon Turtle Froglings Phaerimm Skeleton Troll True Dragons Wood Golem

pages.title: Beastman
pages.content: beastman-optimized.png Beastmen gain +2 on Strength-based checks, saving throws versus disease, and saves versus fear or charm effects. Their tough hides and fur afford them AC 7 even when not wearing armor. They impose a -2 reaction penalty when interacting with non-beastmen or non-party members. Replace +2 damage bonus if a PC beastman's Strength bonus is greater than +2. When beastmen score a critical hit, the target must make a DC 15 Constitution check or be knocked prone ” this applies to small and medium targets. A beastman gets an attack of opportunity with advantage against a knocked-prone foe.

pages.title: Bugbear
pages.content: No. Enc: 2d4 (3d10) ¢ Alignment: Chaotic ¢ Movement: 30' ¢ Armor Class: 7 ¢ Hit Dice: 3+3 (typically 14-17 HP) ¢ BAB +4 ¢ Attacks: by weapon ¢ Damage: By single weapon attack (2d6) ¢ Save: F4 ¢ Morale: 10 ¢ Hoard: 2d6 chroma, 1d4-1 royals, 1d4+1 copper (25% it's Red Cuprous ) bugbear-optimized.png Anytime ten or more bugbears are found together, one of them will be a 4+3 HD specimen with 31 HP with 1d4+3 royals, 2d4+4 chroma, 1d4+4 copper (15% it's Red Cuprous ). This leader will have the same Morale and saving throws as its fellows. A defeated leader bugbear is worth 245 xp. Bugbears are disciplined combatants and particularly dangerous in groups. A bugbear can make a Flanking Strike up to three times daily. These creatures are born for battle and mayhem and that they bully those weaker than themselves. Bugbears are hairy humanoid creatures that are often tall and hulking. They are cousins of hobgoblins and goblins, yet bugbears love to enslave and bully them into giving them what they want. They are known to be unreliable allies and bloodthirsty monsters. They worship a lesser god called Hruggek, and they believe that when they die, their spirit will have a chance to fight alongside this deity. When they have no hobgoblins or goblins to bully around and enslave, they form loose warbands led by the fiercest bugbear in the pack. Also, despite their hulking presence, they are surprisingly stealthy. They love to ambush their victims yet flee when they think they are outmatched or outnumbered. They are dependable mercenaries when paid well but they know no loyalty when their life is on the line.

pages.title: Chargammon
pages.content: A powerful black dragon who lives in a great cavern beneath the redacted . Probably one of the five most powerful dragons.

pages.title: Couatl
pages.content: A couatl is a celestial creature with a Challenge Rating of 4, with a hit point range of 1,100 XP, an Armor Class of 15, and can use innate spellcasting abilities. It can attack with a bite that deals 1d6 + 5 piercing damage and has a constrict attack that deals 2d6 + 3 bludgeoning damage. couatl-celestial-optimized.webp Couatl Statistics General Information Attribute Value --- --- Challenge Rating 4 Hit Points 1,100 XP Armor Class 15 Attacks Attack Type Damage Additional Effects --- --- --- Bite 1d6 + 5 piercing - Constrict 2d6 + 3 bludgeoning Grapples target (escape DC 15) Special Abilities Innate Spellcasting: Can cast spells requiring only verbal components. Telepathy: Communicates with intelligent creatures within 120 feet. Magic Weapons: All weapon attacks are considered magical. These statistics highlight the couatl's capabilities in combat and its role as a celestial creature in gameplay.

pages.title: Dragon Turtle
pages.content: A gargantuan sea monster with high hit points and powerful attacks, including a bite and claws. It can also use a breath weapon that deals significant damage in a wide area. Dragon Turtle Stats in Old School Essentials (OSE) General Information Classification: Gargantuan sea monster Hit Points: High (exact value varies by edition) Armor Class: 20 (natural armor) Abilities Ability Value --- --- Strength 25 (+7) Dexterity 10 (+0) Constitution 20 (+5) Intelligence 10 (+0) Wisdom 12 (+1) Charisma 12 (+1) Attacks Multiattack: The dragon turtle can make three attacks: Bite: Attack Bonus: +13 to hit Damage: 26 (3d12 + 7) piercing damage Claw: Attack Bonus: +13 to hit Damage: 16 (2d8 + 7) slashing damage Tail: Attack Bonus: +13 to hit Damage: 26 (3d12 + 7) bludgeoning damage Special Abilities Breath Weapon: Type: Scalding steam Area: 60-foot cone Damage: 52 (15d6) fire damage (DC 18 Constitution saving throw for half damage) Recharge: 5â€6 (can be used three times per day) Movement Speed: Land: 20 ft. Swim: 40 ft. Additional Traits Amphibious: Can breathe air and water. Senses: Darkvision 120 ft., passive Perception 11. These stats make the dragon turtle a formidable opponent in any encounter, capable of dealing significant damage and with a strong defensive capability.

pages.title: Dragonbone Golem
pages.content: dragonboneGolem.webp No. Enc: 1 ¢ Alignment: Chaotic Evil ¢ Movement: 40' ¢ Armor Class: 2 ¢ Hit Dice: 14 (typically 120-140 HP) ¢ THAC0: 9 ¢ Attacks: 4 ¢ Damage: claw 1d6+4 (x2), bite 1d8+4, tail-lash 2d4+4 ¢ Special: harmed only by magic or magical weapons ¢ Special: resistance to slashing/piercing damage ¢ Damage: resist cold 5/fire 5/lightning 5/acid 5 ¢ Special: Petrifying Breath (every 3rd round) ¢ Save: F14 ¢ Morale: 13 Dragonbone golems are made from the bones of dead dragons. They are very loyal, dependable guardians for their masters. At the start of each round, a dragonbone golem regains 3 HP, unless it begins a round at less than a single HP. If damage is being dealt to the golem using Scarlet Heroes rules, consider 2 HD of previous damage to the golem to be undone as it starts each new round. Dragonbone golems don't check morale until they are down to 40 or fewer HP. There is a 90% chance that a dragonbone golem watches over 1d4+2 magic items and (2d8 x 1000) GP worth of coins and valuable objects.

pages.title: Froglings
pages.content: Occupying swamps, marshes, wetlands, mires, these small creatures are known for attacking individually superior foes when the froglings have at least 2:1 numerical superiority. froglingAttack.png Froglings are 1 HD small creatures, generally 12 to 18 inches in length. They have THAC0 of 20 but gain +1 when flanking or leaping at foes (+2 if both at once). Rumors are that these creatures are cannibalistic as well, but this hasn't been confirmed.

pages.title: Geppettin
pages.content: geppettin.webp ¢ No. Enc: you should hope just one... ¢ Alignment: Chaotic ¢ Movement: 20' ¢ Armor Class: 5 (small size and Dexterity) ¢ Hit Dice: 3+3 (typically 14-17 HP) or by PC level ¢ BAB +3 ¢ Attacks: by weapon or 1d2 ¢ Damage: By single weapon attack (1d4) ¢ Save: F4 ¢ Morale: 11 ¢ Hoard: 2d6 chroma, 1d4-1 royals, 1d4+1 copper (25% it's Red Cuprous ) Experience Yielded: 500 for an individual Geppettin Geppettin do not require food or drink. They do not sleep. They are +4 to save against mind-affecting effects. They are resistant to cold-based damage but suffer normal vulnerability to electrical, acid, and fire-based damage. Geppettin don't breathe; therefore, they are immune to gaseous attacks and drowning / suffocation. Geppettin do not blink. They just ... stare at you.

pages.title: Gnoll
pages.content: gnoll.webp No. Enc: 2d4 (3d10) ¢ Alignment: Chaotic ¢ Movement: 30' ¢ Armor Class: 7 ¢ Hit Dice: 2+1 (typically 10-13 HP) ¢ BAB +3 ¢ Attacks: by weapon ¢ Damage: By single weapon attack, +1 to damage ¢ Save: F3 ¢ Morale: 10 ¢ Hoard: 2d6 chroma, 1d4-1 royals, 1d4+1 copper (25% it's Red Cuprous ) Anytime ten or more gnolls are found together, one of them will be a 3+3 HD specimen with 21 HP with 1d4-1 royals, 2d4+4 chroma, 1d4+6 copper (25% it's Red Cuprous ). This leader will have the same Morale and saving throws as its fellows. A defeated leader gnoll is worth 325 xp.

pages.title: Goblin
pages.content: goblin.webp ¢ No. Enc: 2d4 (3d10) ¢ Alignment: Chaotic ¢ Movement: 30' ¢ Armor Class: 7 ¢ Hit Dice: 1-1 (typically 2-4 HP) ¢ BAB +0 ¢ Attacks: by weapon ¢ Damage: By single weapon attack, -1 to damage ¢ Save: F3 ¢ Morale: 10 ¢ Hoard: 2d6 chroma, 1d4-1 royals, 1d4+1 copper (35% it's Red Cuprous )

pages.title: Monster
pages.content: A creature, natural or supernatural, that is generally feared, and/or generally unwelcome. Monsters may be (but tend not to be) humanoids. They are often powerful combatants. Some have spells or spell-like abilities. Monsters generally pose a threat to travelers, hamlets, thorpes, and towns. Adventurers are sometimes hired to slay monsters that have become problematic. A monster may also be slain in order to use one or more of its parts for spell components or to catalyze certain rituals. Monsters can be NPCs; however, most NPCs are not monsters. An example of a very powerful surface monster is the Dragon Turtle. A similarly powerful monster in the Underdark is the Ulitharid. A dreadful monster that has made its way across worlds, even across crystal spheres, is the dreaded Phaerimm. A camel is not a monster, but it's rider might be. An octopus is a naturally occurring sea creature, though giant ones are monsters feared by sailors everywhere.

pages.title: Orc
pages.content: orc.webp No. Enc: 2d4 (3d10) ¢ Alignment: Chaotic ¢ Movement: 30' ¢ Armor Class: 7 ¢ Hit Dice: 3 (typically 17-20 HP) ¢ BAB +4 ¢ Attacks: 1 by weapon ¢ Damage: 2d4 + 2 ¢ Special: knock prone on natural 20 to-hit ¢ Save: F4 ¢ Morale: 9 ¢ Hoard: 5d4 chroma, 2d4+4 royals, 2d4+8 copper (30% it's Red Cuprous ) Orcs are brutes. They flee when reduced to 8 HP or fewer, if possible.

pages.title: Owlbear
pages.content: owlbear.png No. Enc: 1 ¢ Alignment: Neutral ¢ Movement: 30' ¢ Armor Class: 6 ¢ Hit Dice: 5 (typically 31-33 HP) ¢ BAB +5 ¢ Attacks: 2 (claw & beak) ¢ Damage: claws for 2d6, beak for 2d10 ¢ Save: F4 ¢ Morale: 10 ¢ Hoard: 1d6 chroma, 1d4 royals, 1d4 copper (15% it's Red Cuprous ) Owlbears have one claws swipe attack and one beak attack; if the claw attack hits, the beak auto-hits. An owlbear isn't a natural creature by a long-ago result of wizardry gone awry. Owlbears regenerate 1 hit point per round, or one full HD per six rounds.

pages.title: Phaerimm
pages.content: The Phaerimm are among the most terrifying and influential villains in the history of the Forgotten Realms. They are ancient aberrant spellcasters whose war against Netheril helped transform one of the greatest empires into ruin and contributed to the creation of the great desert of Anauroch. These creatures are highly magical and have infiltrated other worlds in addition to Faerun. Appearance Phaerimm are typically depicted as floating, cone-shaped aberrations with a central tooth-lined maw, multiple clawed limbs radiating from the upper body, and a long tapering tail. Their appearance is intentionally alien and unsettling, reflecting their role as ancient magical predators and enemies of Netheril. Keep in mind that official artwork has varied across editions of Dungeons & Dragons, so different artists portray them somewhat differently while retaining the core features: Levitating cone-shaped body Ring of clawed arms Large circular mouth Long stinger-like tail Powerful magical aura One of the most iconic depictions appears in the AD&D 2nd Edition sourcebook The Fall of Myth Drannor, where they are shown as bizarre floating horrors rather than dragon-like or humanoid creatures. A phaerimm resembles a floating, cone-shaped creature with: A circular, tooth-filled maw Several clawed arms surrounding its body A long, tapering tail ending in a stinger No obvious legs, as they levitate naturally Many observers describe them as looking like a horrifying cross between a jellyfish, a sunflower, and a giant magical grub. Why They Are Feared Phaerimm are not merely monsters; they are innately powerful spellcasters . Even young phaerimm possess magical abilities that rival accomplished wizards. They cast magic instinctively rather than through the traditional study and memorization used by most humanoid mages. Among their notable traits: Natural spellcasting Strong resistance to magic Ability to detect magical energies Exceptional intelligence Long lifespans Extreme hatred of most other intelligent races They are often described as cruel, arrogant, and sadistic. The Fall of Netheril The phaerimm are most famous for their conflict with the ancient empire of Netheril. Netheril was once a lush land of forests, rivers, and fertile plains ruled by extraordinarily powerful human archmages. As Netherese magic expanded, it began damaging the magical environment upon which the phaerimm depended. In retaliation, the phaerimm developed devastating "lifedrain" spells. These spells slowly drained vitality from the land itself. Over centuries, these magical assaults: Destroyed fertile farmland Turned forests into wasteland Forced migrations Helped create the vast desert known as Anauroch Although the famous collapse of Netheril is usually associated with the archwizard Karsus and his disastrous attempt to seize divine power, the phaerimm were instrumental in Netheril's long decline and the destruction of its remaining lowland territories. The Sharn and the Imprisonment of the Phaerimm The phaerimm became such a threat that powerful beings known as the Sharn (sometimes called "weave ghosts") eventually intervened. Using immense magical power, the Sharn imprisoned many phaerimm beneath Anauroch in magical prisons. For centuries, most of the race remained trapped underground. Some later escaped and appeared during various Forgotten Realms stories and sourcebooks. Origins Their exact origin has varied somewhat across editions and lore sources. Some sources suggest they were brought to Toril long ago by the ancient Imaskari empire, while others simply treat them as an ancient aberrant race that has existed beneath Faer»n since prehistoric times. The details have never been completely settled in canon. Using Phaerimm in a Campaign For a setting like your Scarlet Horizons world, phaerimm make excellent: Ancient buried masterminds Manipulators behind the fall of civilizations Mage-hunting horrors Creators of magical wastelands Imprisoned entities beneath forgotten ruins Secret enemies of wizardly orders such as Arcantryl A single adult phaerimm can function as a campaign-level villain. An elder phaerimm can threaten entire kingdoms.

pages.title: Skeleton
pages.content: skeleton.webp No. Enc: 2d4 (3d10) ¢ Alignment: Chaotic ¢ Movement: 30' ¢ Armor Class: 7 ¢ Hit Dice: 1+1 ¢ Number of Attacks: 1 ¢ Melee Damage: 1d6 ¢ Save: F2 ¢ Morale: 12 ¢ Hoard: 3d6 chroma, 2d4+5 royals, 2d4+4 copper (65% it's Red Cuprous ; otherwise, 45% it's Dark Cuprous ) Anytime ten or more skeletons are found together and fought together, when four or more have been defeated in a way that doesn't entirely vaporous their substance ” as when a cleric destroys undead ” there is a 25% chance those four will form into reborn one , a 4+3 HD specimen with 27 HP with the same treasure as other skeletons. Once per encounter, a cleric may target any undead within thirty feet of her position by showing her holy symbol and calling down the wrath of whatever power the cleric serves. Roll one d8 die per total core class Cleric levels the cleric possesses ” or one d8 die per (overall character levels divided by two, and rounded down) ” whichever is greater . Treat these like Fray Dice that can only target these particular undead. In the context of Scarlet Horizons , a turning attempt occurs when a non-evil cleric presents her holy symbol and pronounces anathema on undead within thirty feet of the cleric. This turning attempt is accompanied by a d20 roll and the Turn Undead table is consulted. For each type of undead present (i.e., within thirty feet of the cleric), cross-reference the full core-Cleric class levels of the cleric with the HD of that particular undead. If there isn't a table entry, the cleric isn't yet powerful enough to affect that undead. A numerical entry in the table means if your d20 result is that high or higher, that undead will move its maximum possible distance from you over the course of the next five rounds. A result of "T" means that particular undead is automatically turned and will stay as far from you as it can get for the duration of the encounter while you continue to display your holy symbol, given your power as a cleric; and a "D" result means the undead is utterly destroyed. A cleric gets a single turning attempt per undead entity per encounter and must make the attempt the very first round of the encounter. In subsequent rounds, a cleric may target undead that were not (T)urned or (D)estroyed by making a Fray Die attack up to thirty feet away each round against a particular undead entity, inflicting the Fray Die result as HD of radiant damage. Note that individual undead for which there isn't a result of (T) or (D) on the table may attack you after five rounds have elapsed, assuming your turn attempt was strong enough to make them temporarily flee in the first place. If a cleric opts to attempt to Turn Undead in the first round of an encounter in which one or more undead are present, she may not make a normal use of Fray Die in that round. For a round in which a cleric uses her Fray Die to inflict radiant damage against a particular undead entity, the cleric may not make a normal Fray Die use against another target.

pages.title: Tipsy
pages.content: One of two giant pack lizards the Phandelver campaign PCs recovered from an old abandoned mine in the foothills above Phandalin. Mate to Topsy. Apparently, the mine was being used by goblins and orcs whose intentions and purpose the PCs have not discovered.

pages.title: Topsy
pages.content: One of two giant pack lizards the Phandelver campaign PCs recovered from an old abandoned mine in the foothills above Phandalin. Mate to Tipsy. Apparently, the mine was being used by goblins and orcs whose intentions and purpose the PCs have not discovered. Topsy gave birth to seven lizards after the party moved her to their farm on the western outskirt of Phandalin.

pages.title: Troll
pages.content: troll.png No. Enc: 1 (2d3) Alignment: Chaotic Movement: 40' Armor Class: 5 Hit Dice: 12 (90-95 HP) BAB +10 Attacks: 3 claw/claw/bite, or 1 by weapon Damage: 2d6+4/2d6+4/1d6+4 Special: Keen Smell, Regeneration: 10 hp/round Save: F14 Morale: 10 Hoard: 6d4 chroma, 2d4+4 royals, 2d4+8 copper (50% it's Red Cuprous else 25% Dark)

pages.title: True Dragons
pages.content: When the Visitors came so many millennia ago, True Dragons were a servitor alien race that they brought with them. Practically immortal, magically adept, and physically imposing, these creatures are thought by modern Sages to be the predecessors of today's dragons. The designation 'true' alludes to the original alien DNA of these scaled servitors. Most modern dragons are the progeny, many generations removed, of creatures that the Visitors created in their experimentation with True Dragon DNA. It may be that a few Visitors and True Dragons still live to this day, though few are recorded in any ancient writings that have been found and translated. The most ancient texts refer to these True Dragons variously as The First Brood, The Blood Unmingled, and Those Who Remember The Stars.

pages.title: Wood Golem
pages.content: woodgolem.webp Wood golems have resistance to cold, electricity, acid, and piercing damage. These attacks do only half the rolled damage, rounded down, to a minimum of one point of damage. A wood golem's enchantment prevents it from decaying/rotting. These golems typically stand five feet in height and weigh about three hundred fifty pounds. A wood golem that is destroyed will slowly pull itself back together over the next two turns ” unless it received a majority of damage from a magical slashing/hacking weapon, magical fire, or was disintegrated . Alternatively, if dispel magic succeeds against the golem before, during, or immediately after combat, it will not reintegrate itself.

pages.title: Abbot Fornost d'Voivodja
pages.content: A Seeker cleric of the late first-century, early second-century PR.

pages.title: Algorn Druff
pages.content: algorn-druff.webp Algorn is a human witch-hunter operating in the Northern Reaches, usually within Middenmark. He and those of his order are Scyntarn, and constitute an important faction in the region. As a child, Algorn was imprisoned by an evil witch for seven years in the Red Thicket. The story of how he escaped her is one best told by bright firelight and after proper fortification with a beverage banned by the Red Laws.

pages.title: Ardan Hearthward, Sir
pages.content: A weather beaten man in patched mail, Sir Ardan tends the shrine as its wandering guardian. He is rarely seen in towns, preferring the quiet of the hills and the company of the shrine’s eternal flame. His duties are simple but sacred. Keep the brazier lit, offer shelter to travelers in need, and watch for threats that creep from the deeper wilds. ardan-hearthward.webp Ardan is courteous but reserved, speaking slowly not unusual for one who has spent many years alone. He knows the Blanryde Hills well every sheep path, every forgotten cairn, every place where the old gods still whisper. Those who earn his trust may find him a steadfast ally, especially in matters where hearth, family, or missing folk are concerned. Reputation & Rumors Farmers claim Ardan once drove off a band of orcspawn single handedly, though he never speaks of it. Travelers say the shrine’s fire burns hotter when danger is near. Some whisper that Demetra herself walks the hills at dusk, and Ardan has seen her more than once.

pages.title: Arford Shrewdbody
pages.content: An elderly gnome (well, half-gnome/half-halfling -- and yes , it is possible), proprietor and single employee of Arford's Mill in Eastdale.

pages.title: Auriochos d'Rosenberg
pages.content: A human cleric natively of Helix and a member of The Seekers. Slain by a gnoll arrow in the Fall of 204 PR. Slain when a gnoll's arrow pierced his left eye on Oct 25th.

pages.title: Banville Mask
pages.content: Keeper of the Heart Queen's pictures, accomplished thief, and an agent of the Order of the Gauntlet. It was Banville who provided Celaena Sardothien some Residuum with which to enchant her great sword. As an old man, Banville contracted a terminal wasting illness, but used a magical gemstone in his possession to transfer his consciousness into a clockwork Guardians' Rest. He has continued his existence in this way for decades. It is thought that he may be guild master of the Fire Blades.

pages.title: Bezarcane
pages.content: Surname unknown or perhaps lost to time, he is a half-elven sage (MAGE 17) who is a well-respected and highly placed member of the Order of the Gauntlet. It is believed that Bezarcane disguises himself or becomes invisible often, and so the phrase has arisen 'Bezarcane is watching'. Some say he is a double-agent, embedded in both the Order of the Gauntlet and The Zhentarim. Interestingly, those who say this don't survive very long. His ultimate agenda is unknown, and he may be in possession of ancient magic recovered from ruins the in the Forbidden Zone.

pages.title: Billworth Turgen
pages.content: Owner of Turgen's Trade Goods and local representative of the Silver Standard Caravan Company in Helix. Billworth facilitates shipments to Ironguard Motte and imports from the same. At 55 years old, Turgen is quite well-off financially. He's an unclassed expert merchant with 4 HP. He has a mustache, speaks in a bass voice, smokes a pipe, and is a likable fellow who just became a grandfather in the Spring of 203 PR. Merchant 4 Hp 4 Str 7 Dex 7 Con 10 Int 9 Wis 6 Cha 11 When traveling, Billworth is accompanied by his nephew Thurgan Newl, a 2nd level ranger, and his grandson, Berric, a 3rd level fighter. If traveling with one of his caravans, he will also have 1d4+4 guards that may be mercenaries or adventurers, or a mix of the two. He sources NPC guards from the Silver Standard Trading Company because they're well-trained. Sometimes, however, he will hire adventurers because they'll usually work for less pay.

pages.title: Borca Sintarn
pages.content: Name & Title: Borca, Veteran Class & Level: Fighter/1 XP: 0 Strength: 9 Intelligence: 9 Wisdom: 9 Dexterity: 9 Constitution: 9 Charisma: 9 Armour Class: 9 Hit Points: 1/1 Movement Rate: 120' (40') THACO: 19 Saving throws Death Ray or Poison: 12 Magic Wands: 13 Paralysis or Turn to Stone: 14 Dragon Breath: 15 Rods, Staves, or Spells: 16 Borca has leather armor and a mundane but serviceable bastard sword that he carries in a scabbard hung from his back, bandolier-style. He has tough leather boots, a sharp belt knife.

pages.title: Bran Hammerspike
pages.content: A dwarven warrior (109 PR-?) who, in the winter of 199 PR while helping Crynwyth Ironfist search for the Doors of Galduhr in the Moon Peaks, saved Crynwyth's life after she was badly hurt by a fire elemental.

pages.title: Brannock Tilden
pages.content: A human cleric of Oghma, he was the head of the Oghman temple in Helix from PR 197-208.

pages.title: Breanna Badmouth
pages.content: A 3'4" female Halfling farmer of the first century PR who sold her 10-acre farm on the western outskirts of Phandalin to the PCs and remained as overseer. She helped take care of Tipsy and Topsy when the PCs were out adventuring. Her last name is properly pronounced 'bah-mooth', but the locals ” mainly to tease Breanna ” pronounced it in a way that suggested the halfling used profanity and off-color humor. She didn't , at least not very often.

pages.title: Breldik Blackbeard
pages.content: A 6'4" man, 275 lbs and with a bushy black beard and very muscular physique (STR 18), Breldik was the lone blacksmith in Phandalin in the early first century PR. Breldik was married to Brenda Halfast, and they had a Saint Bernard named Big Ben.

pages.title: Brenda Halfast
pages.content: Wife of Breldik Blackbeard of Phandalin, Brenda was born 03 PR in Kirkilston, where she grew up the third child of a miner father and a barmaid mother.

pages.title: Bruce Bancroft
pages.content: Bruce "Beer-Brewer" Bancroft is the human proprietor on the Stonehill Inn in Phandalin. He sneers at the Red Laws' prohibition on drinking alcohol. Bruce has developed a friendship with the leader of the Inglorious Bastards, Maven Dursk, a human female thief. The fact that she is extremely comely may be a significant influence on this development. For Bruce, abstinence is a condition not to be tolerated.

pages.title: Bryce Lightstep
pages.content: Bryce was a ranger who lived in the vicinity of Phandalin from PR 12 to 48. It was rumored ” though not by many ” that Bryce is a member of the Harpers. Bryce is the many-times grandfather of Reglar Ashbow. Though Reglar is usually referred to The Ashbow, his surname nevertheless remains Lightstep.

pages.title: Celaena Sardothien
pages.content: A human fighter who operated in southeast Stigrix in PR 204 and forward. Celaena's companions were Feyre Archeron and Lancaster Fox.

pages.title: Cere-Lukh
pages.content: In 204 PR, a champion warrior of the Scarface goblins, Cere-Lukh is a brute of a goblin who enjoys the statistics of a bugbear with two levels in Barbarian. Cere-Lukh means Bloodletter in Goblin.

pages.title: Chucky
pages.content: A Geppettin warlock who serves as sidekick to the St. Yggian paladin, Whiteheart Stiffwhiskers in the early 200s PR. Whiteheart is deceased but Chucky yet endures...

pages.title: Crumwich Ironfist
pages.content: The king of Citadel Silver who financed the reclamation of the in 27 PR via the valiant Gauntwood Galleries, dwarven adventurer Xavamros Battlebeard I. This king championed efforts to reclaim the Golden Age of the dwarven kingdoms throughout his long life. In 201 PR, he began negotiations with the ruling council of the Gauntwood Galleries dwarves, seeking to put together an expedition to first recapture and then to map the vast ancient dwarven kingdom of Gundgathol.

pages.title: Crynwyth Ironfist
pages.content: Daughter of King Crumwich Ironfist of Citadel Silver. Crynwyth was a a powerful elementalist in her own right, though she found fewer opportunities to test her mettle in life than she'd have liked, given her protective liege and father. Crynwyth was 48 years old in PR 27. Those closest to her continued to call her by her childhood name, Crynwyn, until her death in PR 369.

pages.title: Devra Trueaim
pages.content: A human woman who has resided in Eastdale since PR 396 and who serves with the mercenaries operating out of this town. Could she in actuality be Demetra Kesloril, a Zhentarim agent, or at least a sympathizer?

pages.title: Elbramoth Battlebeard
pages.content: Second-born (by 1 minute: he and Xavamros Battlebeard III are twins) son of Xavamros Battlebeard II, King of the Gauntwood Galleries. He currently is waging a years-long campaign to retake ancient Golbrandur.

pages.title: Eldreth Moss-Walker
pages.content: Eldreth is the leader of The Sporebane Brotherhood. A druid of great power and wisdom, he has seen the destruction that the Soul Fungus can wreak firsthand and is determined to prevent its spread. His connection to the natural world allows him to sense the balance of life and death in the land, and he feels the pain of the infected earth deeply. eldreth-mosswalker.webp Eldreth is patient and pragmatic, understanding the magnitude of the task at hand. He realizes that the battle against the Soul Fungus is one that the Brotherhood might not win, but he believes that as long as they fight, there is hope. ""Nature's balance teeters on a precarious edge, and the Soul Fungus threatens to tip it into oblivion. We fight not for victory, but for the chance to restore harmony to this land." Eldrith shares leadership with Elowen Starshadow.

pages.title: Elowen Starshadow
pages.content: Background: Elowen is a young and promising wizard within the Sporebane Brotherhood. She hails from a lineage of skilled arcane practitioners and has dedicated her talents to the Brotherhood's cause. Appearance: With raven-black hair cascading in waves down her back and striking emerald eyes, Elowen possesses an ethereal beauty that belies her fierce determination. She wears the robes of the Brotherhood, adorned with intricate green and silver embroidery, signifying her commitment to nature's balance. elowen-starshadow.webp Personality: Elowen is inquisitive, quick-witted, and possesses a thirst for knowledge that rivals her magical prowess. Despite her youth, she carries herself with a sense of maturity and responsibility beyond her years, understanding the gravity of the Soul Fungus threat. Magical Abilities: Elowen is a gifted spellcaster, specializing in the manipulation of elemental forces and protective spells. Her magical abilities are a crucial asset to the Brotherhood, whether it's creating magical barriers to contain the Soul Fungus or harnessing the power of nature to cleanse corrupted areas. Motivation: Elowen's motivation to join the Brotherhood stems from a personal tragedy. Her beloved mentor, a wise druid, fell victim to the Soul Fungus during an expedition to study its effects. Elowen vowed to honor her mentor's memory by using her arcane talents to combat the plague and prevent others from suffering a similar fate. Role within the Brotherhood: As a young wizard, Elowen plays a pivotal role in the Brotherhood's research efforts. She is responsible for deciphering ancient texts, studying fungal samples, and collaborating with the other members to develop magical solutions to contain and combat the Soul Fungus. Her optimism and unwavering dedication inspire those around her, reminding them that even in the darkest of times, there is hope.

pages.title: Exodore Swift
pages.content: Exodore (ecks-uh-DOOR-ay) Swift (PR 376-402) ” traveling companion and lover of Deornoth Stelgaard. A petite fighter-rogue, Exie was a troubled teen. At age 18 she joined the Blackfists Mercenaries out of Prelm. She was killed at age 26 by beastmen in Arden Vul.

pages.title: Faramund Beckette
pages.content: The fourth son of minor baron of southern Hohnberg, Faramund joined his Uncle Ulred's mercenary band, The Felicitously Forsworn, at the age of seventeen, squiring for his uncle and building experience. Now, at the age of twenty, he has traveled to the region of Locations/Stigrix in the Westmark, seeking a former superior officer to his uncle.

pages.title: Felix Villafreud
pages.content: PR 368-? The ranking cleric of Imperiosa in the Northern Reaches, Father Villafreud resides in Helix. From there, he manages a group of 'problem solvers' known as the Fist of Felix. These five individuals, three of them clerics of Imperiosa, are generally lawful, but vary on the continuum between good and evil. As a group, they lean toward the latter. Nevertheless, they are effective and sometimes have come to the aid of the Seekers.

pages.title: Fenwick Sedgewater
pages.content: Fenwick was a young man in his early twenties, and an initiate of the Seekers who joined the order in PR 199. He came from a noble family in the Hohnberg Pact, and so possessed wealth ” though he was never ostentatious. He seemed to be trying to atone for some real or imagined transgression, and made of himself a general dogs body to everyone else at the Chapterhouse.

pages.title: Festivus Chrahl
pages.content: Born PR 375, this half-elven bard who travels a circuit from Threshold, to Seven Cities, to Sizemordicus, then back to Threshold ” also performing in smaller towns along that route when in between those three large cities.

pages.title: Feyre Archeron
pages.content: A red-headed female elf (a rarity) who is a magic-user operating in the southeastern Locations/Stigrix area, in the vicinity of Middenmark and Slaytonthorpe from 19 to 37 PR. Feyre was a member of the Phandalin Three.

pages.title: Garrick Ironmane
pages.content: A dwarf trade representative based in Eastdale to represent Citadel Silver. He oversees trade caravans and can supply armor, dwarven arms, and basic adventuring equipment.

pages.title: Gaston Fellshroud
pages.content: The middle-aged gnome proprietor ” and retired adventurer ” of the Griffon's Tongue pub and diner in Eastdale. It's rumored that Gaston wears a magical cape that magically slays anyone who inflicts injury upon its wearer.

pages.title: Ghirandiahn
pages.content: A bronze dragon warlock pledged to Anu-eya, a former greater god believed by some to still possess deific status but choosing to grant warlock spells as a patron.

pages.title: Gintarn Khalidson
pages.content: A dwarven adventurer and member of the The Felicitously Forsworn in the early Post-Ravaging decades. Gintarn died in PR 153.

pages.title: Golnadeg Grue-Spitter
pages.content: Golnadeg Grue-Spitter ” a Shou witch-priestess slain in PR 20 by Kurg Blacktooth on the site that would later contain Blacktooth Keep.

pages.title: Grant Caddyshanks
pages.content: An elderly human farmer (PR 172-263) who now lived in a farmhouse, kept a few chickens, and only rarely ventured to Smokeshadow for supplies. More often, he relied on the once- or twice-monthly visits of Caravan Master Earnest Thromb. Thromb brought the old geezer supplies and news, and Caddyshanks paid with jars of moonshine and often news of his own pertaining to the happenings in a ten-mile radius.

pages.title: Grashnak One-Eye
pages.content: Grashnak, known to his underlings as Red-Tusk, has realized that open warfare against humans is costly and prefers to profit from Ranchefus's growing influence. He provides warriors and scouts in exchange for weapons, slaves, and promises of territory once civilization collapses. His base of operations lies in the old abandoned Gnarlstone Mines in the Blanryde Hills.

pages.title: Gursk Spiritspeaker
pages.content: The shaman of the Scarface goblin tribe that resides south of Helix at the edges of the bog. This isn't the original Gursk Spiritspeaker; he is many goblin generations removed from his spiritual forebear. The witch Nuanda Nemere has predicted that the modern Gursk will have a pivotal role to play in events that will shake both the Northern and Southern Reaches. In the second decade of the first century PR, Gursk predicted the zhou'kast of his people, if the undead boiling out of the Barrowmaze were not soon checked.

pages.title: Helegath Aerengard
pages.content: The Threshold noble (PR 177-214) whose abuses sparked off the Commoner Rebellion in PR 210.

pages.title: Hourby Minutos
pages.content: Human owner and proprietor of the Brazen Strumpet inn and tavern in Helix. Innkeep 3 January 03, PR 376 - ? Hp 1 AC 9 Str 6 Dex 7 Con 8 Int 7 Wis 9 Cha 9

pages.title: Hurg Scarface
pages.content: Chief of the Scarface Goblin tribe, in the first century PR, that resided south of Helix at the edges of the bog.

pages.title: Inzeldrin
pages.content: As of 406 PR, an ancient green dragon that resides in Shrieken Mire, in Slaytonthorpe.

pages.title: Jacobus Macman
pages.content: A well-to-do farmer in Thicket-thorpe who is a friend of Maelin Vey, the ranger Kuiper, and others in the area. He treated the heroes of the Seekers of the Lost band to a lavish breakfast late on the morning of May 10, 406 PR. jacobus-macman-full-size.webp

pages.title: Jelenneth Laneworth
pages.content: Jelenneth is the young teen daughter of farmers Parker and Heldrith Laneworth, whose farm lies northwest of Kirkilston. Jelenneth was abducted April 27th, 406 PR. On May 06th, the PCs visited Nuanda Nemere at her cottage in the forest. They spent the night, and on the morning of May 07, 604, the witch -- having visited the Dream Time while wearing a glove of Jelenneth's -- was able to relatively pinpoint the girl's location to within the past eight to ten hours. jelenneth.webp The party returned to Kirkilston on May 7th after overnighting with Nuanda Nemere, 10 days after Jelenneth's abduction. The Kirkilston Crew then joined a caravan as guards and, after some unfortunate encounters, arrived in Raven's Pass early on May 8th, 11 days after Jelenneth's disappearance. On the morning of May 9th, 12 days after the girl's disappearance, they left The Mason's Apron with additional companions, entering the Red Thicket and heading west from Raven's Pass.

pages.title: Jorun Fielenghast
pages.content: Nephew to Lord Falsta, a powerful figure in Prelm City from PR 240-258.

pages.title: Karg Barrelgut
pages.content: The blacksmith, armourer, and weaponsmith for the village of Helix. He is well-liked, honest, and hard-working. He is not comfortable talking about his past. There is a rumor he fled something in his youth back east in the Stonelands.

pages.title: Kelda Rue
pages.content: Grand Magus of Arcantryl at the Temple of the Seven Stars in Eastdale. The temple is the largest Arcantryl church outside Threshold, with a library that attracts scholars and mages. Kelda oversees low-level priest/mage-priests and stands as a softer counterweight to St. Ygg's harsher religious order. Class & Level: Magic-User 9 Alignment: Lawful Neutral Race: Human Experience Points: 25,000+ (approx. level 9) Hit Points: 31 (rolled 4d4 + 9 for Constitution bonus) Armor Class: 7 (robe + minor protective wards) THAC0: 18 Movement: 120 / 24 Saves: vs. Death/Poison: 9 vs. Magic Wands: 11 vs. Paralysis/Polymorph: 12 vs. Breath Weapons: 14 vs. Spells: 13 Abilities: Strength: 10 Dexterity: 12 Constitution: 13 Intelligence: 18 (+1d4 extra spells) Wisdom: 16 Charisma: 15 Special Abilities / Features: Arcane Spellcasting: Knows all 1stâ€5th level Magic-User spells available at level 9. Temple Authority: Commands respect within the Temple of Arcantryl; may call upon acolytes, magical wards, and temple resources. Ritual Expertise: Can perform complex magical rituals, including divination and planar wards. Artifact Knowledge: Highly familiar with Arcantryl relics and enchanted objects. Equipment / Magical Items: Staff of Arcantryl (focus for spellcasting; grants +1 to casting and as a quarterstaff) Robe of Protection +1 (AC bonus and resistance to minor magical effects) Ring of Sustenance (does not require food or water) Spellbook with 1stâ€5th level spells fully recorded (protected by magical wards) Component pouch, ceremonial dagger, ink, and parchment 120 gp (temple stipend) Spells Prepared (example 9th-level MU): 1st Level: Magic Missile, Shield, Read Magic, Detect Magic, Sleep 2nd Level: Invisibility, Knock, Mirror Image, Web 3rd Level: Fireball, Dispel Magic, Haste, Lightning Bolt 4th Level: Confusion, Greater Invisibility, Stoneskin, Polymorph Other 5th Level: Teleport, Wall of Force, Dominate Person, Cone of Cold Personality: Stern but fair, Kelda Rue emphasizes logic, discipline, and study. She values knowledge and order above all, but is deeply committed to the protection of Arcantryl's secrets. She rarely shows impatience, but those who defy temple law or misuse magic risk swift reprimand. Known for mentoring promising apprentices and occasionally sending them on dangerous quests to test skill and loyalty. Background / Roleplaying Notes: Grand Magus of the Temple of Arcantryl in Eastdale, responsible for magical research, temple defenses, and the education of acolytes. Acts as a political and arcane advisor to Eastdale's leadership. Can provide quests or magical guidance to adventurers, but tests character and moral alignment before granting aid.

pages.title: Kier Anthelm
pages.content: kier-anthelm.png 1st-Level Loremaster Bard (OSE Variant) XP: 0 / 2,500 Ability Score Modifier Strength 9 ” Intelligence 15 +1 Wisdom 10 ” Dexterity 12 ” Constitution 11 ” Charisma 13 +1 Class: Loremaster Bard (OSE Variant) Prime Requisites: Intelligence & Charisma Alignment: Lawful Hit Points: 5 hp Armor Class: 14 (Chainmail + Shield) Combat Attack Progression: As Cleric Weapons: Short sword Dagger Staff Short bow Armor: Chainmail & Shield Saving Throws (As Cleric 1): Save Target Death / Poison 11 Wands 12 Paralysis / Petrify 14 Dragon Breath 16 Rods / Staves / Spells 15 Class Abilities: Lore, Saga of Heroes, Tongues & Scripts Lore - Kier may attempt to identify: ancient ruins heraldry relics magical inscriptions forgotten cultures monsters historical events Chance of Success: 2-in-6 Saga of Heroes : Once per day, Kier may recite heroic lays and ancient sagas. All allies within earshot gain: +1 morale, +1 saving throws vs fear Duration: one encounter or one exploration turn Tongues & Scripts Kier begins literate and knows: Common Old Helvecian Trade Cant of Brine May attempt to decipher unknown writing: 2-in-6 chance Equipment: Weathered chronicles of St. Ygg Rune-carved ash staff Chainmail hauberk Shield bearing a faded silver tree sigil Short sword Bone flute Horn lantern Ancient regional maps Satchel with parchment, ink, charcoal sticks, and sealing wax Travelers cloak lined with wolf fur 14 gp Spells: Identify, Read Magic Background: Kier Anthelm was raised among the fading monasteries near the northern marches of Middenmark, where the old songs of saints and kings are still whispered beside cold hearthfires. As a youth, he copied fragments of pre-Futurus chronicles salvaged from ruined abbeys and plague-haunted keeps. His wandering studies eventually led him into the wild roads of the Northern Reaches, where he now seeks forbidden histories tied to the Soul Fungus, the ruined Helvecians, and the forgotten dead beneath the Barrowmoor. Though welcomed in many halls for his learning and calm demeanor, Kiers habit of uncovering uncomfortable truths has earned him wary looks from priests, bannermen, and nobles alike. He believes memory itself is sacred”and that buried truths inevitably return.

pages.title: Kruger Gullby
pages.content: Abbot of the Middenmark, answerable to the Prelate, Mordicar Justhand.

pages.title: Kurg Blacktooth
pages.content: The half-orc Ranger (-29 PR to 28 PR) who is credited with slaying the Shou witch-priestess Golnadeg Grue-Spitter and her elite bugbear unit, putting an end to the swath of destruction they had carved through Smokeshadow, Dolecherry, and Silent Diamond.

pages.title: Lacklund Parlfried
pages.content: Killed by the 12-headed hydra in the Great Rock Dale, Slaytonthorpe, in 20 PR.

pages.title: Lancaster Fox
pages.content: A halfling thief who, at age 22, felt wisdom the better part of valor and left Seven Cities by cover of night and in some haste. He worked the southeastern portion of the region of Locations/Stigrix over the next few years, eventually forming an adventuring band with the elven mage Feyre Archeron and the human fighter Celaena Sardothien. Lanky was a persuasive and likable rogue.

pages.title: Livy Dapplestaff
pages.content: Livy Dapplestaff was intended to be a gnome PC but the player withdrew before entering IC play Class: Thief 1 Race: Gnome Alignment: Neutral Title: HP: AC: Stats STR: 8 (-1 Melee, Open Doors on 1/6) INT: 13 (+1 Language, Literate) WIS: 6 (-1 Magic Saves) DEX: 13 (+1 AC, +1 Missile, +1 Initiative) CON: 11 (+0 HP) CHA: 9 (+0 Reaction, 4 Retainers, Loyalty 7) Abilities Defensive Bonus: Due to their small size, gnomes gain a +2 bonus to Armour Class when attacked by large opponents (greater than human-sized). Detect Constructions Tricks: As expert tunnellers, gnomes have a 2-in-6 chance of being able to detect new construction, sliding walls, or sloping passages when searching. Infravision : Gnomes have infravision to 90. Listen at Doors: Gnomes have a 2-in-6 chance of hearing noises.

pages.title: Maelin Vey
pages.content: Str 5 Dex 9 Con 10 Int 16 Wis 13 Cha 14 A scholar of ancient languages with the Hûl Hildresu, and wife of Hurlon Vey of Vey Valley Station. maelin-vey.webp

pages.title: Magen Eisenthrast
pages.content: An accomplished mage who commanded a position of respect in the Seekers Chapterhouse in Helix to which Auriochos d'Rosenberg and Matthias D'Slaytonthorpe belonged in the first half of the first century Post-Ravaging.

pages.title: Malaster Rendalis
pages.content: The proprietor of a well-known adventurer supply company based in Eastdale. Most of the goods sold in Malaster's are originally sourced from Tien Lung, Threshold, Sizemordicus, or Seven Cities. I addition to running an emporium catering to adventurers, Malaster also sells mounts and carts, potions, maps, even some scrolls. Of course, he charges top dollar.

pages.title: Malvik the Mad
pages.content: In the forest north of Raven's Pass, not too far from the road, but far enough, lies Malvik's Tower. It was built by Malvik the Mad, a mage of fantastical power, several hundred years ago. malvik-the-mad.webp Long abandoned, it has not been discovered in many a year, as the only adventurers to find it never returned to tell the tale. It is rumored the tower is in the forest east of the trail and that it lies on top of a vast dungeon. The stories are very old, from the time of Malvik himself. According to stories, treasure and magic lie unclaimed in the dungeons, but protected, possibly, by Malvik's lich. Who knows what is true and what isn't? Malvik the Mad was a powerful necromancer 600 years ago or more. He had been discovered raising the dead in Helix and was forced to flee for his life lest they put him to death. He fled east into the Red Thicket. He wandered for a bit, then, finding a suitable spot near a trail through the forest, he established a tower to continue his studies into undeath! As he was not too near, but close enough he could acquire bodies, or make his own from unsuspecting travelers, he gained knowledge and power. After more than two decades, after carving out extensive dungeons using his minions, he finally realized his dream! He moved into undeath himself, that he might live on forever, seeking even more knowledge and power! Over the years, he went further and further into insanity, sinking deeper into depravity! Somewhere in those dungeons lies a vast trove of gold and magic, but can anyone ever live to claim even a portion of it? For it is guarded by the mad lich and his undead minions! contributed 06.20.2026 by player Maximilian Yragerne, who plays PC Maximilian Yragerne

pages.title: Matthias D'Slaytonthorpe
pages.content: A scholar-mage of the first century Post-Ravaging who belonged to the Seekers in Helix, Locations/Stigrix, in the Principality of Brine. Matthias was Nabblat to the Scarface Goblins.

pages.title: Maven Dursk
pages.content: The female human leader of the Inglorious Bastards, a group that was banned from Eastdale by Sir Chevae Thrace in 399 PR. There seems to be a friendship developing between Maven and Bruce Bancroft, a tavern/inn owner in Phandalin. He is the proprietor of the Stonehill Inn. Maven is a weasel in the hen-house, if there ever was one.

pages.title: Melgarith
pages.content: A medusan witch of the deep Darkforest who has reputedly melded herself with a 7-headed hydra.

pages.title: Mentos Ilthracin
pages.content: An illithid merchant of the first century PR who also acted as a mercenary with ties to Shallowtown and subduing Surface races into Underdark slavery. Lancaster Fox was one of Mentos' contacts.

pages.title: Morgan Canden
pages.content: Morgan Maynard Canden is the proprietor of Morgan's Morsels in Kirkilston, formerly known as Morgan's Morsels & Tankards but '& Tankards' has been painted over after repeated excoriations from clerics and paladins of St. Ygg. morgan-canden-kirkilston-innkeep.png Human male, age 44 Innkeep 2 Fighter 1 Hp 2 Str 6 Dex 6 Con 9 Int 8 Wis 7 Cha 10

pages.title: Muirron the Magician
pages.content: An arcane scholar interested in Archaians, Archomancy, spellbooks, scrolls, and ancient lore. He is a useful patron for dungeon delvers returning from Archaia with magical writings or inscriptions. Muirron can be found 60% of the time in Ironguard Motte, 35% of the time in Eastdale, and the other 5% of the time traveling with a caravan or bodyguards. Muirron Artelba is a former adventurer who pivoted into the role of collector and sage after a few modest successes in the 590s PR with a band styling themselves the Men of the Motte .

pages.title: Nimba Armstrong
pages.content: Wife to Samuel Armstrong, proprietor of The Broken Hilt. Also, sister to Nuanda Nemere. Nimba runs The Mason's Apron. Nimba.webp While Nuanda operates more overtly in the realm of the strange and occult, Nimba has chosen a life of deep cover. The hustle and bustle of The Mason's Apron is the perfect camouflage. Born into the Nemere line, Nimba and Nuanda share a bloodline touched by ancient, perhaps forbidden, traditions. While Nuanda became a seeker of raw magical components and ancient rites, Nimba realized that the best place to gather secrets, influence events, and protect her family's interests was from behind a counter where everyone lowers their guard. She moved to Raven's Pass, integrated herself perfectly as a local fixture, and uses the sensory overload of a tavern—the sizzling grease, the clinking mugs, the rowdy miners or guards—to mask her pages.title: Nolo Silvershaper
pages.content: A dwarf of Citadel Silver who wants the Keep on the Borderlands retaken from the humanoids infesting it. Nolo believes that the keep is built atop the entrance to an ancient dwarf hold.

pages.title: Nuanda Nemere
pages.content: Level 5 NPC Witch System: Old-School Essentials Alignment: Chaotic Class Basis: Witch treated as a spellcasting NPC similar to a Magic-User, with occult flavor Constitution: 12, no HP adjustment --- Ability Scores Ability Score Modifier --- --- --- Strength 8 -1 Intelligence 16 +2 Wisdom 15 +1 Dexterity 10 +0 Constitution 12 +0 Charisma 11 +0 --- Combat Stat Value --- --- Armor Class 9 [10] Hit Dice 5d4 Hit Points 14 THAC0 19 [+0] Attacks Dagger or spell Damage 1d4 dagger Movement 120 / 40 Morale 8 Save As Magic-User 5 --- Saving Throws Save Target --- --- Death / Poison 13 Wands 14 Paralysis / Petrify 13 Breath Attacks 16 Spells / Rods / Staves 15 --- Spells Prepared 1st Level Charm Person Detect Magic Sleep 2nd Level Invisibility Phantasmal Force 3rd Level Hold Person --- Witch Abilities Familiar: Nuanda is accompanied by a black cat named Morrow , which serves as her familiar and omen-beast. Morrow has 3 HP, AC 7 {12}, Move 150 / 50, and excellent hearing. If slain, Nuanda suffers a -1 penalty to saving throws for 1 week. Evil Eye: Once per day, Nuanda may curse one visible creature within 60. The target must save vs Spells or suffer -2 to attack rolls and saving throws for 1 turn. Herbal Hexcraft: Given 1 turn and access to her satchel, Nuanda may prepare a minor folk remedy, sleeping draught, warding charm, or bitter poison. These are not instantaneous combat powers unless prepared beforehand. Ritual Magic: Nuanda can perform non-combat rituals involving curses, divination, spirit-binding, or weather omens. These require time, materials, and referee adjudication. Stone Step : Once per fortnight, Nuanda may vanish from her current location on this material plane and reappear next to the dolmens of the henge which is located in the Forbidden Zone. Take Hengeange : After twenty years of study, Nuanda has developed the ability to call upon the nearest Henge, located in the Forbidden Zone. Once daily she may draw upon the ancient magic of the henge to drop a living, breathing foe to 1d4 remaining hit points; if the victim saves versus spell they instead suffer only 1d4 damage. Nuanda has a sister, Nimba Armstrong of Raven's Pass. --- Equipment Blackthorn wand Iron dagger Bone-handled ritual knife Pouch of grave salt Small mirror of polished black glass Bundle of dried herbs Witch-bottle containing hair, pins, and ash Spellbook wrapped in oilcloth 45 gp in mixed coin Silver charm worth 30 gp --- Personality Nuanda Nemere is quiet, watchful, and unnervingly polite. She speaks as though she already knows what others are about to say. She rarely threatens directly, preferring hints, omens, and unsettling bargains. She has a special hatred for oathbreakers and those who harm children, animals, or the helpless. --- Appearance Nuanda is a pale, dark-haired woman in her late thirties or early forties, usually dressed in layered black and moss-green garments. Her eyes are sharp gray, and her fingers are stained from herbs, ink, and ritual ash. She carries the scent of damp earth, smoke, and lavender. witch-nemere-cartoon.webp --- Roleplaying Notes Nuanda may serve as a dangerous village wise-woman, hidden patron, minor antagonist, source of forbidden knowledge, or morally ambiguous protector of an isolated community. She prefers payment in secrets, old bones, rare herbs, names of the dead, or favors owed.

pages.title: Olophorn Eld
pages.content: The 21-year old brother of the Eld Brothers, Olophorn was slain 25th Oct. 204 PR in battle.

pages.title: Orlogast Highsember
pages.content: A powerful yuan-ti mage posing as a librarian, sage, and researcher working from within the Red Temple in Eastdale. The Zhentarim believe him to be a spy for the prelate.

pages.title: Orvair Leonas
pages.content: The quarter-orc baron (PR 378-?) of Caldamis located in the southeastern Southern Reaches. There are at least two sages whose research has led them to believe that Orvair has Sarrukh -- perhaps even Visitor blood flowing in his veins, and that his true birth occurred early in the Cumerian Age. These two sages are extremely careful with whom they choose to share this speculation.

pages.title: Othar Dellen
pages.content: A 5th level cleric of St. Ygg who cares for the Spiral Shrine in the village of Helix.

pages.title: Quelline Alderleaf
pages.content: Quelline (PR 178-226) was half-sister to the halfling Breanna Badmouth, Quelline and her sister shared farming as an occupation. Quelline managed the ten-acre farm west of Phandalin purchased by the Phandalin Three in PR 204.

pages.title: Radloc Hudson
pages.content: A veteran warrior and founder of Hudson's Grey Company , the Eastdale mercenary guild. His company works as caravan guards and sometimes reinforces the towns defenders. Radloc Hudson is less a merchant himself and more the security broker for Eastdale commerce. Given that Hudson's Grey Company guards caravans and reinforces town defenses, Hudson sits at the intersection of merchants, clergy, dwarven trade, and criminal pressure in the Northern Reaches. Mordicar is the real power in Eastdale, even though the merchant guild heads supposedly form the ruling council. Radloc's company needs Mordicars approval to operate openly. Mordicar Justhand uses Hudson's Grey Company for lawful caravan protection, militia reinforcement, and discreet muscle against bandits or black-market routes. Garrick Ironmane represents Citadel Silver in Eastdale and oversees dwarven trade caravans. Since Citadel Silver trades almost exclusively through Eastdale, Radloc often provides guards, contract veterans, or emergency escorts for Garricks shipments of ore, arms, armor, and finished dwarven goods. Someone secretly runs The Darkeyes thieves guild, which profits from contraband created by the Red Laws. Radloc's mercenary guild protects warehouses, caravans, and hiring yards, so Radloc naturally interfere with theft, smuggling, and intimidation. It may be the case that The Darkeyes bribe some Grey Company guards, but Radloc himself is likely an obstacle. Zistrus of Guardians' Rest runs a fortified caravan station and has become wealthy enough to anger The Darkeyes. Radloc may value Guardians' Rest as a secure route asset, but also resents Zistrus drawing protection money, contracts, and influence away from Eastdale-based mercenary services.

pages.title: Rafell Riverwarden d'Helix
pages.content: A fifty year-old expert human (169-227 PR residing in the Seekers' Chapterhouse in Helix, and serving as their quartermaster as well as head of their Antiquities Research division. Rafell is credited with discovery of the Mythalvane in 193 PR ” an ancient and powerful magical item that helps protect Helix in ways of which no villagers and even very few Seekers brethren comprehend.

pages.title: Rengar the Bold
pages.content: A fighter who hails from Sizemordicus and who sometimes works as a mercenary out of Eastdale. This is the man that Matthias D'Slaytonthorpe hired to help train his as a warrior.

pages.title: Retep Garnetstone
pages.content: The proprietor of Reteps Relics and secretly guildmaster of the Darkeyes , the thieves guild of Eastdale/Middenmark. He deals in antiquities and precious-metal objects, but his shop fronts for the underground network that profits from the Red Laws by moving alcohol, gambling, prostitution, and discreet passage through the sewers. Mordicar Justhand is no fool, nor is his spy network ineffectual. He knows of this black market and directs considerable resources toward finding its mastermind.

pages.title: Revole Ting
pages.content: Known in most circles as Earnest Thromb, Revole is now no longer entirely just a halfling, as his mutated arm attests, notwithstanding the fact that he keeps it hidden by wearing a tough and serviceable canvas long-sleeved jacket when he is among gentlefolk. It isn't known whether Revole has survived into the fifth century PR. No normal halfling could do so, but Revole isn't normal...

pages.title: Rogier Van Der Weyden
pages.content: The Father-Abbot of the Seekers in PR 27, in their chapterhouse at Helix. Rogier passed away in PR 58.

pages.title: Sagius Nithrexus
pages.content: Thought to be a spy for the Prelate in Eastdale, Sagius appears to be a human who sells his services as a scribe and herbalist.

pages.title: Sirac Silverhair
pages.content: An elven fighter well into his second century of life, Sirac is something of a constable and all-around problem-solver in Phandalin. He is a seventh-level fighter with 43 HP. He wears elven chainmail +2 which ” with his Dexterity bonus ” gives him AC 0. He bears a Mithrilantine long sword named Astaldo . It is a +1 weapon, +3 versus humanoids. With this sword, Sirac enjoys a modified THAC0 of 12 (10 vs humanoids).

pages.title: Talyan Querdi
pages.content: A half-elven ranger slain by lizardmen in the Misty Mire, Slaytonthorpe, in 22 PR.

pages.title: Tauste
pages.content: A mage who lives in a tower in the community of Wizard's Tower, southwest of Dolecherry in the Farground Expanse. Tauste claims to be 800 years old; it might be true. Tauste's tower stands in Wizard's Tower but also in Slaytonthorpe just on the northeastern edge of Milborne. Tauste can walk through any doorway in his tower and the room he arrives in will be located in either his tower in Wizard's Tower or in Slaytonthorpe, whichever he chooses. In this sense, his entire tower is a Gate, or can be thought of as an instant teleporter. However, the truth is that Tauste exists fully in each tower at the same time. Tauste claims to have lived in his tower for over three centuries. Sure enough, the articles of incorporation for the town of Milborne make reference to the wizard, and those articles were drawn up in PR 312. Rumors have it that Tauste has rediscovered the process of manufacturing Plast. Sure enough, two Plast breastplates are known to be in circulation. Stronger and more damage resistant than any material other than Mithrilantine, these breastplates weigh only one-tenth of what their standard metallic counterparts weigh, and they are buoyant.

pages.title: Thad Clovenshield
pages.content: A dwarven warrior slain in the winter of 199 PR while helping Crynwyth Ironfist search for the Doors of Galduhr in the Moon Peaks.

pages.title: Thalas
pages.content: The High Priest of Thoth. He is the supreme authority within the enclave and is primarily focused on the restoration of ancient knowledge and the maintenance of the Great Library.

pages.title: The Elder Stranger
pages.content: The tree is called Vaelathuun , though among local woodsfolk it is more commonly known as the Elder Stranger . Vaelathuun is unlike any other tree in the Red Thicket. Its vast, iron-gray trunk is deeply fluted rather than conventionally barked, and its roots descend so far beneath the forest that some sages believe they penetrate into strata laid down before the present age of the world. Its narrow, dark crimson leaves contain branching veins that faintly luminesce under starlight. Throiki fragments translate Vaelathuun approximately as “That Which Remembers the First Sky.” This has fueled the old claim that the tree did not originate in this world at all. According to the story, the Throiki transported a living sapling here more than 800,000 years ago , perhaps as a botanical specimen, perhaps as part of an experiment, or perhaps because the tree itself possessed some property they considered important. The most disturbing version of the legend maintains that Vaelathuun was already ancient when the Throiki brought it here . No one has ever successfully counted its rings. A boring taken from the trunk supposedly produced neither recognizable growth rings nor sap—but a translucent black fluid that hardened into something resembling smoky glass. And despite its enormous age, Vaelathuun is still growing .

pages.title: The Sitarns
pages.content: A trio comprised of a sister and two brothers -- Velordra, Borca, and Corba, a mage of sorts, a fighter, and an archer, respectively.

pages.title: Thelgarr Blackstaff
pages.content: Thelgarr Blackstaff, Arch-Mage, Grand Magus and Demithuerge of Arcantryl, founded the Temple of the Seven Stars in Eastdale 103 years ago. As the High Priest of the temple, Thelgarr lead the faithful for 87 years, a leader in learning, education, and a researcher unparalleled in his era. He built a massive library of knowledge and had a grand laboratory at the peak of the East Tower. He was a chief advisor of the realm and aided in the education of the youth of the city. In his time, Thelgarr tutored many aspiring mages and priests for Arcantryl, none more promising than his last apprentice, Kelda Rue. She aided him in his research and studies for seven years, fine tuning her art. Then, 16 years ago, Thelgarr, with his apprentices aid, attempted to summon a demon and imprison it to his service. At the height of the ritual, Kelda, his apprentice, made an error, whether accidental or with intent to assume control of the temple, no one could say, but Thelgarr was snatched through the portal by the demon into another Plane, never to be seen or heard from again! As Thelgarrs apprentice, the priests and magi that helped run the temple and school, elected Kelda as his successor, and she assumed the role of Grand Magus of the Temple of the Seven Stars. She has lead these 16 years, growing in power and might. Thelgarr Blackstaff Class & Level: Mystic Theurge 18 Alignment: Lawful Neutral Race: Human Status: Assumed deceased Strength: 13 Dexterity: 13 Constitution: 11 Intelligence: 19 Wisdom: 16 Charisma: 14

pages.content: The administrator of the House of Coins in Gosterwick (b. 363 PR)

pages.title: Thoras Goldpanner
pages.content: A semi-famous former dwarven resident of Silent Diamond who is responsible for the town's current name. Thoras passed away in PR 73.

pages.title: Thrangir of Belaphas

pages.title: Thraxis Corvale
pages.content: An older gentleman-scholar, Thraxis is was a member of the Seekers of Helix until his death in PR 195; he was one-quarter dragonborn, and was a self-avowed expert on dragonkind. He often gave advice to the Phandalin Three (sometimes Four ) and helped them navigate their ... scaly complications.

pages.title: Thurgan Newl
pages.content: Nephew to Billworth Turgen, Thurgan (PR 382-?) is the son of Billworth's half-brother, Chez -- the brother slain during an orc attack on Kirkilston in the winter of PR 390. Thurgan has been assisting his uncle 'Bill' since the spring of PR 395, after turning eighteen on January 18th of that year. thurgan-portrait.jpg Ranger 2 Hp 10 AC 6 Str 12 Dex 11 Con 13 Wis 9 Int 8 Cha 12
