pages.title: Jelb's Family Genealogy
pages.content: 1st Generation: Garrick (m. Dirla of Threshold) Notes: Helped found Kirkilston in 107 PR. He was a blacksmith and enchanter of reasonable skill - not a practitioner of witchcraft, but an enchanter of items and devices. He had little to no actual spellcasting ability, or at least he didn't let on much that he did. Some thought he had some elven blood in him. Others suggested he was actually an archmage pretending to be a blacksmith. The truth of that has been lost to the proceeding centuries. What is known for certain is that his skill was sufficient that his skill and creativity were sufficient to get him multiple commissions in Threshold. He saved much of the wealth he made, and when he finally married and settled in Kirkilston, he passed that along with a strong creative drive on to his children. Masterpiece: Many-pieced ornate iron blacksmith puzzle that forms a 1' diameter ball when fully assembled and pieces can stack into a small iron rod that holds together solidly. When left part-way between the 2 forms (either each partially assembled or with loose pieces) the puzzle reassembles itself to the last completed form at 12:00 AM of the first day of the week. Unknown Secret: The pieces would even be summoned back from different planes, and if the puzzle were destroyed and even one piece remained, it would recreate the rest of the puzzle at that time. Famed Connections: Unknown Death: ca. 147 PR --- 2nd Generation: Berik (m. Adna) Birth to retirement from leading family: 117-176 PR Notes: Berik Garrick (whose rhyming name issue did not appear during his lifetime as Garrick was not actually used as a proper surname until the prime years of the third generation) studied material science, especially in glassmaking. He sought to make increasingly harder and more durable forms of glass. Masterpiece: A uniquely formed glass-like water vessel that can quickly heat or cool liquid passed through its intricate insides, depending on whether it is placed over heat or not. Famed Connections: Thorgar Flamehammer, a young dwarven hero out of Gauntwood Galleries once took a bet that he could shatter one of Berik's creations with his hammer. Had he succeeded, Berik would have given him the secrets of his craft. When Thorgar failed, he was bound to spend the next decade of his life accompanying Berik on journeys to find ingredients for his glasswork and to sell his wares along the route between Gauntwood Galleries and Kirkilston. Thorgar continued adventuring after that decade before eventually settling down to pursue some glassworking of his own and raise a family in the Galleries. He is quite old now, but has had occasional contact with the Garrick family over the centuries. Death: ca. 176 PR --- 3rd Generation: Kindo (m. Jera Everlight of Glittering Canopy) Birth to retirement from leading family: 135-207 PR Notes: If Kindo was not a full druid, he at the very least had naturalist inclinations. He developed a method of growing furniture and artwork. He would cutscion branches from a single tree, then sprout them as individual trees. Then branches of appropriate sizes from the cloned and parent trees would be grafted and woven together to form the furniture, before slowly being split off from still-living main trees. There was great demand from both elves and men for both his methods and his workmanship. Masterpiece: A four-poster bed with shaped-by-vine curves and whorls on each posts, curtains of woven whiteboard, and effectively a box-spring of curled shoots. Famed Connections: Kindo spent a great deal of time visiting Aelith-Calaer and learning from her people. He was named elf-friend once his heart and interests were known and became at least passing friends with the mage Faranthas Starsong and and fast friends the druid Sorenal Everlight. He is perhaps the only man from Kirkilston to be invited to travel by magic with the elves from Aelith-Calaer to The Glittering Canopy. While on that trip and sharing his skills and their products with the elves there, he stayed with the extended family of Sorenal, making friends with much of the Everlight family, and eventually marrying one of their daughters and returning home with her. Death: 227 PR --- 4th Generation: Balan "Halfelven" (m. Gala Finnegan) Birth to retirement from leading family: 154-203 PR Notes: Following somewhat in his father's footsteps, Balan's interests were in the natural world. He bred lines of sables and used their hairs to make incredibly brushes for painters and artisans all over the region. Having long handed over leadership of the family, Balan eventually left the household along with his mother and word of his passing near the turn of the third to fourth centuries came to the family some time later. Masterpiece: A set of ornately carved wooden-handled sable-fur paintbrushes, of various shapes and sizes, ranging from just a few fibers to one that would be more fitting for a house-painter. Famed Connections: The painter Alvin Derve of Threshold used Balan Brushes exclusively once his career began to take off. He brought word of Balan all the way to Sizemordicus, which in turn sent a few entrepeneuring merchants from that city all the way to Threshold. One, Goran Tordal, even made it all the way to Kirkilston and purchased many sets of brushes that he hawked all the way on his return route to Sizemordicus, selling them on the fame of Alvin. By the time he finished selling the brushes in his home city, Goran was set to retire wealthy, and did so. Death: 298 --- 8th Generation: Cianda (m. Gelkor Coor, reputed to have been a skilled diviner, who took her surname when they inherited the estate) Birth to retirement from leading family: (242-289) Notes: Cianda had been entranced by Berik's Masterpiece from a young age. She took what he had discovered and explored the opposite end of the spectrum - exploring ways of making glass break in certain patterns based on material and internal tensions. Masterpiece: Twofold - a 5' tall glass phoenix that had been freed from a carefully created glass cube with a single, well-placed hammer tap; it rests upon a 5' glass cube with a green glass spot on one corner with a hammer. The bottom cube is not to be struck until the hour of the family's greatest need. Jelb had several times wondered if he would need to break it and see what happened, but he managed to successfully allocate the family's few remaining funds to set himself and his siblings up to support themselves going forward. With himself and Funn both having net-positive incomes, this is no longer a thought in the back of his mind. Famed Connections: Gelkor Coor himself was a well-reputed sage and diviner in his home city of Sizemordicus. The latter skills (combined with the endless machinations of many in the city) led Gelkor to depart the city wander to find a more remote place to live and ended up in Kirkilston. After marrying Cianda, he did what he could for the other residents of Kirkilston. The couple eventually took a brief trip back to Sizemordicus so that Cianda could see where Gelkor had grown up. They brought a dozen unbroken sculptures of various beasts and a few trees. Several sculptures were broken-out from cube to creature at a public auction by Perune Auction House. They were purchased by wealthy families including the Dummer and the Lorgens families. One was gifted to the Auction house, and the other eight were auctioned off unbroken. Death: 289 --- 11th Generation: Dorik (m. Baina Kinney) Birth to retirement from leading family: 307-356 Notes: Dorik followed in the glass-making line of the family and developed acid etching techniques that gave various shades and colors to glassware, as well as stronger and weaker acids that would also create unlevel surfaces. Masterpiece: A glass table with ornately cut legs and map of Kirkilston acid-etched into the tabletop. The set of six chairs have smaller versions of six other cities etched into the table-side of their backs. Famed Connections: Created several 1-piece stained glass windows for a few of the wealthiest families and businesses in Threshold, many of which were lost in the attack of 386. Death: 385 --- 14th Generation: Murfex (m. Aria) Birth to retirement from leading family: 368-[death] Notes: Murfex combined Berik and Cianda's glassworking techniques to make extremely fine glass tubing and perforated glassware. Jelb repeatedly saw Murfex working to develop a fountain for the garden that would hold a large reservoir of water and intermittently spritz out a mist over the garden until the reservoir was empty. Something was apparently always wrong with the sculpture though, as it was regularly replaced with a new version in a completely different form. Masterpiece: Not selected yet, Jelb is looking for an appropriate piece of his glassware Famed Connections: Athelbyn Lothaybin the alchemist had several specialty pieces made by Murfex. Applications of both fine but sturdy tubing, and perforated glass for slowed or time-delayed reactions proved invaluable in his craft. Daranna Worten the inventor had a number of pieces and was trying to use them to design tools for wealthy mercenaries and adventurers, like potion-sippers that would sequentially drain vials in one's backpack. As of Murfex's death, none of her inventions using his glassware had worked. Death: [date not picked yet - between 396 and 404, keeping open for making a story connection - en route to Threshold]

pages.title: Jelb's Chronicles - 1
pages.content: The party, consisting at the time of Jelb Garrick, Kelpie Lawfuller, and Urvan Hall met up by happenstance one night at Morgan's Morsels & Tankards in Kirkilston. Hearing of a missing young woman named Jelenneth Laneworth. The three were bound together in a desire to see her saved. They spent the night at the Garrick home and set out the following morning. They met Nuanda Nemere, a local white witch, who divined after the young woman, determining that she was part of a rash of bandit abductions and disappearances in an area to the north. She recommended the party speak with the ranger, Kuiper, who dwells in that area and gave them a letter of introduction to him. Nuanda also recommended taking a caravan to Raven's Pass to start the journey, and that in Raven's Pass they should meet up with Nimba Armstrong at The Mason's Apron Tavern and in addition to speaking with her, ask to see her husband Samuel who is a blacksmith and could help with gear maintenance. Nuanda also personally requested that the party provide her with the following if they should be willing and able: (1) an amethyst of at least 50 golden coins' value, (2) a rare herb called Hwyanthemon, and (3) the hair of a slain orc.

pages.title: Jelb's Chronicles - 2
pages.content: jelb-garrick.webp The party departed Nuanda's the following morning and returned to Kirkilston to join a caravan led by Billworth Turgen north to Raven's Pass, joining the guards headed by Thurgan Newl. They were joined by others both in the job to guard the caravan and the mission to rescue Jelenneth by others who were in the area. New members of the party included Maximilian Yragerne, Geoffrey Morin, and Narinza Izrut. While journeying north, the caravan paused at a likely ambush spot and sent out scouts. Both sets of scouts encountered bands of Orcs and dealt with them. From one of the two, they recovered a note written in orcish and detailing some of the goals of the orcs' masters: specifically gaining knowledgeable, strong, or healthy slaves. The caravan rushed north to a known quarry, Blightstone Pit, to make a stand against the oncoming orc forces. As the caravan traveled, the orcs were delayed by an illusory rockslide created by Jelb as well as being felled by arrows and ranged attacks from Thurgan and others. Nevertheless, many of the orcs continued in their pursuit. Metal, magic, arrows, dogs, and even flame were deployed against the orcs at the Pit. Before victory could be fully accomplished, a large tentacled monster rose from a deep hole, killing nearby orcs and moving to threaten the party. The caravan fled the quarry, as did the few remaining orcs. When the caravan halted and Thurgan made a quick patrol to discern whether they were still pursued, the group realized that they had lost Narinza and Urvan. They quickly counseled together regarding their immediate and more far-reaching plans.

pages.title: Jelb Chronicles III
pages.content: Once the caravan had time to mend its wounded, the decision was made to press on for a time to leave farther behind whatever was in the pit as well as any nearby orc raiding parties. They all agreed that they would have to continue on after camping. While the more adventurous would have liked to ensure Narinza's safety and freedom, she was capable and may have left them voluntarily. Meanwhile, the caravan had wounded and civilians to get to safety. A few hours later into the evening, they they halted and made camp. After a wary but much needed night's rest, the survivors journeyed on. They successfully reached Raven's Pass the next day for trading, treatment of the wounded, and settling accounts. The party separated from the caravan with well-wishes, their pay, and free meals to come at the Mason's Apron. They turned down further offered reward so that the families of the fallen caravanners could be better provided for. At the Mason's Apron, Kelpie, Geoffroy, Maximilian, and Jelb made a number of new friends and acquaintances. Nimba, sister of Nuanda, greeted them and provided them with more than they could ask for: both credit to trade and drinks aplenty, which - while explicitly having passed the Red Laws certification - seemed more "effective" than other similarly compliant drinks. Her husband Samuel also offered services to the party - a special honing of their blades. As evening wore on, the group began recruiting. A number of members ballooned the size of the group, to one that seemed like it might even be capable of dealing with the threats before them: A drow ranger named Shade, who had a purported interest in locating Nerissa; A paladin of Cromm named Neria, who sought a worthy cause to fight for; A cleric named Nerissa, who seemed to be of similar interest; and the three Sintarn siblings, Borca, Corba, and Arilia. Unbeknownst to them at the time, they were also being watched and reported on...

pages.title: Jelb Family History
pages.content: Many generations ago, the Garrick family was founded by Garrick himself, a blacksmith and enchanter of reasonable skill. He was no witch, but an enchanter of items and devices. He had little to no actual spellcasting ability, or at least he didn't let on much that he did. Some thought he had some elven blood in him. Others suggested he was actually an archmage pretending to be a blacksmith. The truth of that has been lost to the proceeding century and change. What is known for certain is that his skill and creativity were sufficient to get him multiple commissions in Threshold. He saved much of the wealth he made, and when he finally married and settled in Kirkilston, he passed that along with a strong creative drive on to his children. At least one member of each generation of Garricks has had a drive to create something great and new, and an artifact of each generation remains in the back room of the family home. A surpassingly complex blacksmith puzzle from Garrick himself, a uniquely formed water vessel that can quickly heat or cool liquid passed through its intricate insides from the next generation, a painting with unique hues in it from another. It continues all the way down to Jelb's father Murfex, who should have left a masterpiece of glassware but had died enroute to Threshold with his wife Aria several years ago, without making one. Jelb would go to great lengths to acquire one of Murfex's masterpieces for the hall, should he come across one. While the vast wealth of Garrick had diminished over time, each generation was able to do well enough for themselves. In addition to being able to lay aside a masterpiece each generation, they were able to set the next generation up to succeed, while also being generous supporters of the community. With the early passing of Murfex and Aria, however, there was little more than enough to finish Jelb's education, cover Kerina's dowry, and set Funn up with some high-quality woodworking tools.

pages.title: Journal Entry Excerpt 8a
pages.content: Dated [date of fights with orcs while traveling from Kirkilston to Raven's Pass] This portion encoded within original I spent far too long considering the Orc before me while Geoffroy recovered and tested a sword, just after my first actual combat. Hopefully the others thought my hesitation was due to emotional issues with the fighting or something of like kind. Instead it was an internal debate of what hairs to bring back to Nuanda. There were several obvious options and others less obvious for obtaining the hair required for her quest. The first and most obvious was right from the top of the head. It was my first instinct and what I ended up taking. Not only was it easily reached without exposing my eyes and mind to any more of the orc's foul anatomy, but it also didn't have any... excretory additions either from brain leaking from its ear or from whatever other emissions might come from a formerly healthy orc. Not that the orc was likely to have used any kind of soap for cleaning its hair I realize, but there was a potential sigma to using anything lower - both anatomically and proprietarily. I might have done such to one who deserved some comeuppance, but Nuanda had not designated herself as one of those to this point. Besides, she might know where it had come from, and I would not want the awkwardness of that turned and used as a foil to poke me instead. And even if she didn't, Oceneroth almost certainly would and I'd rather not face his displeasure or have him reveal it to Nuanda. All that passed in a brief second of thought. That is when I hesitated. Oceneroth could not tell Nuanda. He would know. I would know. And he couldn't say anything without causing himself (and possibly the universe as a whole for all I know) a great deal of trouble. He'd have to sit with his goody-two-shoes-slippers (or whatever) on and not say anything. I almost broke down laughing at the thought and went forward with damaging my own eyesight to expose other hairs to take... but then I realized that he had also done nothing to deserve that type of treatment. Oceneroth had instead expended at least some power to keep tabs on us and had sent me a form of minor aid for this day and all those going forward. I could not lightly betray that, even for such a good entrapment of a jest. I really need to stop making such nice acquaintances and fall in with some bores or beasts or bandits for a time so I can at least have some good excuse for exercising my creativity. With a mildly forlorn sigh, I cut the hair and went off to the further adventure that I had little idea awaited me that day.

pages.title: Max on Blanrydes
pages.content: Blanryde Hills The Blanryde Hills are a group of rugged low hills stretching from a few miles west of Slaytonthorpe northeast to Threshold, with a branch of the hills extending just a bit to the northwest of that town. These hills are home to many different groups from small enclaves of gnomes and halflings, to hideouts for monsters of all sorts, orcs, goblins, a few gnolls and some bigger creatures as well like hill giants to more exotic creatures like manticores and wyverns. Gnomes Glickstonehome is the name of a gnomish settlement just to the west of Slaytonthorpe, on the western side of the Eelhold and the Oldscutt River. There are 8 clans of gnomes living there in warrens and mines under the hills where they mine for gemstones of emerald. The emeralds of their mines are of the highest quality and the skills of the gem cutters and lapidaries are unparalleled in the lands. The gnomes here trade with the humans in Slaytonthorp and the halflings of Lindendale just to the north of that town by about 8 miles or so, as well as the gnomes and dwarves to the east of the river on the edge of the hills. Halflings There are 3 small halfling enclaves in the Blanryde Hills, Lindendale being the largest. Lindendale is mostly oriented to farming and such, growing some of the finest foods around on their lands. They are at the edge of the hills near the edge of The High Moor and their warriors spend a fair amount of time defending their homes from the denizens of that moor.

pages.title: Du'mal
pages.content: The Du'mal is a third part of the triadic pantheon, these gods hold sway almost entirely in the Underdark, as opposed to the World Above gods of the Anganach and Futurus.

pages.title: Argent Shields
pages.content: The most famous mercenary company under regular contract to the Silver Standard Trading Company. 150-300 veterans. Known for discipline and reliability. Silver kite shields bearing the company seal. Frequently assigned to high-value caravans.

pages.title: Argent Twilight
pages.content: The Argent Twilight is a secretive organization dedicated to recovering lost arcane lore and magical items. They also are intensely focused on recovering technologies from Ancient civilizations. This organization courts arcanists ” particularly Enchanters, and Thieves ” especially Dungeoneers. They seek reports, recovered scrolls and tomes, and ancient magic items and technologies so that they may study and (it is hoped) be able to replicate them. In exchange for members' supplying ” or promising to supply ” these things, the Argent Twilight is willing to provide its members supplies, knowledge, wealth, and other forms of assistance.

pages.title: Basilisk's Claw
pages.content: The Basilisk's Claw is a cultic faction operating out of Threshold that is believed to focus on countering the efforts of the Lightbringers and the Harpers.

pages.title: Calico Five
pages.content: An adventuring band that lost a cleric of St. Ygg when infiltrating Gundgathol in PR 203. According to the surviving four party members: a fighter, a warlock, a ranger, and a dungeoneer. the Righteous Arm of Ygg, Cheluthim Sarcos, died during a fight with a deep dragon. A when a wing buffet blew him into a crevasse. One member of this band survives: the dwarf Slengar Skullcrusher, who resides in Khalidheroneth.

pages.title: Cult of the Dragon
pages.content: A widespread cult active for many thousands of years. This cult believes that dragons are a remnant left behind by the Visitors. The cult seeks to spread the worship and rulership of dragons, and sometimes convinces dragons to undergo a ritual to become dracoliches.

pages.title: Eld Brothers
pages.content: Four brothers from Sizemordicus who worked together as mercenaries and caravan guards in the first century Post-Ravaging. The brothers were named Mintarn, Belphor, Caspius, and Olophorn.

pages.title: Fire Blades
pages.content: A thieves guild in Threshold that stubbornly refuses to be stomped out, despite the efforts of both the Lord of Threshold and the Prelate. Possibly ruled by Banville Mask.

pages.title: Fist of Felix
pages.content: The Fist of Felix is a group of five ... what shall we call them? Adventurers? Fixers? Three clerics of Imperiosa, a magic-user, and a fighter who uses a rare long sword +2 named 'Nevertheless'. They are based in Helix.

pages.title: Gray Lances
pages.content: The Gray Lances of the Snarling Steeder are elite Duergar crusaders and fighter-priests who serve as the elite cavalry of gray dwarven armies, and their most common opponents are Drow mounted on riding lizards.

pages.title: Hûl Hildresu
pages.content: Naturalists, archaeologists, and other researchers whose interest lies in uncovering secrets of past inhabitants of Issenda and the artifacts they left behind. Many Hûl Hildresu venerate Arcantryl.

pages.title: Harpers
pages.content: A clandestine organization that works to protect freedom by opposing any and all groups that seek power at others' expense. The Harpers stand in very particular opposition to the Zhentarim.

pages.title: Inglorious Bastards
pages.content: Relative newcomers, this band first showed up in the Northern Reaches in PR 398. They have done some work for the Radloc Hudson's mercenary company. They have loud mouths and loose morals. In PR 400 they were warned by Sir Chevae Thrace to stay clear of Eastdale, a warning they have heeded. In the past few years, they have been active primarily in the Phandalin-Isenton-Westkeep area.
