pages.title: Lightbringers
pages.content: An adventuring company founded in Slaytonthorpe in PR 25 by Xavamros Battlebeard I. The group went on to defeat a concerted threat to the entire region at the Battle of the Broken Spire in PR 26. They held that fortress and remained a company for two decades afterward.

pages.title: Order of the Gauntlet
pages.content: A devout and vigilant group, consisting largely of St. Ygg adherents who for whatever reason didn't enter his priesthood or the Red Bannermen (or were discharged from either group), that seeks to protect others from the depredations of evil-doers. The order is always ready to smite evil, enforce justice, and enact retribution against any who try to subjugate or harm others.

pages.title: Red Bannermen
pages.content: Paladins of St. Ygg whose ultimate loyalty is to their god, though they usually are found submitting to their seniors in the bannermen and clergy. Red Bannermen are also sometimes referred to as Excoriators, and many certainly live up to this appellation -- unlike Urvan Hall, sometimes known as Urvan the Mild. These templars (some are paladins, a few merely militant clerics) are answerable to Mordicar Justhand, and in service to St. Ygg. They maintain order and enforce the Red Laws in Eastdale. In general usage, 'Red Bannermen' refers to fighters or (more often) clerics serving the Red Temple and St. Ygg. Technically, paladins of St. Ygg are indeed Red Bannermen, but in normal usage people mean fighters or clerics of Ygg when using the term. Paladins of St. Ygg are known as Excoriators.

pages.title: Scyntarn
pages.content: The Scyntarn are witch-hunters who have access to secret lore that aids them in their extermination efforts. Scyntarn never worship the Anganach. Most worship the Futurus, the majority Arcantryl, Oghma, or St. Ygg. Algorn Druff is a member of the Scyntarn.

pages.title: Seekers
pages.content: A brotherhood that works to reclaim the lost knowledge of Earth's (referred to as Issenda by it's current inhabitants) previous ages, even back in the dimmest past. The Seekers are based in Helix. Suspected current and former members of The Seekers include: Thraxis Corvale (deceased) Auriochos d'Rosenberg (deceased)

pages.title: Singing Swords
pages.content: A group of five adventurers (three humans and two halflings) who, in PR 203 penetrated into ancient Undalan where they sought a way downward to a rumored earlier settlement, Benediction. This group was never heard of again, and is assumed to have met their end somewhere in the Undalanic ruins.

pages.title: The Darkeyes
pages.content: The thieves guild operating under Eastdale, profiting from everything the Red Laws drive underground. They are not simply criminals; they also serve as middlemen between lawful, chaotic, wealthy, and discreet clients.

pages.title: The Felicitously Forsworn
pages.content: A powerful band of mercenaries operating out of southern Hohnberg in the nation of Westmark in the period 12-32 PR and primarily in the Southern Reaches. By PR 68 all but one of the band had died, and only the dwarf Gintarn Khalidson survived. He passed in PR 153. Gintarn's grandson is Garbald Khalidson, age 83, born PR 375. As of 405, Garbald was residing in Khalidheroneth.

pages.title: The Hearthguard of Demetra
pages.content: A faction associated with Demetra, the Anganach goddess of farmers and homesteaders. The Hearthguard is associated with the protection of homes, families, farmland, and rural communities. One of its key members in the Northern Reaches is Ardan Hearthward, a knight. Ardan is particularly well-known for helping travelers, negotiating peaceful settlements, and maintaining multiple shrines to his goddess. “I am the shield of the harvest. I defend the hearth, the home, and the humble. I take only what is freely given. I give more than I take. Where I break, I mend. Where I fight, I sow peace. By Demetra’s flame, I stand.”

pages.title: The Sporebane Brotherhood
pages.content: A group dedicated to curbing the spread of the magical Fungal Spore disease from its epicenter, Mordoom Keep. Elowen Starshadow and Eldrith Moss-Walker are leaders of this faction.

pages.title: The Weighty Eight
pages.content: Riothamus, Glaurthogos, Pryrates, Inzeldrin, Balagos, Claugiyliamatar, Iymrith, and Mornauguth ” the eight original and still extant True Dragons. From these oviparous scalies have come all dragons that ever graced Earth's skies, plundered its caverns. Some sages hold that these Eight also somehow embody the consciousness of the original Visitors, now long since departed.

pages.title: Tivuld-Gho
pages.content: The Tivuld-Gho (pronounced tee val, GWAH) are a very small set of beings, theorized by some sages, who are Visitors who continue to bide on Issenda. Are they hibernating or in stasis? Could they still rule/influence from the shadows, through proxies? Might there be a Tivuld-Gho residing deep beneath Phandalin?

pages.title: Zhentarim
pages.content: An organization that operates throughout the Reaches, seeking to consolidate power and wealth for its members and to manipulate politics to their own advantage.

pages.title: Gods
pages.content: Gods are beings that can be communed with and who can grant spells to followers, gods are also extraplanar beings that usually do not reside on the material plane with mortals.

pages.title: Anganach
pages.content: The Elder Gods, still venerated by many in the Northern Reaches. The Anganach were widely worshipped long before the advent of the Futurus. The Anganach are comprised of the following deities: Cromm Cruach, Herne, Impurax, Nergal, Orcus, Set, Silvanus, Valdghar, and Zuul. Some sages believe that Omari was/is one of the Anganach.

pages.title: Anu-eya
pages.content: anueya-optimized.webp Anu-Eya God of Achaia Lawful Neutral Symbol: A somewhat alien face with a large round headdress Anu-Eya is an ancient deity from the time before time. He long predates the arrival of demi-humans and humans to the Southern Reaches. He is a greater god and creator of the Achaians. Anu-Eya gave life to his people and bestowed many gifts upon them. These included innate magical abilities and knowledge of the cosmos. When the Archons of the Trium sought to ascend to godhood and challenge him, Anu-Eya wrought destruction upon the great city of Archaia. His wrath cracked the earth, swallowed the city, and destroyed his people -- or so he thought. The Archons survived and, with the help of Impurax, have been plotting their revenge. Anu-Eya is tall, lithe, with slightly pointed ears. He is often depicted wearing a large round headdress and loincloth. His arms, neck, fingers, ankles and toes are decorated in gold and platinum jewelry. He is a vengeful god. Some believe that Anu-Eya is the father of Zuul. In fact, some of both Anu-Eya's and Zuul's faithful believe this. Of very great interest, to those few people who are in the know, is the fact that since 196 PR four (count them, four ) clerics of Anu-Eya that are operating within the Reaches have been identified by the spymaster of Threshold, who is both an arch mage and a skillful investigator. Yes, apparently Anu-Eya has chosen for the first time since destroying his people (the Achaians) in PR 103 to take an interest in the mortal realm.

pages.title: Arcantryl
pages.content: arcantryl-optimized.webp Arcantryl, also called Magus , is a Lawful Neutral Futurus/New God associated with magic, arcane knowledge, ordered learning, and the laws of the cosmos . Her doctrine frames magic not as wild superstition, but as the disciplined understanding of universal structure: study the hidden laws of existence, then harness or bend them to create magical effects. In the Northern Reaches/Middenmark, her church appears to be more urban and scholarly than rural. Sources note that her clerics have focused on larger centers such as Ironguard Motte , Threshold , and Eastdale , with smaller shrines appearing elsewhere rather than a wide village presence. A shrine to Arcantryl exists at Ironguard Motte, and a larger stone temple is described as under construction, intended to serve both clerics and magic-users. Her clergy are astrologer-priests, spell-theologians, librarians, geometers, and ritual scholars . Her temples contain star charts, spell formulae, polished lenses, mathematical diagrams, locked archives, and instructional chambers for both divine and arcane casters. Her faithful treat careless magic as nearly sinful, because magic is sacred knowledge and should be practiced with precision, discipline, and restraint. Politically and religiously, Arcantryl is part of the Futurus, alongside St. Ygg, Imperiosa, Oghma, Orcus, and Set. Unlike St. Ygg's aggressive church, Arcantryls followers are less forceful in conversion and seem more focused on scholarship, temples, magic-users, and institutional knowledge.

pages.title: Asmodeus
pages.content: asmodeus-symbol.webp Asmodeus King of Hell Lord of the Ninth Lawful Evil Symbol: A seven-pointed star Asmodeus is a lawful, ancient, calculating, tyrannical deity who is associated with contracts, domination, pride, temptation, and infernal hierarchy. He is the ruler of Nessus , the ninth and deepest layer of Hell. He is not just a powerful fiend but the organizing intelligence behind the entire infernal order. Devils under him are bound by rank, law, obligation, fear, and ambition. Unlike chaotic demons, Asmodeus represents evil through control, hierarchy, legalism, corruption, and perfectly worded bargains . asmodeus-optimized.webp His most important themes are: Lawful evil authority. Asmodeus is the tyrant who makes oppression look orderly. His evil is not random cruelty; it is systematized, codified, and justified through law. Contracts and temptation. He rarely needs to force mortals into damnation. He offers power, revenge, security, forbidden knowledge, or survival, then binds the soul through a bargain whose hidden cost becomes clear too late. Pride and cosmic ambition. Asmodeus believes he is the only being capable of imposing true order on creation. He sees himself not as a villain but as the necessary ruler who understands reality better than gods or mortals. Infernal religion. Cults of Asmodeus are usually not sloppy murder-cults. They are secret societies, corrupt legal orders, noble houses, tyrannical churches, oath-bound cabals, or ambitious magicians. His worshipers may present themselves as defenders of civilization, law, tradition, purity, or necessary discipline. Asmodeus isn't a cackling devil, but as a calm, regal, terrifyingly reasonable figure. He should sound like someone who always has the moral high ground prepared in advance: I did not make them betray their oaths. I merely gave their oaths consequences. His symbols vary by setting, but common imagery includes a ruby rod , serpents , horned crowns , black-and-red infernal stars , contracts , pentagrams or heptagrams , and regal infernal sigils. Asmodeus is a distant patron or ultimate power , not an ordinary monster. His agents might be judges, inquisitors, corrupt nobles, diabolists, contract-devils, or warlocks who promise stability in exchange for obedience. A low-level party may never meet him, but they can feel his influence through contracts, cult cells, infernal legal codes, and temptations that seem practical rather than obviously evil. The use of Hellbane is often associated with Asmodeus' followers.

pages.title: Cromm Cruach
pages.content: cromsymbol.webp Crom (Cromm Cruach) Neutral Good God of Strength and Battle Chaotic Good Symbol: A silver crown over a white capped mountain An Ancient One worshipped largely by fighters, rangers, barbarians, and clerics. Due to the constant threat of monsters and monstrous humanoids from the Barrowmoor and the surrounding forests, Crom's faith among warriors and mercenaries has remained steady in comparison to that of Silvanus and Herne. The clerics of Crom seek to advance their faith through strength of arms and feats of daring in battle. crom.webp

pages.title: Deep Duerra
pages.content: deep-duera-optimized.webp Deep Duerra Alignment: Lawful Evil Portfolio: Psionics, conquest, expansion, duergar supremacy, war strategy Clerical tone: militant, authoritarian, disciplined, expansionist Likely domains: War, Knowledge, Order, Tyranny, Mentalism/Psionics Deep Duerra, also known as Queen of the Invisible Art or the Axe Princess of Conquest, is the duergar (deep dwarves) goddess of psionics, conquest and expansion. The legends of the duergar tell of the gray dwarves' greatest queen, a warrior queen named Duerra, who led her grim troops to numerous victories against the surface dwarves, the drow, the illithids, and other Underdark races. During her centuries long reign, the empire of the gray dwarves expanded to include vast reaches of the Underdark, including much of the territory that once composed Deep Shanatar, bringing the duergar to the pinnacle of their power. Tales of dubious authenticity also relate how Deep Duerra overran a city of mind flayers and wrested from them numerous powers of the mind. Supposedly Duerra's victory allowed the duergar to gain their current ability in psionics and enabled them to hold their own against the spells of the drow and the psionics of the illithids. Although much of Deep Duerra's empire has since fragmented and contracted, the gray dwarves still revere her uncompromising drive to expand duergar power throughout the Underdark. Duerra is bombastic, arrogant, and imperious. She expects her every whim to be attended to instantly, and she is firmly convinced other own inalienable right to rule. The Queen of the Invisible Art is dismissive of wizardly magic, considering it inferior to the power of the mind. Duerra is always plotting, planning, and strategizing her next conquest. She is never satisfied with what she has already acquired, as it is the conquest, not the holding, that she enjoys. deep-duera.webp The Axe Princess is ruthless in her drive to ensure victory, and she has absolutely no tolerance for any being, mortal or divine, who does not live up to her standards. Likewise, Duerra considers no sacrifice too great if it offers greater benefits down the road. The Queen of the Invisible Art occasionally dispatches her avatar to aid in conflicts between the duergar and other psionic races, particularly aboleth and illithids. Duerra also dispatches an avatar when a city of gray dwarves has a golden opportunity to expand its territorial holdings at the expense of other races of the Underdark, but for whatever reason, the duergar rulership is reluctant to act on it. Deep Duerra is venerated by gray dwarves skilled in the Invisible Art (psionics) as well as duergar warriors who seek to conquer much of the Underdark and chafe at the defensive mindset of Laduguer's priests. A few rare surface dwellers with wild talents have begun to call on the Queen of the Invisible Art as well for aid in understanding (and more importantly, concealing) their powers, which are viewed with suspicion and fear by most of the populace. Deep Duerra's clerics are known below the surface as norothor ("those who seize enemy land"). Their recent efforts in the Underdark have made them the talk of underground way stations and trading communities. Within gray dwarven communities, perceptions of Duerra's church vary widely. Younger duergar admire the brashness and assertiveness her priests display. Older gray dwarves view Duerra's priests as impertinent upstarts who are likely to bring the combined wrath of the aboleth, drow, illithids, and other races of the Underdark down upon their heads. The norothor nonetheless serve an important role in society, training young gray dwarves in the development of their natural psionic abilities, attending to and controlling the slaves who form the underclass of duergar society, and scouting and clearing out nearby tunnel systems that the community might grow. Lastly, their focus on the mental disciplines makes them ideal ambassadors to psionic races such as the illithid and aboleth, though the inherent brashness of the faith means that many such missions end in utter disaster. The clergy of Duerra consists primarily of gray dwarves, but a handful of gold dwarves, shield dwarves, and wild dwarves skilled in the Invisible Art secretly serve the Daul of Laduguer as well while remaining in or near their own communities. The ceremonial garb of Duerra's priests includes ornate, gleaming chain mail (often treated with everbright or Mueshine) and dark blue velvet robes trimmed with the fur of surface animals. No headgear of any sort is worn, but a beautiful weapon, often bejeweled, is always borne. The holy symbol of the faith is a two-inch diameter silver orb, carved to resemble the skull of an illithid, with a large crack running across the top. A steel chain is usually threaded through the skull's ear holes so that it can be worn around the neck. Outside of ceremonial functions, Duerran priests eschew their glittering mail for the drab chain or dwarven plate mail common to the duergar and a hooded, ankle-length gray-blue robe. The primary weapon of most priests is the battle axe, in deliberate imitation of their goddess, but Duerra's priests are also skilled in the use of weapons favored by most gray dwarves, including heavy and light crossbows, picks, short swords, spears, and war hammers. Novices of Duerra are known as the Close-minded. Full priests of the Queen of the Invisible Art are known as Mindaxes. In ascending order of rank, the titles used by Duerran priests are Psionic Blaster, Mind Thruster, Ego Whipper, Id Insinuator, Psychic Crusher, and Thought Conqueror. High Old Ones have unique individual titles but are collectively known as Axe Princesses/Princes of the Invisible Art. Duerra's temples are hewn from solid rock and are always constructed in symmetric patterns designed to be architecturally pleasing to the observer and to muffle sound. On an elevated dais in the central chancel is an empty seat in the middle of the room. Called the Daul's Throne, the chair serves to remind the norothor that as Queen of the Invisible Art, Deep Duerra is always present and watching. Duerra's houses of worship serve as armories, barracks, and command centers for the senior priests who lead the temple army. Most are extensively fortified and well stocked with emergency supplies, weapons, and armor. Deep Duerra's clerics pray for spells at night. The Duerran church celebrates two holy days annually. The first, known as the Rallying, is celebrated on Midwinter eve. On this night, the followers of Duerra assemble to commemorate the triumphs and conquests of the previous year and to proclaim their intentions to seize new territory. Grim chants of war and the pounding of hammers against stone echo through the tunnels as the duergar work themselves into a grim fury. The culmination of such martial exaltations is the display of the newly seized skull of an enemy from another race whose territory will be besieged in the coming year. The other holy day of the Duerran faith is celebrated on the 5th of May. On this day, skilled practitioners of the Invisible Art assemble in Duerran temples to join in the Melding, a psionic ritual in which the assembled minds of the gray dwarves contact Duerra herself. The duergar temporarily form a common mind that rivals that of the great Elder Brains of the illithids. It is from such Meldings that many insights leading to great advances in duergar technology and psionics have come. Offerings to the Queen of the Invisible Art are made at both ceremonies; these typically include dirt or stone carried back from the borders of newly conquered territory, the brains of psionic individuals, or shattered skulls from members of any intelligent race. The children of Laduguer shall conquer the earth and stone from which they sprang and the voids in which they dwell. The seizing of new lands, new wealth, and new servitors is the manifest destiny of those who mine the Nigh Below. Magic is weak, unreliable, and unsubtle when compared to the powers of the mind unless bequeathed and steadied by the will of the gods. By means of the Invisible Art, the duergar shall destroy or enslave all those reliant upon petty magics to survive. Deep Duerra is a short stocky figure, thinner than "surface" dwarves. She has dull gray skin and has silver-gray hair (unlike most duergar, who are usually bald). Immediately on her apotheosis, she was exiled by Moradin. Because of this, Deep Duerra had no friends among the Morndinsamman. Some myths claimed that Laduguer was her father, but the two didn't show any compassion towards each other. While they were nominally allies, they constantly plotted against one another. Over the past centuries with only small successes, Duerra came very close to attempting to depose Laduguer as the duergar prime deity. She was hated by the illithid god-brain Ilsensine for the many thefts of psionic energy and information from it.

pages.title: Demetra
pages.content: demetra-symbol.webp Anganach Goddess of Agriculture & the Hearth Patron of farmers, homesteads, and all who work the soil. Demetra teaches that safety is earned through toil, and that every season repays the labour of the last. Her followers value diligence, community, and the quiet strength of a well kept fire. Prayer From toil springs the safety and just rewards in later seasons

pages.title: Dhaelven Deity Worship
pages.content: The pair of deities most often worshipped by Dhaelven in Scarlet Horizons is Arcantryl and Imperiosa—with the two representing complementary halves of Dhaelven civilization. 1. Arcantryl — Magic, arcane knowledge, ordered learning, and the laws of the cosmos. Arcantryl is a Lawful Neutral Futurus whose religion treats magic as the disciplined understanding and manipulation of the hidden structure of reality. Her clergy include spell-theologians, astrologers, geometers, librarians, and ritual scholars. (Obsidian) For the Dhaelves, this fits extremely well because they descend from the Aelves , themselves descendants of the Throiki servitor lineage. Even if modern Dhaelves no longer understand that ancestry correctly, they retain a very old cultural conviction that mastery of magic is their birthright . Their unusually sophisticated magical traditions actually preserve distorted remnants of Aelven—and ultimately Throiki—knowledge. Dhaelven theology claims: Magic is not granted to us. It is remembered. That makes Arcantryl particularly interesting because surface worshippers regard her as a relatively new Futurus , while Dhaelven theologians often insist that humans have simply rediscovered a Power the ancestors knew long before humanity learned her name . That creates a wonderful theological problem for Kelda Rue and the Hûl Hildresu. 2. Imperiosa — Tyranny, domination, and destruction. Imperiosa is Lawful Evil, militaristic, and explicitly teaches the destruction of weakness and the pursuit of domination. Significantly, she is most often depicted as a beautiful black-skinned warrior woman , with the clawed black fist as her symbol and the maxim, “By our swords, we rule.” (Obsidian) She fits Dhaelven history even better thematically than she first appears. The Dhaelves descend from a race whose extremely remote ancestors were servitors . A powerful cultural reaction to that forgotten racial memory is an absolute horror of subordination: The Aelves served. The Dhaelves will never serve. Over millennia, that has become one of the central assumptions of Dhaelven society: there are ultimately only masters and servants , and the greatest possible disgrace is to be the latter. Imperiosa's theology transforms that inherited trauma into doctrine. Strength proves fitness to rule; weakness invites domination. This is the particularly Scarlet Horizons explanation for the classic dark-elf preoccupation with hierarchy, ruthlessness, intrigue, slavery, and personal power without simply importing Lolth wholesale. The Dhaelven religious duality Arcantryl + Imperiosa are the two great competing/complementary Powers of Dhaelven civilization: Arcantryl represents mastery of reality . Imperiosa represents mastery of others . Or in Dhaelven philosophy: Knowledge gives Power. Power gives Dominion. This also produces interesting factions rather than making every Dhaelve generically evil. An Arcantrylite Dhaelven sage might be cold, secretive, arrogant, and utterly obsessed with recovering ancient Aelven knowledge without being evil at all. An Imperiosan noble house, conversely, might regard scholarship merely as another weapon by which intelligent beings establish dominance. The most powerful Dhaelven cities have two great priesthoods constantly maneuvering around one another : the Magi of Arcantryl controlling magical education, ancient archives, divination, and relic study, while Imperiosa's priesthood legitimizes aristocracy, military authority, conquest, and slavery. A very strong third choice: Beltar Some Dhaelves remain distinctly alien, subterranean, cruel, and religiously distinct from surface civilization . These often worship Beltar . Beltar is an old rival associated with authority over mines. (Obsidian) Her traditional associations with caves, pits, malice, monsters, and deep places make her exceptionally suitable for particular Dhaelven communities. But Beltarism is an older chthonic Dhaelven religion , rather than their principal civilization-wide religious practice.: Arcantryl — the Mind Ancient knowledge, sorcery, Throiki mysteries, magical supremacy. Imperiosa — the Fist Hierarchy, conquest, rulership, strength, refusal ever again to serve. Beltar — the Deep The subterranean world, hatred, survival, ancient darkness, and the powers beneath the earth. Arcantryl and Imperiosa are the canonical Dhaelven pair . They tie the Dhaelves much more deeply into Scarlet Horizons' own cosmology : they aren't “drow with different names.” Their religion is an echo of what they actually are— descendants of an unimaginably ancient created people who have forgotten that their ancestors once served beings from beyond Issenda, yet have built an entire civilization around magical mastery and the determination never to serve again.

pages.title: Gods of Issenda
pages.content: The gods are comprised of the Powers/Gods/Anganach, the Morndinsamman, and the The Futurus. There may be unknown gods. Anu-eya Arcantryl Asmodeus Beltar Blood Queen, The Callarduran Smoothhands Cromm Cruach Deep Duerra Demetra Diinkarazan Diirinka Great Mother, The Grumbar Gruumsh Gzemnid Herne Hruggek (worshipped by some bugbears) Blibdoolpoolp Ilsensine Ilxendren Imperiosa Impurax Laduguer Malachai Maglubiyet Moradin Thaneduhr Nergal Oaxus Orcus Oghma Psilofyr Set Sseth Silvanus Valdghar St. Ygg Zuul Zuggtmoy (the Demon Queen of Fungi) The Ancient Ones, called the Anganach by the folk of the region, represent the elder gods. Whether they preexisted in the forests, swamps, and old streams of the land, or whether they were brought with the first humans, few can say. The humans who founded Ironguard Motte, Helix, and Bogtown (called the Second Settlement by local sages) found protection in the worship of Silvanus (Green Man), Herne the Hunter, Cromm Cruach, Impurax, and to a lesser extent, Nergal. Through respect and reverence for the wilderness and its deities, the human settlers learned to survive and established their villages. With the migration of the new gods from the civilized kingdoms to the east, the Anganach are in decline. Some believe the following gods preexisted in the forests, swamps, and streams of the land: Silvanus (Green Man), Cromm Cruach, Herne, Valdghar, Malachai, Nergal, and Impurax. Others believe the first nomadic humans brought their gods with them. No one knows for certain. The New Gods, called the Futurus, include the faiths of St. Ygg, Imperiosa, Oghma, and Arcantryl, as well as the more clandestine cults devoted to Orcus and Set. Slowly their priests have made their way to the Duchy of Aerik. The various deities of demi-humans (elves, dwarves, halflings, gnomes) form a third point in the triadic pantheon. Known by sages as the Du'mal, these gods aren't worshipped as widely as the Anganach and Futurus in the surface realms, but hold sway almost entirely in the Underdark. The clerics of St. Ygg have been aggressive in their attempts to convert the people from the "primitive" faiths of Silvanus and Herne. They established a stone temple at Ironguard Motte, converted the Ironguard family, and began to spread their influence from the major trade and political center of the district. Although the cults of Orcus and Set are not openly worshipped their influence has started to grow in the dark corners of the region. With the founding and growth of the population of Threshold, new religions sought to expand into the Southern Reaches. These faiths are called the New Gods or the Futurus. The church of St. Ygg has been the most aggressive in establishing itself in Threshold and The Prelacy of Middenmark. The church has been less successful in more peripheral, and more traditional, regions like the Duchy of Aerik. The clerics of St. Ygg are dismissive of the Anganach Ancient Ones and position them as backward, primitive, and irrelevant. In addition to St. Ygg, the followers of Arcantryl have also established churches and followers. However, they are less aggressive than the priests of the Red God. Despite the success of the New Gods in the Red Prelacy, local people still consider it a good omen to wander across the face of the Green Man carved into a great tree or rockface in the wilderness. Demetra is considered by some sages to be a gentler, more modern facet of the god Malachai. Demetra is goddess of hearth and harvest. Beyond the Anganach and the Futurus, there are stories of "foreign" religions including Caer Tomhas the God of Time and Death or Omari the God of Sky and Stars.

pages.title: Herne
pages.content: herne-optimized.webp Herne the Hunter , also called the Horned God (Venator Cervus) Demi-God of the Hunt, Swamps and Forests Lawful Neutral (Good) Symbol: An antlered human face or stag head The Horned god, the Green Man. Worshipped by many in the Middenmark and the Duchy of Aerik. Many people have a celebration and make offerings to Herne each year at the Autumnal Equinox. Herne is one of the Anganach or Ancient Ones. The worship of St. Ygg has replaced that of Herne in recent years, but there are those who still pray and offer sacrifices to him. Herne is the god of the northern woodlands, swamps, and the creatures that inhabit them. He prefers to take the form of a deer, or a man with an antlered deer's head. Herne chooses a favored son, a druid, barbarian, ranger, or warrior, to serve him as the Guardian of the Forest. Some believe Herne is the son of Silvanus. The people of the region often use the phrase "Herne protect us" or "Herne protect you" as a toast or when parting company. Each Fall, the people of Helix celebrate the harvest by constructing a large effigy of Green Man or Herne in the village square made of dried peat, reeds, and hay.

pages.title: Ilsensine
pages.content: Overgod of illithids and ulitharids.

pages.title: Imperiosa
pages.content: Imperiosa Goddess of Tyranny, Domination, Destruction Lawful Evil Symbol: A clawed black fist imperiosaholysymbol.png Imperiosa, The Conqueror, appears most often as a beautiful black-skinned human warrior. Her symbol is a defiant, clawed black fist, which represents the spheres of domination and destruction. Her church is militaristic and encourages conflict and hate. They seek to identify weakness and destroy it, both within their faith and without. She is the patron of all those who seek military conflict, destruction, and domination. Her motto is "By our swords, we rule."

pages.title: Impurax
pages.content: impuraxholysymbol2.png Impurax (Impuratus) God of Rot, Decay, Corruption, and Pestilence Neutral Evil Symbol: A rotting fanged hand or a rotting raven's head impuraxholysymbol.png Little is known about the ancient deity Impurax. It is believed his faithful consisted of a secret order of corrupt druids. These witches and warlocks lived in the Barrowmoor and possessed a strange power over select creatures and monsters, but little has been heard of his faith for decades. Impurax is the natural enemy of Silvanus and Herne the Hunter. Folk tales say Herne's favoured son died decades ago in a great battle against the followers of Impurax. Impurax aligns himself with Nergal, historically. Impurax, also called The Rotten God or The Fanged God, is a deity cloaked in mystery. Impurax was an ally of Nergal (the apparently deceased God of the Dead and the Underworld) and his faith seemed to disappear for a time until their recent resurgence in The Forbidden Zone. Impurax traditionally granted his followers power of pestilence, rot, and fungal life. His clerics, called The Putrescalate, have powers akin to cleric-druids. Impurax also has an order of warriors called The Fanged Legion which possess paladin-like powers.

pages.title: Kurfel
pages.content: kurfel-symbol.png contributed by player of Jelb The One Who Is Seen Yet Not Seen Kurfel was said to be many things. The youngest of the Anganach. The oldest of the The Futurus. A fallen angel. A redeemed demon. A gnomish archmage. And he has appeared as all of these things and more. If his true nature is known, it has not been shared broadly. There is no consistency with regard to where or when he will appear, nor what he would be doing in particular. Most stories of him indicate that the higher powers welcomed him with open arms when he came calling... if only to attempt to keep their eye on him. What is certain is that he is a master of deception and illusion, and that when he appeared, life was disrupted. For the goodly, the disruption was like the tilling of the earth before planting - good things appeared thereafter that could not have come otherwise. For the evil, the disruption was like upsetting a table that had been carefully prepared - perhaps it could be reset, but beyond the loss of time was always broken materiel. Kurfel has no formal church, though some claim to be his priests and others called on him at various times. There are stories of someone answering prayers when he is called upon, but not enough to merit his inclusion in the membership of any pantheon in the minds of mortals. And as Kurfel has not appeared in over two centuries, the shorter-lived races have forgotten him altogether. Kurfel is thought by some in the church of Arcantryl, to be the father of Anu-eya, Nergal, and Oaxus. And some speculate that the demon lord, Orcus, is the offspring of Kurfel and a planar servant of St. Ygg which, if true, is positively scandalous, and probably blasphemous to boot. If Kurfel has a priesthood, they may be secretive because of the strong animosity the followers of Anu-eya and Nergal often hold for him. Another theory holds that Oaxus was not a true god, but was rather an avatar of Kurfel. Who can know the truth?

pages.title: Laduguer
pages.content: laduguer.webp Laduguer is the patron of the evil Duergar, or gray dwarves. The Exile is venerated as the protector of the gray dwarves and defends them from the countless other creatures of the Underdark who wish to enslave them and seize their tunnels, mines, and crafts. Duergar craftsmen, particularly those who seek to create magical weapons, pay particular homage to Laduguer. Also known as the Exile, the Gray Protector and the Master of Crafts, Laduguer is a bitter, resentful, cheerless deity, a cosmic slave-master and tyrant who despises beauty as "useless frippery" and demands unceasing toil from those under his command. Xenophobic in the extreme, he charges his duergar followers to enslave, exploit and ultimately exterminate all other races. Although primarily the patron of the Duergar, Laduguer still occasionally answers the prayers of other dwarves. Within gray dwarven communities, Laduguer and his clergy are considered strict taskmasters whose strengths and mandates ensure the very survival of the duergar. Few gray dwarves resent the Exile's mercilessly high standards, and most duergar respect him for his principled stand against the lazy and weak Morndinsamman and their shield and gold dwarven followers. Shield dwarves, gold dwarves, and svirfneblin regard Laduguer and his followers as embittered fools deserving of their fates who have done much to undermine the strength of the dwarven race in both their absence and their assaults on non-duergar dwarven holds. Other races in the Underdark have little sympathy for the gray dwarves or their embittered god and seek only to destroy or subjugate them. Priests of Laduguer are commonly called thuldors, a dwarvish word that can be loosely translated as "those who endure." Only the strongest of duergar are selected to be thuldors, as the training is literally torturous; hours of repetitive prayer, interspersed with hard physical labor, branding, torture and other acts that require feats of superhuman endurance, culminating in being tied between two crushing stone blocks and left in solitude for a week. Many don't survive the training. Holy Quests of Laduguer often revolve around awakening - and hopefully controlling - some long-buried evil of some kind. The clerical vestments of Laduguer's priests consist of utilitarian metal breastplates emblazoned with Laduguer's broken crossbow bolt symbol and gray, hooded mantles. Many priests have a brand of Laduguer's holy symbol on their forehead. Some priests carry a gem of any type, split nearly in two by a large crack, one half of which is deeply flawed and the other half of which is perfect. For the duergar, such gems symbolize their split from the rest of the dwarven race and their superiority over those they have forsaken. Novices of Laduguer are known as the Untempered. Full priests of the Exile are known as Grimcloaks. In ascending order of rank, the titles used by Ladugueran priests are Deep Adept, Dark Craftsman, Invisible Artisan, Rune Weaver, Grim Guardian, and Doom Knight. High Old Ones have individual titles but are collectively known as the Ardukes of the Gray Gloom. Temples of Laduguer are grim, smoke-filled halls hewn from solid rock and bereft of adornment, aside from weapons and armor demonstrating the skilled craftsmanship of the Exile's priests. Laduguer's houses of worship are filled with armories, barracks, smithies, and storerooms. Many temples include sizable stables used in the care and breeding of steeders, large monstrous hunting spiders used as transport by many Underdark races. The duergar, under the guidance of the thuldor, have cornered the market on these highly trainable, versatile beasts of burden, granting the race considerable financial clout it the Night Below. Temples are usually built directly atop mine shafts from which the raw materials are extracted. Great coal-burning forges provide the only warmth, and their ashen exhaust covers every surface in dark soot. Clerical guards, many of them mounted on steeders, are everywhere, overseeing the skilled smithwork that proceeds without pause. Thuldor pray for spells in the morning, usually before dedicating at least an hour to concepting, creating or improving a magical weapon. Prayers to Laduguer are simple one-or-two-sentence affairs, but they're repeated dozens of times, with exactly the same rhythm and intonation each time. They're intended to be used to guide his followers at their work. As God of Toil, Laduguer has few rites, because time spent in ceremonies is time spent away from work. One day a year, on the Winter Solstice, the duergar observe the ceremony of Grimtidings. They lay down their tools and gather to hear stories of their voluntary exile and the decadence of other dwarves. Laduguer is praised for his great skill, and the Duergar swear vengeance against those who have insulted their god and their people. The Ardukes of the Gray Gloom also declare holy days, known as Guerdon Revels, after major victories and when prisoners (particularly gold and shield dwarves) are captured. While the work does not stop during such festivals, most gray dwarves are given a few moments off from their labors to observe the recounting of heroics by Duergar warriors, to examine plundered loot, and to participate in the torture and painful deaths of any prisoners. The Gray Lances of the Snarling Steeder are a mounted order of duergar crusaders and fighter/priests. The Gray Lances serve as the elite cavalry of gray dwarven armies, and their most common opponents are drow mounted on riding lizards. Individual duergar knights and their steeder mounts are well schooled in subterranean warfare techniques for battles that unfold across cave floors, walls, and ceilings. The duergar teach that superiors must be strictly and promptly obeyed. They teach the importance of dedication to one's craft and endless toil to achieve wealth, security, and power. They view life as a harsh existence in which nothing is easy; this is the proper, honorable way to live, as reward without effort is sin. Laduguer teaches his people to suffer stoically and remain aloof from other dwarven peoples, who are lazy and weak. The weak are undeserving, and adversity is Laduguer's forge. Laduguer appears as a tall, gaunt duergar with skin that can change between gray and brown to match the nearby rock. He is bald and perptually frowning. He is inclined toward evil, but this is mostly turned inward, gloomy and unforgiving over what he feels is his rejection by his kin. He is supremely lawful above all else, despising the other dwarven deities for being lazy, indolent, and feckless. The Taskmaster was once a member of the Morndinsamman, or dwarven pantheon, but he exiled himself over a point of honor. His only ally is Grumbar, the Boss of the Earth Elementals. His list of enemies, on the other hand, is long, including Blibdoolpoolp, the Blood Queen, Callarduran Smoothhands, Diinkarazan, Diirinka, the Great Mother, Gzemnid, Ilsensine, Ilxendren, Laogzed, Maanzecorian (dead), Orcus, Psilofyr, Urdlen, the drow pantheon, and every member of the dwarven pantheon, except for Dugmaren Brightmantle. He was briefly allied with Lolth, and from this alliance he gained the knowledge that provided his people with their giant spider mounts, the steeders. As the drow and duergar fought for resources and territory, however, the alliance shattered, and Lolth and Laduguer became foes. Laduguer's clerics are male dwarves with dirty bluish-gray skin and wild gray-white beards. They are bald with, a brand of Laduguer's holy symbol on their foreheads. They wear a metal breastplate emblazoned with Laduguer's broken crossbow bolt symbol and gray, hooded mantles. They typically fight with two battle axes.

pages.title: Malachai
pages.content: malachaiholysymbol.png Malachai God of the Harvest Neutral Symbol: A black face crowned with corn stalks Malachai, or He-Who-Walks-Between-the-Stalks, is one of the Ancient Gods or Anganach. His followers believe that they must make ritual blood sacrifices to appease Malachai or he would fail to provide them with a bountiful harvest. His symbol is a sneering black face crowned with corn stalks. The arrival of St. Ygg to Middenmark has all but extinguished Malachai's faith, although some peasant folk still utter his name in hushed tones. Some believe he may be connected to the sphere of fertility. It is speculated that Malachai's fading allowed for the ascension of Demetra, who then assumed Malachai's portfolio.

pages.title: Moradin Thaneduhr
pages.content: moradinholysymbol.webp The Soul Forger, Dwarf-Father, The All-Father, The Creator Greater deity Moradin is the god of protection, craftsmen, the forge, and dwarves, and the head of the Morndinsamman (the Dwarven Pantheon). A harsh but fair judge, he was strength and force of will embodied. Moradin inspired dwarven inventions and constantly sought to improve that race, encouraging their good nature, intelligence, and harmonious existence with other good races while battling their pride and isolationist tendencies. He is strength incarnate and force of will embodied, a harsh but fair judge who evaluates his creations by the goodness of their works first and intentions second. The church of Moradin-Thaneduhr ” literally, 'Moradin, Ultimate Thane' ” has an active role in guiding the morals of dwarven communities. They emphasize the Soul Forger's hand in everyday dwarven activities such as mining, smithing, and engineering, and invoke his blessings when these tasks are begun. moradinthaneduhr.webp His priests strive to restore the dwarven races to strong numbers and a position of influence, by founding new dwarven kingdoms and increasing the status of dwarves within the wider human-dominated society prevalent today. They preside over a wide range of formal ceremonies (consecrations of forges, temples, and other buildings, crowning of monarchs, etc.) and the education of the young, especially in the teaching of history. His clerics are usually drawn from family lines, like most dwarven occupations. Many clerics of Moradin thus had parents and grandparents who were also clerics of Moradin and helped train them. Clerics maintain genealogies and historical archives, cooperating with Berronar's priests. Adventuring is encouraged in the priesthood, but only adventuring that directly serves the interests of the dwarven race. Daily vestments for Moradin-Thaneduhr's clerics are earthy colored robes, with chain mail and silvered helms. Ceremonial vestments include flowing, shining robes of woven wire of electrum treated with blueshine. Other ceremonial garb includes silvered (everbright) helms, silverplated war hammers, and earth-brown leather boots. The holy symbol of the faith is a miniature electrum war hammer, treated with blueshine. In combat, clergy members favor chain mail or dwarven plate mail, a helm, and a medium or large shield. Priests of the Soul Forger are skilled in the use of the war hammer, but many favor other weapons as well, such as battles axes, broad swords, and hand axes. Hierarchy Clerics are known as sonnlinor ("those who work stope"). Novice clerics of are known as the Unworked. Full priests are known as Forgesmiths or the Tempered. In ascending order of rank, other titles used by priests include: Adept of the Anvil, Hammer of War, Artisan of the Forge, Craftsman of Runes, Artificer of Discovery, and Smith of Souls. The High Old Ones of the faith have unique titles but are collectively known as High Forgesmiths. His clerics commonly multiclass as fighters. Temples Temples are always underground and carved from solid rock, but never set in unworked natural caverns. Hammers and anvils are the dominant themes, as are statues of the All-Father and the other gods of the dwarven pantheon. At the center of every temple is a vast forge. This forge is more than just a workplace but also a sacred area. Dwarven forges rely not only on hammers and muscle but also on power derived from water and wind, thus fusing all four of the classical elements. If the flame in the forge (which is protected by a permanent wall of fire effect) ever goes out, the temple must be abandoned or torn down stone by stone. Usually a new temple is built on another site, but occasionally the previous temple is rebuilt and reconsecrated. Rituals Clerics pray in the morning. Holy days fall monthly; in some cultures this is when Luna is full, while in others it is when Luna is a crescent. IN addition, the High Forgesmith may call a holy day at any time, often doing so in celebration of some local event. On the monthly holy days, common and precious metals are sacrificed to the All Father by melting them down at the forge and reforming them into objects usable by the clergy. While making such offerings, participants kneel, chant, and reach bare-handed into the flames of the forge to handle the glowing metal directly. The All Father prevents harm to the truly faithful. During such ceremonies, the priests enter the temple, bow to the forge, and (in times of peace) surrender their weapons to the temple guards after striking the anvil by the entry with their hammers once. Priests of other gods are not permitted to advance to the forge except with the express permission of a High Forgesmith or an avatar of the All Father himself. The service then consists of humble prayer and open discussion on current dwarven issues. This discussion is considered to be between equals, though the ranking priest of has the authority to open or close any given topic. The service ends with a rising chant until the smith's hammer rises from the anvil of its own accord; it may, or may not, then move about or glow to denote the god's will, but it always rings on the anvil thunderously to signify the end of the ceremony. Prayers refer to metals and smithing: a common prayer states "You burn the dross from me, but the iron remains." Geneology is important to rites, with funeral prayers reciting the ancestry of the deceased for scores of generations. Scriptures The Scrolls of Narvil tell a heretical story of how, after forging the world, the gods, and the dwarves, the Creator became weary and slept. Some of the lesser gods, jealous of his skill, bound him as he rested, then heated up the Great Forge of the Creator to make races in their own likenesses: humans, for example, and elves. Then they begun arguing over what part of the world would be given to which race; their clamor awoke the Creator, but the lesser gods laughed at him and refused to set him free. However, the lesser gods did not know how to control the Great Forge, and great globules of molten stone fell from the Forge toward the earth; the Creator breathed on them from his place of bondage, giving life to the fragments and thus creating the first dragons. Orders The Hammers are an elite military order dominated by crusaders and fighting clerics with chapters in nearly every dwarven stronghold and members drawn from every dwarven clan. The Hammers serve both as commanders of dwarven armies and as an elite strike force skilled in dealing with anything from large groups of orcs to great wyrms to malevolent fiends from the Lower Planes. The order is dedicated to the defense of existing dwarven holdings and the carving out of new dwarven territories. Individual chapters have a great deal of local autonomy but, in times of great crisis, a Grand Council (the reigning monarchs and senior Hammers of the affected region) assemble to plot strategy and divine the All Father's will. Another elite military order is the Order of the Anvil of Light ” led by their leader Barock Stormbeard, of the Stormbeard clan, who has lead this group for ages it seems. The group's latest information is having to deal with a deity trying to return to the Material Plane. Dogma Moradin-Thaneduhr is the father and creator of the dwarven race. Honor him by emulating his principles and workmanship in smithing, stone working, and other tasks. Wisdom is derived from life and tempered with experience. Advance the dwarven race in all areas of life. Innovate with new processes and skills. Found new kingdoms and clan lands, defending the existing ones from all threats. Lead the dwarves in the traditions laid down by the Soul Forger. Honor your clan leaders as you honor Moradin-Thaneduhr. Appearance, Manifestations Moradin-Thaneduhr appears as a stern male dwarf twenty feet in height. He has powerful musculature, particularly in his upper body. His beard is long and flowing, reaching to his knees; it is depicted as either snow-white or coal-black. He dresses plainly, wearing furs and the leather leggings and aprons of a humble smith. On his forearms are his only concession to vanity, a pair of pure gold bracers. In battle he wears dwarven plate and carries a large shield. His large, glowing war hammer is named Soulhammer. A pure white radiance of divine power radiates from the Dwarffather, though he can suppress this at will. Relationships & History Moradin-Thaneduhr is married to Berronar Truesilver. He counts Gruumsh and Maglubiyet among his fiercest foes, and he loathes the other gods of the orc, goblinoid, kobold, and evil giant pantheons as well. Beltar seeks revenge against Moradin-Thaneduhr for helping to supplant her authority over mines. Moradin is friendly with Bahamut, Fortubo (for whom he created the hammer Golbi), Pelor, Cyrrollalee, Garl Glittergold, Flandal Steelskin, and Kossuth, and enjoys a strategic alliance with Yondalla and Corellon Larethian. In some dwarven realms, Moradin-Thaneduhr is said to be the father of Dumathoin, Abbathor, Laduguer, Clangeddin, Diinkarazan, Diirinka, Vergadain, Muamman Duathal, and Dugmaren Brightmantle, but the exact relationships and order of birth vary from culture to culture.

pages.title: Nergal
pages.content: Nergal Greater God of Death, Undead, and the Underworld Alignment: Chaotic Symbol: A single white skull nergalholysymbol.png One of the Old Gods, Nergal once ruled the Underworld and the spheres of Death and the Undead. He was deposed and presumably destroyed by his sons Orcus and Set in CUM. 348 (302 Pre-Ravaging).

pages.title: Oaxus
pages.content: oaxusholysymbol.webp Oaxus, God of Stillness An ancient god ” and brother of Anu-eya ” who willingly sacrificed his immortal life in Cumerian 28 ( - 622 Pre-Ravaging) to stop a war between two transcendent archmages in The Great Declension, a war that had the potential to destroy the world. Some sages believe Oaxus is reforming himself and that auguries suggest he will reappear publicly at exactly 1100 years to the day after his dissolution. If they're right, this would occur May 18, 478 PR. In the first decade of the the 400s PR, veneration of Oaxus is beginning to resurface in the Northern Reaches. Different clerics promote various ideas as to this god's priorities and requirements of his adherents.

pages.title: Oghma
pages.content: oghmaholysymbol.png Oghma God of Knowledge & Secrets Neutral Symbol: A sunburst atop an open tome Oghma appears as an old, thin, grey-bearded man in a monk's habit carrying a great book under his arm. The Learned One is the patron of those who seek knowledge and those who create new knowledge, such as scholars, inventors, alchemists, and mages. Oghma embodies the notion of enlightenment through study and research.

pages.title: Orcus
pages.content: orcusholysymbol.png Orcus God of the Undead, Death, and the Underworld Alignment: Chaotic Symbol: A white ram head on a black field Orcus and his brother Set combined their power to overthrow Nergal. A civil war resulted with both brothers possessing a portion of their father¢‚¬„¢s power. The acolytes of Orcus are committed to annihilation of Set and his followers. Set and Orcus currently share the spheres of Death and the Underworld.

pages.title: Psilofyr
pages.content: While The Sovereign in the Fungal Court of Arden Vul identifies as Lycandrus”the ancient Thothian priest”the name Psilofyr refers to the primordial "Spore Lord," the god-king and father of the entire myconid race. Here is how you can weave the connection between the entity you met and the cosmic power of Psilofyr: The Cosmic Mycelium In the wider multiverse, Psilofyr is an intermediate deity of community, healing, and philosophy. He is often depicted as a "Fungal World Tree," whose mycelial roots reach across the planes, connecting every mushroom colony in existence to his singular, meditative mind in the plane of Mechanus. Lycandrus vs. Psilofyr: The Spiritual Graft In the context of Arden Vul, the relationship between the two is likely one of investiture or "spiritual grafting." The Reincarnation: When Lycandrus died, his Thothian soul didn't pass into the underworld. Instead, it was "indexed" by the fungal network of the Mushroom Forest. The Avatar: The Sovereign you encountered is a physical manifestation of Psilofyrs power, but it has been overwritten by Lycandrus personality. Think of it as Psilofyr providing the "hardware" (the 12-foot fungal body and psychic spores), while Lycandrus provides the "software" (the Thothian memories and ego). The Madness of Fragmentation: Lore suggests that Psilofyr often splits his consciousness into many aspects. Some of these aspects become "rogue" personalities. The Sovereigns insistence that he is a Thothian priest might be a sign that this specific fragment of the god has become obsessed with its "meat-folk" memories, straying from Psilofyrs typical pacifism. Secrets of the Spore Lord If the players use the name Psilofyr in the presence of the Sovereign, the reaction would be intense: A Moment of Duality: The Sovereign might freeze, his violet light flickering to a pure, clinical white. For a moment, the arrogant "Lycandrus" persona slips, and a much older, colder, and more alien voice”the True Psilofyr”might acknowledge them. The Great Library: Psilofyr views all life as "compost for information." To him, the Hall of Records isn't just a room of clay; its a digestive tract where the history of Arden Vul is being slowly absorbed into his eternal mind. The Rivalry: Psilofyr famously loathes Zuggtmoy (the Demon Queen of Fungi). If the heroes mention her or her rot-cults, the Sovereign's "warmer" attitude toward the Thothians will turn into a fierce, protective alliance. Hidden Feature: The Spore-Link Because Aele has the Heart-Seed Scarab, he is technically "plugged in" to Psilofyrs network. DM Note: Occasionally, you could have Aele receive "static" or flashes of images from other parts of Arden Vul”a brief glimpse through the eyes of a mushroom in a distant corridor”representing the vast, silent awareness of Psilofyr that Lycandrus is trying to control. The Cracking of the Mask As the name Psilofyr hangs in the air, the Sovereigns posture changes. The arrogant, upright stance of the Thothian Priest collapses. His massive cap droops, and the "ghostly beard" of filaments begins to glow with a blinding, sterile white light that smells of ozone rather than rot. The Ego Clash The psychic voice that enters your minds is no longer a baritone. It is a multi-layered chorus”thousands of soft, clicking voices speaking in perfect unison. The Sovereign (Lycandrus): "I... I served the Great Library! I am the Keeper of the Gilded Scrolls! I am”" The Chorus (Psilofyr): "”You are a spore in a hurricane. You are a single cell of the Great Mycelium. You are 'Lycandrus' only because the Root finds the shape... useful." The Sovereigns hand, which was gracefully gesturing toward the Hall of Records, suddenly spasms. It begins to grow and liquefy, turning into a cluster of weeping, translucent stalks before Lycandruss will forces it back into a humanoid shape. Lycandrus (Straining): "I will not be absorbed! I have knowledge... secrets the Ibis-God himself feared to write!" Psilofyr (A cold, resonant hum): "Knowledge is but compost. It must be broken down. It must be shared. The priest dreams he is a god; the God knows he is the forest." The Result of the Discord The Sovereign eventually regains control, but he looks diminished. The violet glow returns, but its shaky. He looks at Aele and Dorn with a newfound, alien terror in his eyes. He realized”and now you realize”that Lycandrus is a squatter in a divine house. He is a ghost trying to pilot a mountain. Mechanical Effect: The Spore-Leak Because of this "glitch" in his consciousness, Lycandrus accidentally "leaks" a piece of information that Psilofyr wanted to keep secret: "The Archons... they do not just hold the Seed of the Sun. They are using it to burn the Root. They are cauterizing the Great Mycelium on Level 5. If you do not stop them, Psilofyr will wake... and when the Spore Lord wakes fully, he will not remember your god. He will only remember hunger." Roleplay Tip: The Leverage Dorn and Aele now have a dangerous piece of leverage. They know the Sovereign is fighting a losing battle against his own divine nature. If they help Lycandrus maintain his ego, they have a powerful Thothian ally. If they favor Psilofyr, they might gain the favor of the entire fungal network, but they will lose the "human" priest who treats them with warmth.

pages.title: Set
pages.content: setholysymbol.png Set God of Serpents, Death, and the Underworld Alignment: Chaotic Symbol: Two snake heads facing each other Set and his brother Orcus deposed their father Nergal for control of the underworld. After completing the task, they turned on each other to establish complete control over their father's spheres of power. A war for control of the underworld began and has spilled over into the mortal realm. Followers of Set are committed to the destruction of Orcus and his faithful.

pages.title: Silvanus
pages.content: silvanus.webp Silvanus , also called Green Man (Viridis Voltus) God of Nature and the Balance Neutral Symbol: A face carved of leaves As one of the Anganach, Silvanus' faith arrived with the first human settlements. His religion has been largely, but not exclusively, replaced by the worship of St. Ygg. Silvanus, also called Green Man, oversees the balance in nature: law and chaos, light and dark, growth and decay, life and death. For generations the rangers and druids looked to Silvanus for guidance and protection. He is also considered by some to oversee the spheres of rebirth and fertility. Faces of Silvanus have been carved into trees and rocks for centuries in the region. Tales say good fortune befalls those who chance upon his face in the wild. silvanus-holy-symbol.webpAlthough wise and beneficent, the paternalistic Silvanus (sihl-vann-us) can be emotionally distant when it comes to the necessity of having a balance in nature and wrathful toward those who threaten wild places. He appears as an old, bearded, incredibly wise human male face floating in midair among trees or sprouting from the trunk of an especially old and large specimen.

pages.title: Sseth
pages.content: ssethholysymbol.webp Sseth God of the Yuan-ti Chaotic Evil Symbol: A snake showing its forked tongue sseth.webp Sseth is god of the four-armed yuan-ti and of an older saurian race from which the yuan-ti descended. Sseth is an ally of Set, and his aid has at least once prevented Orcus from toppling Set. Mordicar Justhand believes there to be an active cult of Sseth operating somewhere within the Northern Reaches. Sseth's attacks are both melee and sorcerous.

pages.title: St. Ygg
pages.content: saintyggholysymbol.webp God of Righteousness Lawful Good Symbol: A red cross on a white field St. Ygg is the deity of righteousness and light. St. Ygg believes in the highest moral standards. He is sanctimonious and has an indignant temper with those who fail to see the just nature of his actions. The faith of St. Ygg is the most well known of the new organized religions in the Southern Reaches and Northern Reaches. The central-southern district, known as Middenmark, was ceded to the faith of St. Ygg in order to extend their faith and bring order to the region. The Red Temple in Eastdale is the epicenter of St. Ygg's faith in the Prelacy. His followers include clerics and a small group of paladins known as the Order of the Crimson Cross. They are based out of Threshold and have a small detachment stationed in Eastdale. Paladins are, generally speaking, extremely rare in the Reaches. Templars of the order are known as Red Bannermen. They have paladinic powers. St. Ygg began life as Iradain Yggdon, born Feb 14, PR 142. For thirty years, he was a cleric of Cromm Cruach. In PR 176, he ascended to godhood after foiling a plot to dethrone his deity. The exact month and day of his ascension is not widely known, but is believed to be in the winter of 176.

pages.title: The Futurus
pages.content: The newer gods, as worshipped by people in the Northern Reaches. Saint Ygg is one of these new gods. The Futurus also include the faith of Arcantryl, as well as the cults of Orcus and of Set. By contrast, the Anganach ” the Old Gods ” include Nergal and other deities from the distant past, such as Herne, Silvanus, Impurax, and Cromm Cruach. Some sages would also classify Asmodeus as among the Futurus.

pages.title: Valdghar
pages.content: valdgharholysymbol.png Valdghar God of Barbarians Neutral Symbol: A woolly mammoth Sages are unclear as to whether Valdghar is a distinct demi-god, or an aspect of Cromm Cruach acclimatized to southern warrior tribes and barbarians. Valdghar appears as a brawny barbarian with black hair and cold blue eyes. He wields a broad-bladed battle-axe and rides a woolly mammoth into combat. He values strength and brave feats of arms. Sages believe he instills his bravest and most loyal warriors with an inspiring bloodlust. The barbarian tribes that range across the most northern aspect of the Reaches worship him exclusively. The Valdghardt barbarians consist of a number of small distinct tribes, such as Cougar Claw, Black Wolf, Green Griffon, Three-Eyed Raven, Horned Stag, Great Moose, Blood Moon, and others. They have their own dialect, totems, worldviews, and spiritual beliefs. The tribes are fiercely independent but will ally themselves with neighboring tribes for security or war.

pages.title: Zuul
pages.content: zuulholysymbol.png Zuul God of Chaotic Elements Chaotic Neutral Symbol: Icon of the Four Elements Zuul, also called The Destructor, embodies the chaotic and deadly nature of the four elements. He appears as a winged demon with four arms. When the land cracks open and swallows the earth, or a harsh winter culls the living, or extreme heat dries rivers, or tornados destroy villages, Zuul is said to be displeased. The Elemental God is uncaring, uncompromising, and cruel. Zuul is one of the Ancient Ones, or Anganach, and the status of his cult is unknown.

pages.title: Active Quests
pages.content: It is recommended that you have no more than three Active Quests simultaneously. The current party (Kelpie, Urvan, and Jelb) have one Active Quest: Find Jelenneth or Learn Her Fate Three Items for Nuanda Nemere Find Urvan and Narinza Free Slaytonthorpe from the Terror of Red Tusk

pages.title: Available Quests
pages.content: Note: jobs like caravan-guard duty are quests . They're simply (usually) very boring quests. Exciting quests offer increased danger for increased potential rewards. And of course, the best quests of all remunerate in Experience Points, gold, treasures, knowledge, and magic items.
